events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

Central Region RWC Introduction Course
The Rescue Water Craft (RWC) commonly known as a Personal Water Craft (PWC) or Jetski is specially outfitted for surf interaction and operated by experienced Surf Lifeguards.

As the operator of a Rescue Water Craft you are responsible for the safety of your crew, the public and yourself. It is important that you understand the risks inherent in operating this type of equipment and your role in assessing and minimising risk.

The qualification has a number of theoretical and practical components such as driving in the surf, patient pick up and maritime regulations to prepare experienced Surf Lifeguards for RWC use.

Prerequisites:

Current & active member of a SLS club
Surf Lifeguard Award (Refreshed)
20 years of age minimum on the first day of the introductory course.
Radio Communication Module or Maritime VHF Operator's Certificate
Senior Lifeguard Award - IRB Driver (Refreshed)*
Surf First Aid (Refreshed)**
400m Pool swim under 7.30 minutes
*A minimum of 2 years from IRB Award including 2 seasons operating as a IRB driver is required (at a minimum one IRB driver refresher must have been completed in the last year)
**An RWC Operator must hold a Surf First Aid prior to attending their RWC exam.

Link to more information and the application form is in the comments.
Send the completed application form to Justine at

events.id: Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026-Rathkeale College Auditorium, Willow Park Drive, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026
events.venue: Rathkeale College Auditorium, Willow Park Drive, Masterton
events.long_description:
Welcome to the Rathkeale Christmas Fête 2026.

Walk through the gates of Rathkeale College on 7 November and be welcomed by a diverse range of colourful stalls, the aroma of freshly cooked food, and plenty of festive inspiration.

Now in its 23rd year, the Christmas Fête has become a must-do event on the Wairarapa spring calendar. Stallholders travel from around the North Island to sell their wares and offer Christmas shoppers plenty of inspiration. From festive decorations, clothing, arts and crafts, to flowers, toys, and plants, there is something for everyone.

Gourmet food is always a highlight at the Fête. Think freshly made gourmet burgers, lamb and mint sausages, salads, and the ever-popular berries and ice cream. There is always a huge variety of flavours to tempt the taste buds. Devonshire teas and home baking served in the Rathkeale Homestead rose garden is a time-honoured tradition, while refreshing cold drinks can be enjoyed as visitors listen to live music performed by students at various times throughout the day. The popular Christmas cake stall features again this year, but visitors are encouraged to get in early, as the cakes often sell out by midday.

The beauty of this Fête is that it’s a day out for the whole family. In addition to the 120-plus stalls, there is plenty to entertain children, including a barrel train ride, face painting, and magic shows throughout the day.

Visitors can also explore the beautiful, expansive grounds of Rathkeale College, including the school gardens designed by Alfred Buxton, the recently installed Paul Dibble sculpture The Choice, the Greek Amphitheatre, and the 3km eco-trail, which weaves through large stands of native trees, including ancient kahikatea.

EFTPOS is available, but visitors are encouraged to bring cash.

Koha / gold coin entry

Rathkeale College is a five-minute drive north of Masterton in the Wairarapa.

events.name: Cheesemaking - Brie And Queso Fresco
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
During this intensely practical, hands-on workshop, you will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Double Cream ‘NZ style’ Brie. You will also be shown how to make Queso Fresco cheese which you will get to sample afterwards. All ingredients included in course fee.

The ultimate class in practical cheese making! Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home. You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.

All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.

During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make. You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.

A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:

Make Brie and Queso Fresco
Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco

Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

1 Day
Presented by Alexis Murti.

events.long_description:
Nature in the Making: A Children’s Nature-Inspired Art Adventure
Let curiosity lead the way in this nature-inspired art adventure for children.

With gentle prompts and plenty of room to explore, children can experiment with paint, texture and mark-making, and may also try collage. There’s no prescribed picture to copy and no expectation of a particular result. The focus is on noticing, experimenting and following the artwork as it develops.

No art experience is needed. Each child can take part in their own way and discover what they enjoy making.

Nature in the Making is a fundraiser for an overseas mission trip.

A ticket supports the trip and gives children a chance to enjoy a creative session inspired by nature.



Who's it for? any children in Year 4 upwards.

Who will be supervising? Kim Shaw (registered teacher and church youth leader) with other police-checked helpers.

What's involved? Children will be supervised outside on the church property observing natural elements, like trees, leaves, flowers, moss, shadows. Weather dependent they will either work indoors in the hall or outdoors on their artwork.

What do they need? a willingness to get curious and have a go, clothes they can get a bit messy and/or a painting shirt or apron.

events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for Permaculture Orchard Workshop – Growing Fruit with Nature. Take a deeper dive into the workings of a permaculture orchard and discover how ecological principles can help us grow healthier, more productive fruit trees.

Through a mix of theory and hands-on practical learning, we'll explore ecological succession, plant guilds, soil health, biodiversity and the relationships that create resilient orchard ecosystems.

Learn practical techniques you can apply at any scale, from a single backyard fruit tree to a thriving food forest.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 10:00am at 108 Whitemans Valley Road (Garden).

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
Explore Stonehenge Aotearoa at Your Own Pace

Our self-guided tour includes a map and a 12-minute audio-visual presentation to help you uncover the secrets of the henge. Afterward, head down to the stone circle and try out its unique acoustics — clap your hands and hear the echo respond, or whisper and see how far your voice carries.

A self-guided tour typically takes around 30 minutes, but many visitors stay longer simply because it’s so much fun. The bigger your group, the better the experience!

Please arrive at least 30 minutes before closing time.
Available during our opening hours: 10 AM – 4 PM.

events.id: Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop-Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt-Mangaroa
events.name: Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop
events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop with Doris Zuur, who has been baking the slow way for decades: rye sourdoughs raised on a living starter, wholemeal loaves that rise through an afternoon, Swiss Zopf plaited by hand, focaccia, and a fermented buckwheat loaf for those who can't take wheat. Her bread is the kind that fills a house with its smell and a table with quiet conversation.

Spend an afternoon with her in our kitchen. You'll mix, knead, plait and bake alongside her. You'll learn how to keep a starter alive, how to read a dough by touch, and the small decisions — temperature, time, a bit of gusto — that turn flour and water into a good loaf.

You'll leave with:

A jar of living starter to take home
A warm loaf from the oven
Doris's full recipe collection (rye sourdough, wholemeal, Swiss Zopf, fermented buckwheat, focaccia, Oaties)
Her "0800 bread helpline" for when you need a hand at home

Afternoon tea included. Bring a clean glass jar with a lid, an apron, and a willingness to slow down.

Good bread likes it slow.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 10:00am at Wharekai - 298 Whitemans Valley Road

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
Valorant Weekend Showdown
# 🎮 VALORANT WEEKEND SHOWDOWN

## A Two-Day Competitive VALORANT Tournament

Get your team together and join us for a full weekend of competitive VALORANT at Respawn Esports Centre.

This is a **Double Elimination 5v5 tournament**, giving teams the opportunity to fight their way back through the Lower Bracket after an early loss rather than being eliminated immediately.

Whether you're competing for the championship, fighting your way through the Lower Bracket, or testing your team against the competition, this event is designed to deliver a proper competitive LAN tournament experience from start to finish.

### 🔥 EVENT HIGHLIGHTS

* 🎮 Standard 5v5 VALORANT
* 🏆 Double Elimination
* 👥 Maximum 8 Teams
* ⚔️ Upper & Lower Brackets
* 🎯 BO1 Matches
* 🏅 Grand Final BO3
* 💰 Cash Prize Pool
* 🗓️ Two-Day Tournament

**Maximum 8 teams. First paid, first confirmed.**

---

# 🏆 TOURNAMENT FORMAT

The tournament will use a **Double Elimination format** consisting of an Upper Bracket and Lower Bracket.

Every team starts in the Upper Bracket.

* A loss in the Upper Bracket moves the team into the Lower Bracket.
* A loss in the Lower Bracket eliminates the team from the tournament.
* Teams can fight their way through the Lower Bracket and make a run for the Grand Final.
* The tournament continues until the final teams remain.

This means **one bad match does not automatically end your tournament**.

The final tournament bracket and match schedule will be published once registrations have closed, teams have been confirmed and the team lock has taken place.

---

# ⚔️ EVENT FORMAT

This is a **Standard 5v5 VALORANT tournament**.

### Tournament Rules

* **Maximum 8 teams**
* **5 players per team**
* Standard VALORANT tournament format
* All standard matches are **Best-of-1 (BO1)**
* Matches use the full **13-round format**
* Overtime will be played where required under the tournament rules
* The **Grand Final will be Best-of-3 (BO3)**

The BO1 format allows the tournament to maintain a good pace across the two-day event while still providing teams with the full standard VALORANT match experience.

The Grand Final will be played as a BO3 to provide a proper championship finish and determine the tournament winner.

---

# 🔒 TEAM CAP & REGISTRATION

This event has a **strict maximum of 8 teams**.

There will be **no additional teams added once all 8 places have been confirmed**.

Each team must register as a complete **5-player team**.

### ⚠️ Registration Does Not Secure Your Place

The first **8 teams to complete payment** will have their places confirmed.

**Registration alone does not guarantee your team's place. Payment does.**

Once 8 teams have been fully paid and confirmed, registrations will close.

### 👥 Team Captain Responsibilities

Team Captains are responsible for:

* Registering their team
* Providing accurate player information
* Ensuring all team members are available for the event
* Arranging payment for their entire team
* Ensuring payment is completed by the required deadline
* Communicating tournament information and updates to their team
* Post in the following channel alerting us that your team has paid https://discord.com/channels/898139022378033154/1484948780062343208

---

# 💰 ENTRY FEE & PAYMENT

### Entry Fee

**$20 per player**

A full 5-player team therefore costs **$100**.

The Team Captain is responsible for arranging payment for their entire team.

### 🔒 Payment Secures Your Place

Your team's tournament place is only confirmed once payment has been received.

**First paid, first confirmed.**

There will be **no on-the-day payments** accepted for tournament entry.

Any team that has registered but has not completed payment by the deadline may be removed from the tournament and their place offered to another team.

### 📅 Payment Deadline

All tournament entry payments must be received by:

**Wednesday 4th November**

**No on-the-day payments will be accepted.**

### 🏦 Bank Deposit

**Expansion NZ Limited**

**02-0316-0592866-000**

### 🏢 In Person

Payment can also be made at the **Respawn Esports Centre Reception**.

Please ensure payment is completed by the deadline to confirm and secure your team's place.

---

# 💵 PRIZE POOL

**60% of all tournament entry fees collected will be allocated directly to the cash prize pool.**

The prize pool will be distributed between the top finishing teams:

🥇 **1st Place**

🥈 **2nd Place**

🥉 **3rd Place**

The final prize pool and exact prize distribution will be confirmed once registrations have closed and the final number of paid teams is known.

**No in-house credit. These are genuine cash prizes.**

The final prize breakdown will be published before the tournament begins.

---

# 👥 TEAM LOCK & FINAL SCHEDULE

All teams will be locked into the tournament **the day before the event**.

Once the team lock has taken place:

* The final team list will be confirmed
* The Double Elimination bracket will be finalised
* Match times will be scheduled
* The final tournament schedule will be published

Once the team lock has taken place, roster changes may not be possible.

Team Captains should ensure all player details are correct before the team lock.

---

# 🗓️ TWO-DAY EVENT

This is a full **two-day Double Elimination tournament**.

All teams should be prepared to remain available throughout the tournament weekend.

Because the tournament uses Double Elimination, the number of matches each team plays will depend on their results.

Teams that remain in the Upper Bracket may play fewer matches, while teams fighting through the Lower Bracket may play additional matches.

The final schedule will be published after the team lock and final bracket have been created.

Teams must be available and ready to play at their scheduled match times.

Failure to be ready when required may result in a **forfeit**.

---

# 🖱️ KEYBOARDS, MICE & PERIPHERALS

Players are welcome to bring and use their own preferred gaming peripherals, including:

* Gaming mouse
* Keyboard
* Mousepad
* Other personal peripherals where permitted

If you do not have your own preferred equipment, **Respawn Esports Centre standard mouse, keyboard and mousepad equipment can be provided**.

If you require Respawn equipment, please let us know **before your scheduled match** so we can ensure it is ready for you.

Players using their own peripherals are responsible for bringing everything they need and ensuring their equipment is working correctly before their match.

---

# ⏱️ MATCH SETUP & WARM-UP

To keep the tournament running on schedule, teams will have a **strict 8-minute setup and warm-up period** before their match.

This time is intended for:

* Setting up personal peripherals
* Connecting equipment
* Checking controls and settings
* Quick warm-up
* Preparing to begin the match

Teams are expected to be ready to play when their allocated setup and warm-up period ends.

Please arrive prepared and have your equipment ready to minimise delays between matches.

The **8-minute setup and warm-up limit will be strictly enforced** to help keep the tournament running on schedule.

---

# 📢 IMPORTANT INFORMATION

By registering your team for this event, you agree to the following:

* Your team must consist of 5 players.
* The event has a strict maximum of 8 teams.
* The first 8 teams to complete payment will have their places confirmed.
* Registration alone does not guarantee your team's place.
* The Team Captain is responsible for organising payment for the entire team.
* All tournament entry payments must be received by **Wednesday 4th November**.
* No on-the-day tournament payments will be accepted.
* Unpaid teams may be removed from the tournament and their place offered to another team.
* All standard tournament matches are Best-of-1 (BO1).
* Standard matches use the full 13-round format.
* Overtime will be played where required under the tournament rules.
* The Grand Final will be Best-of-3 (BO3).
* Teams will be locked the day before the event.
* Teams must be available for the full tournament weekend.
* Teams must be ready to play at their scheduled match time.
* An **8-minute setup and warm-up period** applies before matches.
* Failure to attend or be ready for a scheduled match may result in a forfeit.
* Tournament administration and final rulings will be handled by the event organisers.

---

events.long_description:
A high tea to delight your eyes and taste buds – with new menu inspired by Slow Burn: Women and Photography.

Inspired by Slow Burn: Women and Photography, the latest Eat Your Art Out high tea menu takes its cue from the world of photography.

From the delicate A Heart Exposed and the rich depth of The Chocolate Camera, to the savoury kick of The Apricot Proof, each item has been crafted by our award-winning chefs and is ready for its close-up.

Your high tea includes your choice of tea or coffee, with alcoholic beverages available to purchase. Dietary options are available on request.

Every purchase helps support Aotearoa New Zealand’s national museum.


Set Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

A Heart Exposed
A delicate petite gâteau of tropical guava mousse layered with a vibrant raspberry centre, finished with refined textures and a balance of sweetness, bright berry acidity, and silky indulgence.

The Matcha Take
A refined Japanese-inspired madeleine infused with premium matcha, baked to a tender crumb with gentle earthy depth. Paired with luscious matcha ganache and sharp citrus bursts of yuzu gel.

The Chocolate Camera
An elegant chocolate creation showcasing the rich, velvety depth of premium Whittaker’s chocolate balanced with the vibrant citrus brightness of calamansi.

Golden Hour
A radiant tropical dessert crafted with luscious mango mousse and vibrant passionfruit notes, layered to create a light yet indulgent finish.

The Apricot Proof
A savoury petite muffin featuring sweet roasted capsicum folded through a soft, buttery crumb with delicate pockets of apricot for subtle fruity warmth.

Chicken Strut
Delicately layered smoked chicken paired with crisp cucumber ribbons, peppery rocket, and vibrant red pesto, nestled between soft artisan bread.

Green Screen Sandwich (V)
A beautifully balanced vegetarian finger sandwich showcasing tender grilled courgette, slow-roasted vegetable chutney, and fresh baby spinach.


Dietary Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

The Mango Still (VE/GF)
A smooth mango mousse encased in a delicate chocolate shell, showcasing the fruit’s natural sweetness.

Peanut Butter Proof (VE/GF)
A rich peanut butter slice topped with a chocolate finish, balancing salty depth with a smooth, indulgent crumb.

Chocolate Darkroom (VE/GF)
Dark chocolate cups filled with smooth espresso-infused ganache, rich and intense from start to finish.

Matcha Moment (VE/GF)
Matcha chocolate shells with a bright citrus centre, balancing earthy green tea notes against a fresh citrus snap.

Apricot Aperture (VE/GF)
A vibrant apricot fruit jelly with an intense natural fruit flavour, finished with a delicate sugar coating for a clean, bright bite.

The Garden Negative (VE)
Tender grilled courgette layered with slow-roasted vegetable chutney and fresh baby spinach.

Fritter in Focus (VE)
Golden corn fritters served with beetroot mayonnaise, mesclun leaves, and vine-ripened tomatoes.


Paired with your choice of coffee or tea.

Alcoholic beverages are available for purchase.

Pre-booking is essential for any dietary requirements.

Dietary sandwiches can be made gluten-free on request.

events.long_description:
Join a Shared Guided Tour and experience Stonehenge Aotearoa through the eyes of an expert. In this 90-minute journey, you’ll uncover how ancient cultures measured time, tracked the Sun and Moon, and connected the heavens with life on Earth.

Your experience begins with a captivating introduction and a 15-minute audio-visual presentation explaining how the Henge works. Then, step outside with your guide for a detailed tour of the stone circle, where astronomy, archaeology, and mythology come together in one unforgettable setting.

Perfect for visitors seeking a deeper understanding of the stars and stories that shaped human history.

events.long_description:
Overview

Try your hand at the creative skills behind the movies — from special effects makeup and costume to sword-making, slime and more!

With fantastical creatures, elven jewels, warriors’ armour, vampire portraits and more, Scene Stealers shines the spotlight on the artists behind Aotearoa New Zealand’s film industry. Many of these incredible craftspeople who make movie magic will be at The Dowse to celebrate the opening of this exciting exhibition. There will be opportunities for you to hear from them, see them in action…and even get in on the action yourself.

Scars and Scrapes with Wētā Workshop. Scare your friends with the addition of a special effects scar applied by the team from Wētā Workshop.

Barbarian Productions Dress Up Jam. Get into character with Barbarian Productions and their seemingly bottomless wardrobe department of costumes for you to try on and style. Dress up, act up and wig out!

Fighting and Falling. Stunt Master Allan Henry will teach the tricks of the trade and have you looking like you’re rumbling with the heavyweights without ever landing a punch.

These activities are part of a day of programmes celebrating the opening of Scene Stealers. This also includes industry experts in panel talks:
10.30-11.30am Scene Stealers In Discussion: Creative Costuming
12-1pm Scene Stealers In Discussion: Behind the Lens

events.long_description:
Dive into the fantastic realm of foliage and discover what plants have to teach us about worlds present and past.

Join us for a 60 to 75-minute guided walk exploring the fascinating world of plants and the stories they tell. From ancient survivors and remarkable adaptations to the clues plants give us about changing landscapes, you'll discover how foliage can reveal both the history of our planet and the natural world around us.

As we make our way downhill through Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā, we'll stop to admire a diverse range of trees, shrubs, and groundcovers while uncovering the science, history, and surprising tales hidden among the leaves.

Whether you're a keen gardener, a nature enthusiast, or simply curious to see the garden from a new perspective, this relaxed walk offers plenty to discover.

Meet at the Cable Car Lookout on Upland Road, Kelburn.
Cost: $10 or Free for Friends – bookings required (you’ll get the option to choose your ticket type after clicking ‘Buy Tickets’)

This is part of the regular walks run by the Friends of the Wellington Botanic Garden. They run throughout the year with a different topic every time.

Join the Friends for only $30 a year and all the walks will be free, as well as other great benefits.

events.long_description:
Koha Day at Upper Hutt's Golder Cottage at 707 Fergusson Drive
The Cottage is celebrating its 150 birthday this year!

Come and explore the home of John and Jane Golder and their 12 children. Take a peek into the past and marvel at the way Upper Hutt people lived before electricity and water were installed. You can see the ancient soil tiller and the lawnmower in the washhouse and view the washing paraphernalia used all day on Mondays (washing day).

Faultline Lacemakers will join us again and you can try your hand at lacemaking, along with Upper Hutt Spinners & Weavers demonstrating their craft.

Our stall will be out the front with home baking, jams and preserves, hand-knitted garments, plants & garden books.

Hope to see you there!

Cost: Koha

Learn more on our website:

events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Permaculture Design Workshop that goes well beyond the garden patch. This afternoon session introduces you to permaculture as a design tool for life itself — your community projects, your business, your relationships, even your next family meal.

We'll explore the design process together, then apply it to real situations in small groups. You'll learn to use permaculture ethics as a lens: Is what I'm doing caring for the planet and people? Is it ensuring a fair share of resources? This isn't about following recipes — it's about principles, careful assessment, and truly listening to what each unique situation needs.

When you reach a crossroads in life, whether chosen or unexpected, the permaculture design tool offers a framework. A scaffold for moving forward with intention, embracing diversity and care, and making good use of your time and energy.

This is an introductory session. The topic is as vast as life itself, and as diverse and magical as the natural world around us.

We'll gather in the garden if weather allows, otherwise in the Whare Kai. Expect circle work and small breakout groups where we'll learn from each other's experiences.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 2:00pm at the Mangaroa Events space at 298 Whitemans Valley Road.

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
This workshop will demonstrate the very basics of Tukutuku where each participant will come away with a form of Tukutuku and knowledge to inspire their own mahi toi. 

All materials supplied. Prior to the workshop participants are encouraged to research Tukutuku patterns and become familiar with the meanings.

 

Artist biography.
Elena Rei
Ngāti Toarangatira, Ngāruahine, Ngāti Koata, Ngāti Tama, Sāmoa 

Elena Rei’s creative practice sits within the realm of Te Whare Pora, weaving together customary and contemporary processes of raranga, whatu muka and tukutuku. Interlaced throughout her works are collective dreams, moments of remembering and profound experiences with the materials she uses. Much of Elena’s practice is intuitive, emulating the ways of her tūpuna and drawing from a visual language that has been woven through time. Her works reimage and make familiar our inherent connection to ngā atua wāhine, through themes of aroha, grief, whakapapa and reconnection. 

Elena studied design and textiles at Massey University, where she gained early insights into practices within Te Whare Pora. A formative experience during this time was learning tukutuku under the guidance of Kohai Grace during classes at Whitireia, an experience that continues to inform her practice today.

events.long_description:
In Search of My Moehau (2026)

Directors: Kieran Charnock and Jonathan Watt
Genre: Drama / Comedy | Rated M
Venue: Circus Cinema, Martinborough
Date: Saturday 7 November 2026 | 3pm

Tickets: Book directly through Circus Cinema. Make a phone reservation: 06 306 9442 or book online: https://www.circus.net.nz/films

About the film

What begins as a search for a missing father takes a decidedly strange turn in In Search of My Moehau, a darkly comic found-footage mockumentary set deep in the New Zealand bush.

Morris Fubbins is convinced his father has been taken by a mythical creature. As his search unfolds, folklore, obsession and the absurd collide in this offbeat New Zealand feature, bringing a distinctly Kiwi twist to the found-footage tradition popularised by The Blair Witch Project.

Meet the filmmaker

We're delighted to welcome director Jonathan Watt to the screening. Jonathan will introduce the film and stay afterwards to answer questions, offering audiences an opportunity to hear more about the making of the film and the creative thinking behind this wonderfully unconventional story.

A special Spring Sessions screening

Hot off the festival circuit, In Search of My Moehau enjoyed a successful run at Whānau Mārama New Zealand International Film Festival, screening in Auckland, Wellington, Christchurch and Masterton.

We're pleased to bring the film to Circus Cinema, Martinborough, as part of Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival's Spring Sessions 2026. Directors Kieran Charnock and Jonathan Watt have strong Wairarapa connections and have been making films together for more than 20 years.

This is a special opportunity to experience the film on the big screen and meet one of the filmmakers.

Saturday 7 November | 3pm
Circus Cinema, Martinborough

See the films, meet the filmmaker.

Ear plugs will be provided but bringing your own ear protection is encouraged, especially for under-5s.

events.long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

We will be running 2 starts for this course:
Dates for course:
First course: September 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th
Second course: November 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th

events.long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity as a son or daughter of God led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart of a King: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Remembering: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voices: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Forge: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Roots: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

Sandra has a deep passion for seeing people encounter the healing love and transforming power of Jesus Christ. Through teaching, prayer ministry, mentoring, and training, she helps people understand the impact of trauma and woundedness, and to find healing, rediscover their God-given identity, and step more fully into who God created them to be.

Her teaching combines biblical truth, practical understanding, personal experience, and more than two decades of ministry experience, with an emphasis on creating a safe and compassionate space for people to honour their stories and encounter Jesus.

This event is not suitable for those under 16.

events.long_description:
Exhale Evolution
✨ Grounded Grace Counselling x Alchemy Ascending ✨

https://momence.com/Yoga-Corner/EXHALE-EVOLUTION/143442298

3 hour workshop, Movement ~ Breathwork ~ Sound Journey

Saxon Brazier from Grounded Grace Counselling and Kez Milne from Alchemy Ascending bring you a 3-hour immersive workshop combining Somatic Movement, Conscious Connected Breathwork and Sound Odyssey.

A deep dive into the body — creating space to slow down, rest, digest and reconnect with what is happening beneath the surface.

You might arrive carrying stress, emotions, old hurts, tension, overwhelm or simply the weight of everyday life.

Through conscious connected breathwork, somatic movement and sound, we create a safe and supported space to explore what your body may be holding — without needing to force, fix or figure anything out.


🌿 CONSCIOUS CONNECTED BREATHWORK

Conscious Connected Breathwork is a rhythmic breathing practice where the inhale and exhale are intentionally connected, creating a continuous flow of breath without pause.

As we consciously connect the breath, we bring greater awareness into the body. Physical sensations, emotions, thoughts and patterns may begin to come into awareness, creating space to notice and explore what is present.

Rather than trying to think our way through an experience, the breath invites us to move out of the thinking mind and into the body — meeting whatever arises with curiosity, awareness and compassion.

The practice is centred around presence and allowing, rather than forcing an emotional release or trying to create a particular outcome.


🎶 SOUND ODYSSEY

Following the breathwork, Saxon's Sound Odyssey will invite you into a deeply immersive sound experience designed to help you settle, integrate and reconnect with the body.

Having previously sold out her Sound Odyssey experiences, Saxon weaves together drums, medicine drum, guitar and vocals to create a rich and organic soundscape.

Moving from rhythm and activation into softer, settling vibrations, the sound journey offers space to simply lie back, breathe and receive.

A meeting point of sound, vibration, voice and stillness — allowing the body and nervous system time to integrate whatever has arisen during the breathwork.


✨ YOUR FACILITATORS

Kez Milne — Alchemy Ascending
400-hour accredited Conscious Connected Breathwork Facilitator.

Saxon Brazier — Grounded Grace Counselling
Registered trauma-informed counsellor with training in breathwork and somatic facilitation.
https://www.groundedgrace.nz/

Together, Saxon and Kez will hold a grounded, carefully facilitated container for you to explore breath, body, emotion and sound.


⚠️ SAFETY & CONTRAINDICATIONS

Safety is paramount. Breathwork is not suitable for everyone.

Conscious Connected Breathwork involves sustained, active breathing and can produce significant physical and emotional experiences. For this reason, there are certain circumstances where participation may not be appropriate.

This workshop may not be suitable for you if you:

• Are pregnant or may be pregnant
• Have a history of cardiovascular disease, heart attack or significant heart problems
• Have uncontrolled high blood pressure
• Have a history of stroke, aneurysm or significant vascular disease
• Have epilepsy or a seizure disorder
• Have severe or uncontrolled asthma or significant respiratory disease
• Have a current serious psychiatric condition, psychosis or significant difficulty distinguishing internal experiences from external reality
• Are experiencing acute psychological distress or significant mental health instability
• Have recently undergone major surgery or have another significant medical condition that may make intensive breathwork unsafe
• Are under the influence of alcohol or recreational drugs
• Have another medical or psychological condition that may make an intensive breathwork practice unsafe for you

If you are unsure whether this practice is appropriate for you, please speak with your doctor or qualified healthcare professional before booking.

Participation is voluntary and you can stop or modify the practice at any time.

Every participant will be required to read the full disclaimer and contraindications and sign a waiver confirming that they understand and agree to the terms before entering the workshop space.

We take the responsibility of holding this space seriously. Safety, consent, choice and nervous-system awareness are paramount throughout the experience.


🌿 BOOKING & ONBOARDING

Once your booking has been made, we will send you a full onboarding pack with everything you need to know before the workshop, including what to bring, how to prepare and important instructions for arriving and entering the space.


3 HOURS

Somatic Movement • Conscious Connected Breathwork • Sound Odyssey


Come as you are.

Create some space.

Breathe. Move. Feel. Listen. Integrate.

Tickets here:

https://momence.com/Yoga-Corner/EXHALE-EVOLUTION/143442298

events.long_description:
Ubuntu Cultural Conversations
The Undercurrent presents Ubuntu Cultural Conversations!

The Ubuntu Cultural Conversation is an interactive and inclusive cultural event that explores how humanity is understood, expressed, preserved, and shared through diverse cultural perspectives. Through a combination of live music, poetry, storytelling, and open audience conversations, the event will create a space for meaningful dialogue, cultural exchange, reflection, and connection.

The programme will feature live musical performances by Ras Judah (Botswana), Mohamed Shemi (Tanzania), and friends, alongside poetry and opportunities for audience participation. Shared cultural food will further contribute to the spirit of hospitality, community, and connection that lies at the heart of Ubuntu.

The African concept of Ubuntu is often expressed through the powerful saying, “I am because we are.” Rather than placing individual achievement at the centre of social life, Ubuntu emphasises the importance of community, cooperation, reciprocity, and shared wellbeing. It encourages us to recognise the humanity in one another and to respond to the challenges faced by others with understanding, kindness, and support.

The philosophy of Ubuntu reminds us that our lives are enriched when we care for one another, celebrate our differences, and work collectively to create inclusive and connected communities. It offers an opportunity to reflect on what it means to be human and how our relationships with others shape the societies in which we live.

Saturday Nov 7
Doors 6:30pm
Start 7pm
$15

Tickets available online and at the door!
https://www.undertheradar.co.nz/gig/105488/Ubuntu-Cultural-Conversations.utr

events.name: After God
events.venue: Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
From the creators of the wildly praised, fiercely original verbatim plays TRANSMISSION and TRANSMISSION:BETA, the New Zealand premiere of AFTER GOD is a theatrical journey across continents and conversations, with one of Aotearoa’s most distinguished actors, Michael Hurst, joining director Miranda Harcourt and writer Stuart McKenzie to explore big questions about meaning, madness and metaphysics.

With a hungry mind and burning questions, McKenzie hits the road — travelling from Wellington to Kathmandu, London and New York. Along the way, he encounters a vivid cast of real-life characters: theologians, Tibetan rinpoches, philosophers, cosmologists, taxi drivers, hotel receptionists, a famous singing nun — and his own mother. Each has their own radically different way of making sense of existence.

Created entirely from real conversations, AFTER GOD is a new verbatim theatre work, transforming interviews, ideas and personal stories into an exhilarating theatrical experience.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

The Undercurrent presents Ubuntu Cultural Conversations!

The Ubuntu Cultural Conversation is an interactive and inclusive cultural event that explores how humanity is understood, expressed, preserved, and shared through diverse cultural perspectives. Through a combination of live music, poetry, storytelling, and open audience conversations, the event will create a space for meaningful dialogue, cultural exchange, reflection, and connection.

The programme will feature live musical performances by Ras Judah (Botswana), Mohamed Shemi (Tanzania), and friends, alongside poetry and opportunities for audience participation. Shared cultural food will further contribute to the spirit of hospitality, community, and connection that lies at the heart of Ubuntu.

The African concept of Ubuntu is often expressed through the powerful saying, “I am because we are.” Rather than placing individual achievement at the centre of social life, Ubuntu emphasises the importance of community, cooperation, reciprocity, and shared wellbeing. It encourages us to recognise the humanity in one another and to respond to the challenges faced by others with understanding, kindness, and support.

The philosophy of Ubuntu reminds us that our lives are enriched when we care for one another, celebrate our differences, and work collectively to create inclusive and connected communities. It offers an opportunity to reflect on what it means to be human and how our relationships with others shape the societies in which we live.

Saturday Nov 7
Doors 6:30pm
Start 7pm
$15

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

We’ll see you there ☆

events.long_description:
Trentham Racecourse Ghost Investigation
Saturday 7 November
7:30 PM – 9.30pm or 7.30pm -12am
Step inside Trentham Racecourse after dark for a paranormal investigation at one of Wellington’s most historic sporting venues.
Established in 1906, Trentham Racecourse has witnessed more than a century of racing history. During WWII, parts of the racecourse were used as a military hospital and accommodation for American troops, while nearby Trentham Camp played an important role during WWI.
Ghost Connections is the only paranormal investigation group with access to investigate inside this historic venue, giving you a rare opportunity to explore areas of Trentham Racecourse after hours and investigate its history from an entirely different perspective.
Use paranormal investigation equipment, take part in experiments and join us as we search for unexplained activity once the racecourse falls silent.
Trentham Racecourse, Upper Hutt

events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Dublin International Film Festival -

The always-brilliant Bill Nighy stars in 500 Miles, a life-affirming celebration of the human spirit that follows a broken family who are forced to come together when their two young boys run away from home. After hearing their parents fight, Finn (Roman Griffin Davis, Jojo Rabbit) and Charlie (Dexter Sol Ansell, breakout star of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms) sneak out of their house in Doncaster.

So unfolds an epic road trip from Yorkshire, over land and sea, to the wild West Coast of Ireland. Their destination? The small seaside town of Dingle, County Kerry, where they will reunite with their beloved Grandfather, John (Nighy).

It’s a long, treacherous journey - 500 miles where a lot could go wrong... And while Dingle holds happy memories for the boys, Grandpa John has remained estranged from Finn and Charlie’s parents after fateful events the previous summer.

With knockout performances from all involved, 500 Miles will make you laugh, cry, and hug the people you love.

events.name: Kina:suttsu (Japan) + vegetable.animal.machine
events.venue: 272 Taranaki Street, New Zealand 6001,272 Taranaki St, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Kina:suttsu (Japan) + vegetable.animal.machine
Pyramid Club is excited to present Japanese musician, performance and visual artist Kina:suttsu. Utilising saxophone, electronics, noise, and field recordings, Kina:suttsu creates immersive performances that blur the boundaries between ancient ritual and contemporary experimental music.

Since releasing her first album in 2005, she has performed and exhibited in Japan and internationally. Her releases include music on labels in the UK and France, including a cassette as NAVU and a collaborative release with Phil MFU, Zongamin, E-Da (ex Boredoms, Seefeel). She has recorded with legendary bassist Jah Wobble and released a live recording with Damo Suzuki. In 2021, she appeared in and composed the soundtrack for British filmmaker Daisy Dickinson’s short film Kaki no Shizuku, which was selected for the Los Angeles Film Awards.
-
vegetable.machine.animal (vma) is an interspecies improvisational trio led by drummer Kieran Monaghan, which transforms the electrical signals of living plants and fungi into sound, fusing modular synths and live percussion in performances that are spontaneous, rhythmic, and unpredictable. This is music as a living system - a real-time collaboration where non-human organisms shape the sonic outcome alongside human performers.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

events.long_description:
Kia ora koutou, we are pleased to be welcomed through the airlock of Moon Bar this November for our inaugural event. We are a new collective of selectors looking to get hips moving and contribute to the alive and kicking Welly scene. Expect silly, fun but considered multi-genre dance music.

What does 'Niced Up' even mean? First heard on a festival dancefloor from someone with an inability to conjure up anything more profound, it was used to describe the exact moment when everything had peaked exactly at the same time with no negative energy in sight. It's exactly where we intend to be on November 7th.

We know it is election night so there will definitely be reasons to laugh and cheer, or cry and wail, but this is best done with friends and backdropped by tunes, so we think we’ve got you covered. What’s more, it’s free entry all night long!

We can't wait to see ya, bring your friends, bring your Whānau.

events.id: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India-Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India
events.venue: Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This spring, Wellington will celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. The city will showcase its strong Indian community and cultural connections. This century milestone traces back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team toured New Zealand for the first time, bringing players and communities together. Since then, sport has played an important role in connecting our countries — notably through hockey and cricket, but also across many other sports and exchanges. 

From 23 October to 15 November, Frank Kitts Park and the waterfront promenade will host a free public exhibition. Light Box Historic Walk will feature 10 illuminated light boxes that share stories of Wellington-specific links between India and New Zealand. You’ll also find The Fan Hub on 6 and 7 November as well as 14 and 15 November. Enjoy a feast with local food truck favourites, offering a taste of Wellington's rich culinary scene. Or start the day with sunrise yoga sessions hosted by AWHI Yoga against the stunning waterfront backdrop. To cap off all the excitement, the BLACKCAPS take on India three times in Wellington as part of their summer season.

The Sport100 Fan Hub is proudly delivered through collaboration between WellingtonNZ, Sport New Zealand, Wellington City Council, Cricket Wellington, and New Zealand Cricket, creating a festive gathering place for locals and visitors to connect, celebrate, and enjoy the atmosphere whilst Wellington hosts cricketing giants India in the capital.

Join two major Wellington talents for an afternoon of musical delights. The Michael Fowler Centre hosts a collaborative show for the whole family. ‘Air Force in Concert with Bret McKenzie’ includes kid-friendly hits from Flight of the Conchords, The Muppets, The Black Seeds, and Brett's recent album. events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”

events.long_description:
It looks like New Zealand Cricket (NZC) has smashed it for six. The 2026-27 international home season of cricket promises an exciting few months of action across the country. Wellington has scored six major opportunities to see the BLACKCAPS and WHITE FERNS in action. Three formidable opponents are travelling to New Zealand’s shores. The Indian, Bangladeshi, and Sri Lankan teams have booked their tickets for Aotearoa and will play tests, ODIs, and T20 matches against the Kiwi women’s and men’s teams. 
The Indian men’s team will be particularly busy during their visit. With twelve matches booked against the BLACKCAPS, it will be the most internationals scheduled for an Indian men’s tour in NZC history. Fans will get their chance to see them duke it out in all three formats across the capital, beginning with a T20 at Hnry Stadium on 27 October. 
Make sure you don’t miss the WHITE FERNS. They host Bangladesh in Wellington in a T20 and ODI, during their only home tour of the summer. The Wellington schedule finishes with a visit from Sri Lanka for an ODI against the BLACKCAPS on 19 January at the Cello Basin Reserve.   
With games split across Hnry Stadium and Cello Basin Reserve, the city will be bouncing with life. The 2025/26 season saw bumper crowds, and our men's and women's sides are set to build on this exciting momentum.

Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.name: Duntulm Farm Wairarapa Dog Walk
events.venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
events.long_description:
The Wairarapa Dogwalk Group is an informal group of dog owners who get together once a month to exercise our dogs. The aim of the walks is to go somewhere in the region where we can walk the dogs off lead.
The Duntulm Farm walk is one of our favourites.
On private property in a seldom visited area of the Tararua foothills that offers two walks. Both stop at the Trotternish Shed which is located beside a hidden large pond on a remote corner of the farm for a cup of tea / coffee and a snack.

The Valley Walk follows a gentle 4WD track up a steep sided valley to the shed.
Depending on the weather the return walk can go down the opposite side of the valley via Side by Side vehicle tracks.
Walking time is about 60 minutes including an approximately 15 minute stop at the shed.

The UP and Over walk is for the fitter walkers.
It climbs steeply up Side by Side tracks up to the ridgeline. There is a lookout point with unique views into the Tararuas. A 10 minute stop to catch your breath then the track descends quickly down into the valley and around to the shed for drinks and snacks.
We return to the carpark via the Valley walk 4WD track.
Around a 2 hour walk (including stops).
Walkers on this walk are recommended to carry a small backpack with water and extra clothing.

events.name: Raphael House Steiner School Fair - Outdoor Music Stage
events.venue: 27 Matuhi St, Tirohanga, Lower Hutt 5010
events.long_description:
Raphael House Steiner School Fair - Outdoor Music Stage
Get ready for a fantastic day of live music at the annual Raphael House Steiner Fair Outdoor Music Stage! Celebrating the diversity and creativity of Aotearoa’s music scene, this year’s lineup brings together an exciting mix of heavy riffs, alternative rock, underground sounds and captivating solo performances. Featuring Stretch to Mould, Damiasharko, Hexxer, Undies, Datu Beech, Athena Clark with Cyan Ye and Vince Cabrera, there’s something for every music lover. Come along, support local musicians, soak up the festival atmosphere and enjoy a brilliant day of live music, community spirit and family-friendly fun!

Wellington rock trio Stretch to Mould bring hard-hitting riffs, powerful vocals and dynamic musicianship to the stage. Expect energetic alternative rock with plenty of intensity and a sound built for live performance.

The solo project of Haylee Hailwood, guitarist and vocalist of Wellington grungegaze band Cruelly, Damiasharko explores a gentler, more intimate side of her songwriting. Expect atmospheric sounds, heartfelt emotion and an alternative edge.

Wellington’s Hexxer delivers adventurous alternative rock that blends gritty guitar work, experimental songwriting and unexpected musical turns. Balancing intensity with atmosphere, Hexxer offers a compelling dose of the capital’s independent rock sound.

Undies, (3/5 of Wellington favourites Underwire), serve up catchy indie rock with a punchy, energetic live sound. Mixing alternative rock with surf-punk attitude, garage-rock grit and ska influences, they bring infectious melodies and plenty of personality to the stage.

A familiar face in Te Whanganui-a-Tara’s music community, Datu Beech brings experience across multiple projects and genres, including emo outfit Crying Club and his work with Hunter Jackson. Look forward to a performance showcasing the creativity of Wellington’s interconnected music scene.

Ex-student Athena Clark joins the lineup with a performance celebrating the talent and individuality of Aotearoa’s local music scene. A welcome addition to a diverse programme of artists and sounds. She is supported by Cian Ye, a talented guitarist and singer.

Pink Shoggoth is the solo project of Upper Hutt musician Vince Cabrera, who creates distinctive instrumental music using acoustic bass, blending melodic, ambient and cinematic qualities. His thoughtful, understated approach offers a chance to slow down and appreciate the expressive possibilities of an unconventional solo instrument. Vince sings songs about myths and legends around the world.

Free entry!
Come make a candle and shoot an arrow!!

Undies 11:20 am
Datu Beech 12:00 pm
hexxer 12:40 pm

Stretch to Mould (full band) from 2pm onwards

A super fun day-class, ideal as a stand-alone experience, or as a day to get stuck into projects with your tutor at hand.

Beginners choose from a range of achievable patterns and choose their colour palette. They will learn to cut the glass, and prepare it before foiling and soldering each piece, creating a simple elegant colourful glass project.

The aim of this one day class is to leave with a completed small leadlight glass item.

More experienced students may bring existing projects to work on in class - though emphasis will be placed on focusing on the same techniques of flat, nicely soldered simple designs.

This is a warm and friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and more advanced students. All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.

Your materials for your beginner project are supplied as part of your course fee.
Additional materials and tools are available to purchase.

Not suitable for children. Older teenagers (16+) are welcome.

events.venue: 74 Truscott Avenue, Johnsonville, Wellington 6037, New Zealand
events.long_description:
If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

⛰️ TRAIL INFO

Trail: Skyline Track, Johnsonville

Length: Out & back (halfway), approx. 12km, 460m elevation gain, around 3 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

🎒 WHAT TO BRING?

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

events.name: Twin Peaks The Return: Parts 13, 14, 15
events.venue: 7 Colombo Street, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
events.long_description:
"It was a dream...We live inside a dream"

-Phillip Jeffries

We are now hurtling towards the brilliant conclusion of the series with our second LAST screening of "The Return: Parts 13, 14, 15"

These episodes are truly incredible with arguably the most emotional moments of the entire show.

Also ever since "Fire Walk With Me", every single fan has been haunted for 25 years by the inexplicable lore surrounding David Bowie's character. Get ready to come "full circle" as we meet once again the original head and founding member of the Blue Rose Task Force: The enigmatic Special Agent "Phillip Jeffries" in The Return!

Last seen at "The Palm Deluxe Hotel" in Buenos Aires, Argentina. We will be screening the mythic, uncut original and extended David Bowie performance from "The Missing Pieces of FWWM" to melt our minds in preparation.

It's gonna be a big session filled with emotional highs and lows and filled to the coffee cup brim with lore. So if you're a Twin Peaks fan you can't miss this one!

We'll be playing Parts 13,14,15 from the "Z to A" Blu-ray projected from a 4K player onto a 5.5m x 3.7m screen.

Written by Mark Frost, David Lynch and directed by David Lynch.

This is what we will be watching :

David Lynch "Weather Report" and song of the day.

"Previously on Twin Peaks"

The Missing Pieces: "Buenos Aires, Above the Convenience Store" (23mins)

The Return: Part 13 - "What story is that, Charlie?" (58mins)

Intermission

The Return: Part 14 - "We are like the dreamer." (55mins)

The Return: Part 15 - "There's some fear in letting go." (53mins)

WHERE: Newtown Community Centre. 7 Colombo St. Newtown.

(nb: There is no onsite parking and parking on surrounding streets can be hard to find)

 

WHEN: Gather from 10:45am on Sunday 8th November 2026.

The screening shall start at 11:00am SHARP!



COST: A lucky $7.

This is a small (<40) not for profit community event put on for the love of Twin Peaks and the fans!

All proceeds go to help pay for the venue hire and fun snacks! So come join your fellow Twin Peaks fans as we "shovel our way" through some donuts, "two cookies and a coke...it's phenomenal!"


RULES:
1. Please purchase a ticket for each person beforehand, as capacity is limited to ~40 seats

2. All attendees MUST be 18yo +

3. This is a safe, friendly, INCLUSIVE place. There is ZERO tolerance for discrimination, disrespect or creepy gross behavior of any kind. By attending you agree to the Code of Conduct.

4. Doors close and it's lights off and "Shhhh Shush!!!!" at 11:00am. Don't be late!

5. No Alcohol / No Smoking is permitted.

Thank you! "This is your shiny, gold shovel. Two coats, guaranteed."

Join us for more Twin Peaks community screenings at:

www.facebook.com/fishinthepercolator

www.instagram.com/fishinthe.percolator

Overview

Love cake? So do we! Join us at The Cake Club Picnic – a one-of-a-kind gathering dedicated exclusively to cake. You don't want to miss it!

Welcome to The Cake Club Picnic! 🍰

By popular demand and our first cake picnic was a success, we are happy to host another epic Cake Picnic!

Join us for a deliciously fun day out at Bellevue Gardens Hotel on Sunday, November the 8th, 2026.

Whether your a professional baker, a passionate home baker, or simply someone with a sweet tooth, The Cake Club Picnic is the perfect event to indulge your love of all things cake!

Entry requires both a ticket and a cake - one per person.
Everyone attending must bring a cake of their own. No cake, no entry - no exceptions. This rule keeps things fair and fun for everyone involved.

Even if you're bringing a guest under tickets you have purchased, they must bring a cake too. Sharing one cake between two people won’t cut it. We appreciate your understanding and commitment to the cake-loving community!

🎂 What to Expect:

A relaxed indoor and outdoor garden setting - enjoy the space rain or shine!

A shared cake table filled with baked goodies brought by everyone attending - taste, share, and show off your creations!

Chill vibes and great company - meet fellow cake lovers, swap stories, and make sweet memories.

Picnic-style seating - bring a blanket, find a sunny spot, or grab a seat indoors.

A self-service tea and coffee station to keep your cup full as you sample cakes.

Cake Size Requirement:
Please bring a cake that can generously serve at least 12 people. Think full-sized bakes -enough to share and make sure everyone gets a proper slice (or two)! 🎂✨ - REMEMBER - CAKE ONLY!

Cake Set-Up:
You’re welcome to do final touch-ups at the venue, but please avoid full setups or major decorating on-site. Display tables will be shared with other guests, so we want to keep things smooth and stress-free for everyone.

Serving Tools, cake detailed label & Cake Stands:

events.long_description:
Malaysian Style Deepavali Feast
Kia ora!

Celebrating Deepavali? Curious about Malaysian Indian festive food? Looking for a delicious meal and a lovely way to spend your day? Come join us! 😃

Coming Sunday, we at Macha Jom Tapau are bringing together a delicious spread of Malaysian favourites, lovingly prepared by Chef Muthu, to make our Deepavali (known as Diwali here) celebration extra special 🥰

The menu:
😋 Thosai (rice flour crepes)
😋 Rava Idli (steamed savoury semolina cake)
😋 Mini Roti Canai
😋 Ulunthu Vadai (savoury black gram fritter)
😋 Potato Masala (spiced potato)
😋 Vegetable Dalcha (rich flavourful lentil and vegetable stew)
😋 Prawn Sambal (classic fiery dish in aromatic chilli paste)
😋 Chicken Masala (tender chicken pieces cooked in spiced onion and tomato gravy)
😋 Lamb & Potato Curry (comforting dish with a mix of aromatic herbs and spices)
😋 Deepavali Treats

Come try these comforting classics, rich curries, and all those beautiful flavours that remind us of Deepavali festive gatherings and home-cooked goodness back home in Malaysia.

And of course, what's Deepavali without treats, both sweet and savoury! I'm in the midst of making some 😃

We'll be displaying all the dishes buffet-style, so you can take a look at the spread and serve yourself one generous serving of the dishes you'd love to try 😋

Bring your family, gather your friends, or simply come as you are. Everyone is welcome 🤗

Come hungry, leave happy, and let's celebrate the Festival of Lights together! 🎉

We look forward to celebrating Deepavali with you! 🥰

Follow us on our Facebook or Instagram for updates.

See you!

events.name: A Talent for Murder - British and Irish Film Festival
events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

British national treasure Helen Mirren plays The Talented Mr. Ripley author Patricia Highsmith in this deeply intriguing thriller.

A Talent for Murder takes place in 1995, with Highsmith now in her seventies - and in poor health. Retired to her secluded house in the Swiss Alps, the author keeps to her study, immersed in her books, accompanied by her cats, and surrounded by a collection of antique weapons.

Highsmith’s solitude is interrupted by the arrival of Edward Ridgeway (recent Tony-winner Alden Ehrenreich), a mysterious messenger from a New York publisher, sent to persuade the author to write one final instalment of the Ripley anthology. Aggravated by the unexpected visit from this youthful, overly eager envoy, Patricia declines the offer. That is, unless Ridgeway can help her in conjuring up the perfect murder story.

Mirren embodies the wickedly manipulative author with gusto, while Ehrenreich imbues Ridgeway with enough guile to keep us guessing at his motives.

From director Anton Corbijn (Control), A Talent for Murder is replete with brilliant twists, biting dialogue, and delicious entanglements. Direct from its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, don’t miss this highly anticipated thriller!

Yoga Voice is a form of yoga combining specific vocal tones to tune into the body as a sounding and breathing apparatus. These classes are ideal for anyone who uses their voice and wants to keep their body and voice in optimal health, it can be especially beneficial for singers, actors, performers, yoga practitioners, teachers and musicians.

4 classes for the price of 3 $60.00 book before 1st Nov.

Sascha Perfect (RYT 200 RYVT250)

Her yoga journey began in Ireland and she has trained with voice and somatic practitioners in Europe including Frank Van De Ven, Tadashi Endo, Enrique Pardo, Anne Marie Blink, Karina Schelde and traditional Vedic chanting with Menaka Desikachar.

events.id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Textured Bracelets
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident, you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery-making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee; if you wish to work in silver, you can purchase it on the day.

Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from a flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock.)

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

events.name: Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
events.venue: Futuna Close, off Friend Street, Karori, New Zealand 6012,62 Friend St, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
Dr Malcolm Doidge presents his 360-degree time-lapse photography project, captured in Futuna Chapel across the 2023–2024 equinoxes and solstices. A short film of the project will be screened, followed by insights into the digital processes behind its creation.

About the speaker:

After completing his studies at the University of Canterbury School of Fine Art in 1984, Malcolm Doidge worked for the New Zealand Correspondence School as an illustrator. He received his first commission from Lincoln College (now University), producing the work 'Ascent' in 1984.

In more recent years Doidge has taught Creative Technologies at Weltec (Wellington) and completed a Doctor of Philosophy, Inside Arcadia: An immersive virtual phantasmagoria. His degree was conferred by Massey University, Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, in 2022.

His work has been recognised by several awards including the Wallace Art Award (2004, 2006, 2009, 2013 and 2016), the Visa Gold Art Award (1998) and he was the premier award winner in the NCC Art Award in 2002.
