events.id: Barry Barclay Retrospective-The Circus Cinema, Bar and Cafe, 34 Jellicoe St, Martinborough-Event Finder
events.name: Barry Barclay Retrospective
events.venue: The Circus Cinema, Bar and Cafe, 34 Jellicoe St, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Barry Barclay Retrospective

Wairarapa (1968) + Barry Barclay: The Camera on the Shore (2009). Presented as part of Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival's Spring Sessions 2026, this special retrospective celebrates the work and legacy of groundbreaking Aotearoa filmmaker Barry Barclay (Ngāti Apa). Bringing together two films connected to Barclay's significant contribution to cinema, this screening offers audiences an opportunity to discover his work and see a newly preserved piece of Wairarapa's film history on the big screen.

Wairarapa (1968)

Camera: Barry Barclay
Promotional film | 22 minutes
Made for the Wairarapa Development Council for distribution throughout the world, Wairarapa is a promotional film showcasing the natural beauty, outdoor activities and rural life of the region. From mountain landscapes and wildlife to farming and local events, the film captures a fascinating portrait of Wairarapa in 1968. Newly preserved by Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision, this screening offers a rare opportunity to experience the film on the big screen and revisit a remarkable piece of our region's cinematic heritage.

Barry Barclay: The Camera on the Shore (2009)
Director: Graeme Tuckett
Documentary | 1 hour 42 minutes
A career-spanning documentary exploring the life and work of groundbreaking Aotearoa filmmaker Barry Barclay. Structured around an interview with Barclay shortly before his death in 2008, the documentary offers an insight into his filmmaking career, creative vision and enduring contribution to Indigenous cinema. Together, these two films provide an opportunity to celebrate Barry Barclay's legacy and reflect on the importance of preserving and sharing Aotearoa's film heritage.

Screening Details
Sunday 8 November 2026 | 3pm
Circus Cinema, Martinborough
Tickets: Book directly through Circus Cinema. Click the Book Tickets link to go to their online booking form, or phone 06 306 9442. Book here: https://www.circus.net.nz/book-film

Acknowledgements
Special thanks to the Masterton Creative Communities Scheme for funding the restoration of Wairarapa (1968), and to the film preservation team at Ngā Taonga Sound & Vision for their work in preserving our cinematic heritage. We also mihi to Barry Barclay's whānau for their blessing and support for this screening. We gratefully acknowledge the Martinborough Community Board for its support of this screening at Circus Cinema, Martinborough.

Presented by Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival as part of Spring Sessions 2026. See the films, meet the filmmakers.

events.long_description:
Korimako Trio
Helene Pohl, violin; Rolf Gjelsten, cello; Michael Endres, piano

The concert opens with Zemlinsky's Trio in D Minor, a late 19th century example of Viennese Romanticism, lyrical, dense and emotionally expressive. This is followed by Janacek’s Violin Sonata (for violin and piano) deeply dramatic with folk elements. A return to Romanticism with Chopin’s Introduction and Polonaise Brillante in C major, for cello and piano follows and the concert concludes with Haydn’s Piano trio in A major (Hob.XV), bright and witty, with plenty of classical charm. A beautifully varied journey through four distinct musical eras, balancing full trio textures with virtuoso duo highlights.

events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

Oscar-nominee Saoirse Ronan delivers one of her most daring and memorable roles in the satirical thriller Bad Apples, a bold and timely film that challenges how deeply we hold our core beliefs.

Ronan plays Maria, a primary school teacher whose classroom is thrown into chaos by Danny, an exceptionally disruptive and foul-mouthed student.

Maria reaches her breaking point after Danny has a violent run-in with another student, and taking a drastic course of action, traps him in her home.

In Danny’s absence, the classroom begins to thrive; the children flourish academically, and both parents and school staff celebrate the incredible turnaround. But with everyone else convinced the school’s biggest problem has finally been solved, Maria now finds herself trapped in an increasingly preposterous moral dilemma.

Swedish-born director Jonatan Etzler injects scathing Scandi humour into this daring psychological comedy, which is sure to become one of the year’s most talked-about films.

events.long_description:
Emerging Waves is a space held by a 5Rhythms® Teacher in Training. In this 5Rhythms class, you are invited to move through the 5Rhythms with simple guidance, giving space for your personal expression. Music becomes the teacher alongside the Teacher in Training, supporting your movement practice through the Waves map of Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical and Stillness.

Rooted in the teachings of Gabrielle Roth, 5Rhythms® is practiced by tens of thousands of people around the world. It is a movement meditation, a creative path, and a philosophy grounded in the belief that when we move, we heal. Movement becomes both medicine and metaphor—opening space for personal insight, and embodied presence.

This practice welcomes every body, every culture, every age, and every level of experience. Wherever the 5Rhythms are danced, a community forms—one that moves together, sweats together, grows together, and supports one another’s freedom and authenticity. Here we meet ourselves and each other with curiosity, kindness, and the courage to be real.

Creativity. Connection. Community.

Sober environment – substance free

Bare feet or dance shoes only

Scent free space

events.name: Sunset Guided Tour
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.name: Ascent up Maunga Rangitūmau
events.venue: Te Rangi Lodge, 490 Bluff Rangitumau Rd, Masterton
events.long_description:
Ever wondered what that high hill is just north of Masterton with the aerials on it?
This is the impressive Rangitūmau Maunga - important in the story of Haunui-a-Nanaia, who long ago came this way after pursuing his runaway wife Wairaka down the west coast of Te Ika a Māui.

The group will meet and part at Te Rangi Lodge, and set off together up the hill.
The tramp is a steady, but not steep, uphill climb to the top where there are 360 degree views.

Local writer, researcher and storyteller Joe Potangaroa (Ngati Kahungunu, Rangitane, Tuhoe, English) will participate, and share his knowledge of tikanga, taiao and Wairarapa history linked to Maunga Rangitūmau.

The walk will take 2 - 2.5 hours and is suitable for fit walkers & trampers. The walk starts at 200m elevation and climbs to 604m elevation.
Please note access is through a working farm, please observe all health and safety instructions given on the day.

Koha accepted for the cuppa tea provided.

events.id: Mini Masterpieces - Enamels Short Course-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Mini Masterpieces - Enamels Short Course
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Love pattern, colour and beautiful little things? You don't need to be an artist to create your own miniature masterpiece.

Glass enamels have been used on metal for centuries to create tiny works of art — from portraits and religious icons to royal emblems and intricate decorative pieces. Now it's your turn to discover this wonderfully tactile process.

Over two three-hour sessions, expert tutor Sarah Brock will guide you through creating a miniature artwork on a pre-cut metal shape. You'll start by preparing your metal and building a beautiful enamel background, then choose from a selection of patterns to trace and decals to create your design. No drawing skills are required — Sarah will help you find a design you love and show you how to make it work beautifully on your piece.

From there, you'll build up layers of coloured transparent enamels, ceramic pencil details and special effects, firing your piece between layers in the kiln. With each firing, the colours and textures develop, creating depth, richness and that gorgeous glassy enamel finish.
Your finished piece could become a special piece of jewellery, a keepsake ornament, or a tiny artwork to display in your home.

Perfect for anyone who loves colour, pattern, illustration and design, whether you're completely new to enamelling or simply looking for a new creative medium to explore. Come with an idea, or come with absolutely no idea — Sarah will help you turn it into something beautiful.
All class materials supplied.
events.description:

events.long_description:
Through My Lens, I Bloom: A Journey of Resilience, Light and Quiet Beauty
For fifteen years, Margarita (Margaret) Yiannoutsos has lived with Parkinson’s. During this time, photography has become both a refuge and a way to express herself, finding moments of beauty, stillness and joy.

Through photographs of flowers and personal reflections, Margarita explores themes of resilience, change and perseverance.

“In that time, photography has become both refuge and expression, allowing me to slow down and truly see.”

The photography exhibition invites us to pause, appreciate the beauty in everyday moments, and reflect on the power of creativity through life's challenges.

events.name: Film screening and kōrero with Other Cinemas
events.venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Join us for a special free screening of I Carry It With Me Everywhere by Other Cinemas and The Neglected Miracle by Barry Barclay at Massey University, with kōrero from Arwa Aburawa, Turab Shah, and Hana Pera Aoake on Monday 9 November 6:15pm-9pm.

I Carry It With Me Everywhere was informed by interviews with first-generation migrants living in the UK. This short film weaves together the lives of multiple characters as they confront inherited ideas of belonging. The Neglected Miracle is a film that forms the culmination of five years of international research into the question of who owns our seeds. This involves interviews with corporations, scientists and everyday farmers in the developing world. This was shot over two years in eight different countries. 

We are very lucky to be joined by Turab Shah and Arwa Aburawa of Other Cinemas for a kōrero before the screening. They have come all the way from the UK, so don't miss this chance to hear about the film directly from its makers!

This screening is programmed in concert with the exhibition Unseen. Unheard. Unarchived. by Other Cinemas and Friends, curated by Hana Pera Aoake. The exhibition is on at Enjoy until 19 December.

Snacks and drinks provided!

The screening will be held at Massey Cinema, Old Dominion Museum Building (East entrance): 15 Buckle Street, Mount Cook, Wellington

(Block 10 Tokomaru, Pukeahu Mount Cook, Wellington)

This event is supported by Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, Massey University. Enjoy's Public Engagement programme is made possible by the support of Wellington City Council.

The Neglected Miracle

Film by Barry Barclay. Narrated by Keri Kaa. A Pacific films production. Film courtesy of Aotearoa New Zealand Film Heritage Trust – Te Puna Ataata (ANZFHT) and Ngā Taonga (NT). Festivals: 1985 Wellington Film Festival (World Premiere), 1985 London Film Festival, 2009 NZ International Film Festival, 2013 imagineNATIVE (Toronto).

Image: Other Cinemas (Arwa Aburawa and Turab Shah), I Carry It With Me Everywhere, 2022 (film still).

events.long_description:
Paint a Mo, save a bro, supporting Movember

Get creative for a good cause! This November, we’re getting behind Movember with a special Paintvine event in Wellington supporting men’s health.

Grab your girlfriends, your partner, your dad, your brother – or anyone who’s keen for a creative night out – and join us as we paint our very own moustachioed masterpiece. And to help get you into the painting spirit, your ticket includes one house beer or wine to enjoy while you create. Cheers!

Our Paintvine artist will guide you step by step from a blank canvas to your finished painting, so absolutely no art experience is needed.

And because it wouldn’t be Movember without a magnificent Mo, everyone will get a stick-on moustache to wear on the night!

Paintvine is a proud supporter of Movember, with proceeds from these events supporting their work in men’s mental health and suicide prevention, prostate cancer and testicular cancer.

There’ll also be an opportunity to make an additional donation to Movember on the night if you’d like to contribute even more.

Whether you’re a seasoned painter or haven’t picked up a paintbrush since school, come along, get creative and help us support the health and wellbeing of the men we know, love and couldn’t imagine life without.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.long_description:
Almost thirty years after the duo cut their teeth in the comedy clubs of Wellington, Flight of the Conchords are coming home. Fans can expect a career-spanning set. It will include hits from their Emmy-nominated HBO series and two critically acclaimed studio albums. 

After taking an eight-year break from performing, Bret McKenzie and Jemaine Clement burst back onto the live scene in 2026. They played two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre. That followed five intimate warm-up shows at Wellington’s Meow Nui. While they put the Conchords on ice for a few years, the pair both remained busy. Bret won an Academy Award for Best Original Song for ‘Man or Muppet’, wrote songs for ‘The Simpsons’ and‘The Minecraft Movie’, and released two solo albums. Jemaine has focused on the screen, creating comedy horror TV shows ‘Wellington Paranormal’ and ‘What We Do In The Shadows’. He’s also appeared in films including the last two ‘Avatar’ instalments. 

Don’t just think about it, get your tickets before they’re gone.

Overview

Presentation & korero to equip youth workers with skills to support rangatahi with addictive traits in a culturally safe & responsive way

Explore how the teenage brain is wired for addictive behaviours, including cellphones, vaping, smoking and other substances. Learn to recognise early warning signs, respond effectively, and gain practical strategies to help young people build healthier habits and make positive choices.

The training is suitable for anyone who works with young people who would like greater knowledge and understanding, along with tools to support rangatahi overcome addictive traits in a safe and culturally responsive way.

This training is presented by the Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective, delivered by the Collaborative Trust and made possible thanks to support from Department of Internal Affairs and Rata Foundation. Limited spaces available so get in quick to reserve your placeTickets on sale through Eventbrite.There is no charge to attend this training for Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective members.

Not a member? Sign up here and take advantage of our free training opportunities.




Meet the kaiako;


Dr/Dame Sue Bagshaw
Dame Sue calls herself a 'youth worker with a medical degree'. Incredibly knowledgeable on all things youth... she has been a champion for positive youth development throughout her life, with notable mentions being that she founded Te Tahi Youth (youth one-stop-shop), The Collaborative Trust, and The Youth Hub in Ōtautahi Christchurch.

Ollie Flett
Youth Tutor Ollie Flett works as a youth wellbeing practitioner at St Bedes College in Christchurch in their wellbeing team and is a whānau support worker. He has a psych degree, a post-grad cert in counselling and has lived experience with neurodiversity, substances, online culture, and harmful gaming/technology use.

events.name: Ngā Mokopuna Tour
events.venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.name: Larval Mask - Physical Theatre Workshops
events.venue: 3 Market Lane, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

the warmth of other people's creative energy

events.long_description:
Join us to launch Puke, a new book from essa may ranapiri. The book will be launched by Jasmine Sargent. Ruby Solly and Midden Rahurahu will read poetry in response to Puke.

Tuesday 10 November, 6pm
Unity Books Wellington
Free event – all welcome!

They first meet a million years ago, in the eruption of a volcano.

The second time, it’s in a liquor store: Hinenuitepo is buying a lighter for Mahuika; Hinemoana is picking up drinks.

Before long, they become entangled in rituals of mortality— love, hot chips, a carved bone strap-on, multiple evictions and a new puppy—all while holding down their duties as Death and the Sea.

But there is a great sickness rising in them both. The other atua have begun to disappear, and their world is slowly dying. Somewhere, an insidious power waits.

As the story shifts between our two lovers, Puke weaves a modern puuraakau of desire, decay and decolonisation.

events.long_description:
Getting Started in Standup - Wellington
Have you always wanted to try stand-up comedy but don’t know how to start?

Comedian and writer Neil Thornton brings you a fun, low-pressure comedy workshop.

Sign up here: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/enroll

Suggested koha: $20

Everything you need to know to get a mic in your face:
-generating ideas
-joke writing
-effective delivery
-where and how to get practice
-how to avoid many common mistakes new performers make.


------
This class is also an intro to our upcoming "Complete Course" in Wellington

Getting Started (open to all): Tuesday 10 November 6:00pm-9:00pm (Cavern Club)
Class 1: Tuesday 17 November 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 2: Tuesday 24 November 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 3: Tuesday 1 December 6:00pm-9:00pm
Class 4: Tuesday 8 December 6:00pm-9:00pm
Graduation Show: Friday 11 December 8:00pm (Fringe Bar)

Price $450+gst - Includes all classes and materials, two private writing/coaching sessions, and your graduation video.

More info: https://www.nzcomedyschool.com/



In addition to his career as a stand-up comedian, Neil Thornton has been teaching for more than 25 years. He earned his BA in English from Carnegie Mellon University and his MFA in writing from the University of New Orleans.

He published fiction and essays in several literary journals and magazines and taught college English for 9 years, running classes in Creative Writing, Composition, Creative Nonfiction, Technical Writing, and Managerial Communication.

After moving to New York City in 2007, Neil became a working stand-up comic, performing everywhere from major comedy clubs to seedy dive bars in Washington D.C., Provincetown, Fire Island, and the Poconos. More recently, what was supposed to be a six-month adventure in New Zealand has turned into a permanent home.

Since then, Neil has made a big impact on the New Zealand comedy circuit. He has toured up and down the country and all over the world, entertaining audiences with his battles of understanding Kiwi culture and finding his own identity. He's a regular at The Classic in Auckland, and appeared in the TV3 comedy special "After Hours."

Neil now teaches from Wellington, New Zealand, where he continues to write, perform standup, and raise two giant Alaskan Malamutes.

OFFICIAL SELECTION: Glasgow Film Festival -

One name. Two champions. BAFTA-nominated filmmaker Alex Holmes delivers the definitive portrait of how Damon Hill overcame the loss of his legendary father, Graham Hill, and followed in his footsteps to become a Formula 1 world champion himself.

Featuring exclusive interviews with Damon and his family, Hill is a gripping documentary that charts the racing legend’s journey through tragedy, pressure, and some of the most iconic moments in F1 history.

Discover the inside story of how Damon fought a furious battle with Michael Schumacher, and dealt with the death of his teammate Ayrton Senna, who tragically lost his life at 34.

Hill places an insightful focus on who Damon is as a person - his hopes, joys, insecurities, and heartbreak. This engaging approach creates an emotional narrative that captures the attention of both F1 devotees and the uninitiated alike.

With a seamless blend of high-octane Formula 1 footage and intimate home-movie moments, Hill is pacy, polished, and unmissable.

events.name: LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
events.venue: Newtown Community Centre - Te Whare Hapori o Ngā Puna Waiora,Wellington SCL Newtown, 74 Colombo St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
Calling all those who want to level up their Lindy! We have a special two week crash-course designed specifically for those who want to make the jump from beginner to intermediate (and those who want to brush up on their skills)!

Basically, if you're wanting to move up in your Lindy journey but not sure how to get there, these open-level workshops are for you!*

They’re also a great option for any intermediate dancers who want to build a solid foundation for 2027 and beyond, or for those who want to try switching leading/following!

Week 1 | Nov 10, 6:30pm-8:45pm: Swing-out deep-dive

Swing-outs are one of the fundamental moves that make Lindy-Hop, well, Lindy-Hop! They're awesome but can be tricky to master (journey not a destination!) In this 2h workshop we'll hone in on the craft and techniques that make swing-outs feel oh-so good, as well as introduce some fun styling and variations you can incorporate to make them your own!

Week 2 | Nov 17; 6.30pm-8:45pm: Improver essentials

Switching between the fundamental Lindy footwork can be a challenge! This 2h workshop is designed to build your confidence in moving between 6-count, 8-count and Charleston. On top of this, we'll be focusing on expanding your dance vocabulary so you can hit the social dance floor with style!

*For beginners who come to both workshops you’ll (pretty much) be ready to join intermediate classes in 2026! (Please still check in with the facilitators before committing to intermediate classes).

Venue:
Te Whare Hapori o ngā Puna Waiora | Newtown Community Centre.

Price:
$20/workshop. We want to make these workshops as affordable as possible so there's nothing stopping you reaching your Lindy goals!

**Please aim to arrive at least 10min before class starts so we can sign you in**

events.id: 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast-2 Harris Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast
events.venue: 2 Harris Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Mark 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership between Wellington and its sister city Seoul, with Korean and New Zealand business leaders, officials and organisations over a Korean-inspired breakfast.

Description:

The Embassy of the Republic of Korea, Wellington City Council and the Korea New Zealand Business Council (KNZBC) are pleased to invite you to the 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast.

Seoul is Wellington’s sister city, and this year marks 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership was established during an official mayoral visit, further strengthening the relationship between our two cities. The breakfast brings together Korean and New Zealand businesses, organisations and officials to explore the opportunities shaping the relationship between our two countries, from trade and investment to primary industries, infrastructure and the creative sector.

Held in Te Akapuanga o Waimānga, the Māori whare within the Wellington City Council building, the morning will open with a karakia and mihimihi. This is followed by remarks from Wellington City Council and the Korean Ambassador, a keynote address from Deer Industry New Zealand, and a panel discussion with business leaders sharing practical experiences of working with Korea, including Q&A.

Guests will enjoy a breakfast with a Korean twist alongside tea and coffee.

This is a great opportunity to connect with others who share an interest in the continued growth of the New Zealand–Korea relationship. We look forward to welcoming you.

Agenda

7:30am — Registration, networking, tea and coffee

7:45am — Mihi and welcome

Karakia and mihimihi, Wellington City Council

7:50am — Opening remarks

Wellington City Council

H.E. Byung-ha Chung, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to New Zealand

8:00am — Keynote address: New Zealand’s Deer Industry in Korea

Terry Meikle, Market Manager, Deer Industry New Zealand

8:15am — Panel discussion and Q&A: Business Partnership in Practice

David Sheppard, General Manager, Hyundai Rotem

John McKay, Managing Director, POW Studios

Further panellist to be announced

8:45am — Closing remarks

Gareth Coleman, Chair, Korea New Zealand Business Council

8:50am — Breakfast and networking

9:30am — Event ends

events.long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 2 workshop will equip leaders and managers with the skills to build high performing and motivated teams.

Learn how to make the transition from buddy to boss and lead a successful team. As John F. Kennedy once said, “leadership and learning are indispensable to each other”. Our Leadership & Management courses are designed to help you get the best performance from yourself and your team, providing you with the skills and techniques to become better than you ever perceived you could be.

The Leadership & Management Part 2 workshop will equip leaders and managers with the skills to build high performing and highly motivated teams; the skills to communicate effectively as a leader, become more self-aware, provide coaching and mentoring, deal with conflict in a constructive and productive manner along with developing ways to solve problems as a team.

This workshop also gives participants an understanding of the key concepts of leadership and leadership styles along with how to choose and implement a leadership style that is authentic and beneficial to both the organisation and the teams they serve.

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.long_description:
About This Course

Duration: 1 Full Day (8 Hours)

Delivery Mode: Classroom (In-Person)

Language: English

Credits: 8 PDUs / Training Hours

Certification: Course Completion Certificate

Refreshments: Lunch, snacks, and beverages will be provided


If you would like weekend training sessions, kindly reach out to us at info@mangates.com for availability and scheduling.


Course Overview


The Machine Learning & AI in Python course empowers you to understand, build, and evaluate predictive models using Python. You will learn the fundamentals of supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation metrics, feature engineering, and get a glimpse into neural networks and deep learning. With practical hands-on exercises, this course prepares you to transition from theory to real-world machine learning applications.


Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, you will:

Understand core machine learning concepts and workflows

Build supervised and unsupervised models using scikit-learn

Evaluate model performance using appropriate metrics

Apply feature engineering techniques to improve predictions

Gain basic knowledge of neural networks and deep learning

Use Python for real-world AI and ML problem-solving

Target Audience

Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

Build culture by design, not by default - one ritual at a time.

Facilitate meaningful culture change and create connection through the power of workplace rituals.

This masterclass is for people who want to build stronger, more connected workplace cultures — and are ready to turn values and intentions into real, daily action.

Whether you're a leader, culture champion, facilitator, or change consultant, this training will give you the tools and confidence to run your own Workplace Rituals Workshops using the WRD (Workplace Rituals Deck).

In this Masterclass, you'll learn:

What rituals are and why they are important

Why rituals matter in workplaces

The difference between habits and rituals

In depth knowledge of each of the 4 parts of the deck and why they are important

Tips and tricks for using the deck first hand, along with the story and background behind the deck.

events.id: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp-Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Duntulm Farm hilltop circuit tramp
events.venue: Duntulm Farm, 820 Mangatarere Valley Road, West Taratahi, Carterton
events.long_description:
Explore the regenerating and mature bush on Duntulm Carbon Farm, with some of the tramp exploring the adjacent Tararua Forest Park. Mostly on single footpaths and some on farm tracks.
We should see mature rata, kahikatea, totara, rimu, miro, native clematis, possibly mistletoe and various orchids.
There will be extensive views both over the Wairarapa Plains and up to Taratahi/Mt Holdsworth.
The walk will cross the new bridge, go through a shallow crossing of Kiddie Creek, up into the "dress circle" near point 637, along to Holdsworth lookout, down to Duntulm Cottage for a cuppa, followed by a flattish walk out on farm tracks or an optional extra tramp up to pt 533 and down a different track back to the bridge.
Although there have been walks on Duntulm Farm most Wairarapa Walking Festivals, this is a different and fairly challenging route. We will take it reasonably slowly!

Terrain notes: steep hills, stream crossings, scrambly paths through the bush.
Have you comepleted a half-day tramp in the last 6 months?
Once registered, you will sent details on what to bring, suggested clothing, food, water and will need to supply an emergency contact person.

events.long_description:
Hickety Pips & Others - Aspects of Military Matters in Colonial Wellington 1845-1860

This tour covers a wide range of aspects of military service of early settlers, of soldiers serving in Wellington, and of their wives and children, and the contributions those with military experience made to the development of the city, to society and to economic development.

It traverses the lower part of the cemetery, includes some of the earliest burials, and is easy walking (not suitable for those with mobility issues).

Tour duration 1.5 hours, starting and ending at the Bolton Street Cemetery Museum, lower Bolton Street.

Cost $10 per person, children under 12 free, and good dogs on leads always welcome.

events.id: Wellington - Member Spotlight-Level 9/20 Ballance Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Wellington - Member Spotlight
events.venue: Level 9/20 Ballance Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
We’re bringing our Wellington community together for a relaxed evening of conversation and connection. This is less about formal presentations and more about meeting others in the HealthTech community, sharing experiences and learning from one another.

As part of this catchup, two of our members will share their career journeys, the different pathways that brought them into digital health and some of the lessons they have learned as women working in the industry. Come along for a drink, an open conversation and the opportunity to connect with people who understand the opportunities and challenges of working in HealthTech.

What to expect

5.00 pm-5.30 pm: Arrive, grab a wine and meet others from the Wellington HealthTech community

5.30 pm-6.30 pm: An informal member spotlight and conversation with Catherine Epps and Jennifer Anderson

Meet our speakers

Catherine Epps is Director, Medical Devices at Pharmac, a role she has held since 2023. The range of medical devices used across the public health system is vast, with technology playing an increasingly important role in how many of these devices function. Catherine has more than 20 years’ experience in senior leadership roles across public and private healthcare organisations in Aotearoa, including serving as Executive Director Allied Health, Scientific and Technical at Capital & Coast District Health Board. She later led a broad portfolio at WorkSafe focused on reducing work-related health harm, including carcinogens, mentally healthy work and musculoskeletal harm.

Originally trained as a speech-language therapist, Catherine is a Fellow of the Australasian College of Health Service Managers and a Chartered Director. She is currently Board Chair of Stroke Aotearoa New Zealand.

Jennifer Anderson works in biotech commercialisation, with a focus on technologies that improve human health. Her career spans New Zealand’s public and private sectors, including roles in technology transfer offices, early-stage investment firms and start-up companies. This experience has given her a practical understanding of what it takes to move science from the laboratory to the market, from intellectual property management and financing to building the right team. Jennifer is currently Business Development and Commercialisation Manager at the Malaghan Institute of Medical Research, where she helps identify promising innovations and supports their translation into the clinic.

Whether you’re well established in HealthTech, exploring a new direction or simply keen to meet others in the community, we’d love you to join us.

*Please note: if you arrive and the building doors are locked please call Nuala on 027 244 9692

events.long_description:
Overview

Songs of Solidarity (SoS), in collaboration with our whānau, Hafsar Tameesuddin invite you to the screening of Wandering, a Rohingya Story.

About the film

The documentary film Wandering, a Rohingya Story is an immersive, poetic and powerful look into the biggest refugee camp in the world, the Kutupalong refugee camp. In 2017, within a few months, 700,000 people of the Rohingya Muslim minority fled Myanmar (formerly Burma) to escape genocide and seek asylum in Bangladesh. Between poetry and nightmares, food distribution and soccer games, the Rohingyas of Kutupalong camp bear witness to their daily lives and to the ghosts of the past.

The film will be introduced by our Rohingya whānau, with a brief about her work with Rohingya communities, and ways to be part of the solidarity movement. Koha from this screening will go to a collective selected by our whānau.

THIS IS A FUND RAISING SCREENING! PLEASE BUY TICKETS!

events.long_description:

Indian cooking expert, Manjula Patel, has assembled a range of vegan Indian dishes for you to learn and enjoy making and eating. In this practical cooking course, you’ll observe dishes being made by Manjula and then work in pairs to create most of these dishes yourselves.
Please note this is a practical cooking class that will not cover vegan philosophy.  Not suitable for people allergic to nuts.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Discuss the flavours and spices used in Indian cuisine
• Know where to purchase ingredients for a selection of vegan dishes and finger food
• Read and follow a range of recipes step-by-step
• Create some classic dishes to try again at home
All ingredients included in course fee. Bring an apron, dishcloth, and a couple of tea towels and containers to take any leftovers home.
Note:  Our cooking courses are designed to provide a collaborative and immersive learning experience where learners often work in pairs and/or groups. While we wish to create an inclusive environment for all participants, it is important to note that our courses are unable to accommodate specific food allergies or deviate from the preplanned dishes and menus.

events.name: Wednesday Lost Wax Casting - 6 Weeks Course
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
A fantastic course that's full of fun and inspiration!

It starts on Wed 11 November and runs for 6 weeks till Wed 16 December, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Create interesting designs in wax, then send them off to be professionally cast in metal. Once your pieces are back, you will be taught how to cut, file and shape them into wearable pieces.

Level 1 students: Learn to work in both soft and hard jewellers' wax and send your waxes away to be cast. When they return, you will learn how to clean them up into finished jewellery and/or incorporate them into jewellery in multiple ways. We start with rings, but encourage students to think outside the box!

Level 2 students: Advance your carving skills and learn to set stones in your waxes. This can be done either by creating claws and other settings or trying the cast-in-place technique - an organic, exciting process.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs, which vary from student to student depending on what they want to make. Small castings can cost around $7 - $10, and metals are between $0.35 per gram for bronze - $4 per gram for silver. Please see details on our Regular Classes page.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, PayPal or Afterpay on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

events.id: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon-Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: From Plate to Page: An Evening with Peter Gordon
events.venue: Samuel Marsden Collegiate School, 35 Marsden Avenue, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
Peter Gordon is a chef, restaurateur, writer and fusion pioneer whose eclectic cuisine has had global reach. Join us at this special fundraising event for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden to hear about the books, travel, people and experiences that have shaped his life.

For forty years Peter has gathered ingredients, textures and techniques from around the world and brought them to diners at his award-winning restaurants such as The Sugar Club and The Providores, and into homes through his eight cookbooks. He has cooked for world leaders including Queen Elizabeth II and Barack Obama, presented shows for the Discovery Channel and Whakaata Māori (Māori Television), and appeared on the shows of Nigel Slater and Jamie Oliver in the UK and as a guest judge on MasterChef NZ. He is also the founder of the hugely successful UK charity event Who’s Cooking Dinner? and its NZ equivalent Dining for a Difference.

The evening will begin with a glass of Hunter’s Wines’ award-winning MiruMiru™ and delicious canapés in the foyer (a non-alcoholic option will also be available). We will then move into the auditorium for a conversation with Peter hosted by Katherine Mansfield House & Garden Director Cherie Jacobson.

This event is being held to raise funds for our Category 1 Historic Place and writer’s museum in Thorndon, which is open six days a week. We offer an annual programme of events and activities designed to encourage creativity and we host school and tour groups to share the life, literature and legacy of Katherine Mansfield.

events.id: Pukaha After Dark-Pukaha Mount Bruce National Wildlife Centre, 85379 State Highway 2, Mount Bruce, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Pukaha After Dark
events.venue: Pukaha Mount Bruce National Wildlife Centre, 85379 State Highway 2, Mount Bruce, Masterton
events.long_description:
As evening settles over the forest, head out along Pūkaha’s Loop Track, normally only accessible during the day, and make your way to the top of the reserve.
Along the way, experience the changing sights and sounds of the ngahere as daylight fades and the forest comes alive at night.

At the top, pause to enjoy a warming kawakawa tea and light snack before beginning the return journey under the night sky.
The experience will also include a short presentation exploring Pūkaha, our connection to the ngahere and the importance of protecting our dark skies.

This is a unique opportunity to experience a different side of Pūkaha and see what happens when the daytime visitors have gone home.

events.name: Paint and Wine Night - Summer Sloth (First Drink Included)
events.venue: Hey Coastie, Wellington, 42 Tutere Street, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Looking for a creative night out in Waikanae Beach? Join us for a fun beginner-friendly adults painting class in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. It’s the perfect excuse to switch off, get creative, and try something a little different.

Whether you’re coming along solo, planning a date night, or organising a catch-up with friends, Paintvine is all about good vibes, creativity, and having fun while you paint – you might even surprise yourself with what you can create!

Drinks: FIRST DRINK IS INCLUDED IN THE TICKET PRICE

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit! Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.name: Dungeons & Flagons - A November Night
events.venue: 31 Whitehouse Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Every great Dungeons and Dragons adventure begins in a tavern.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s own Beer Engine is for you.

Turn up solo or with friends and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and just enough danger to make the beer taste sweeter. Because while you’re swinging swords and slinging spells, the bar will be open with Beer Engine’s excellent selection of craft brews on tap.

No prep. No pressure. Just great beer and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards.

New for November!

We've added a Daggerheart table. This is your chance to try your hand at Critical Role's new RPG - Daggerheart. Same fantasy vibes as D&D but different mechanics, new classes and species to play. Daggerheart seats are strictly limited so you'll need to jump in fast.

Dungeons and Flagons can sell out in a week - so book fast, adventurer!

This is an age 18+ event.

events.name: ADONEYE, THE WATCHERS, STUDIO 4
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Looking for something to do on your Wednesday?

November 11th we've got Adoneye, The Watchers (AUS) and Studio 4 to get you pumped for the weekend to come!

Adoneye hails from the tightly knit music circles of Wellington, New Zealand. Inspired by the raw emotion of grunge rock, like “Soundgarden” and “A Perfect Circle” and the crafted songwriter style of “Elliot Smith. They write with clarity and honesty. Relating an interplay of bittersweet truths and liberating mental alchemy, in an attempt to make sense of the human condition. Emphatically emotive and professionally executed, yet retaining a uniquely human disposition.

The Watchers are a high energy, alternative rock band Kaurna, Adelaide South Australia, known for their loud riffs and signature clownery. They have been drawing crowds with their electric stage presence and their head-banging originals inspired by the legends of rock n roll. Their third single set to be released in November, The Watchers are coming across from Australia to celebrate the release.

Studio 4 are a four piece band from Upper Hutt who love making music together with a variety of influences such as classic rock, indie and jazz. This raw high voltage fusion is a group you'l remember!

We hope to see you all there, this gig is pay what you can!!

Tickets here

Overview

Unlock the power of word-of-mouth marketing and get hundreds of quality referrals flowing into your business

Bx - Business Networking Reimagined is a fun, social, dynamic and productive networking event, designed to help your business grow through referrals and business opportunities.

There are over 1000 networking meetings held annually across Australia and NewZealand, plus online. As a member, you can attend ANY and as MANY as you like!

Bx is a Linked Up Business Network where you can connect with hundreds of people, both in the room AND outside the room.

We are the FASTEST GROWING business networking community in Australia, both face-to-face AND online.

We help you GET RESULTS in your networking. There are no minimum requirements or performance measures. Everyone just wants to help!

Meetings are relaxed and friendly, there's structure to maximise networking...but not all the rules! 80% of the meeting is spent getting to know other business owners.

At every meeting we have an à la carte breakfast and barista coffee

We aim to create a relaxed, enjoyable atmosphere for you to get to know - and build strong working relationships with other professionals in order for you to grow your revenue.

We believe that the best way to produce loyal, repeat business is through word of mouth. After all, it's WHO you know, not WHAT you know!

At the end of the day we understand MONEY TALKS and have a money back guarantee on ROI from your time and investment into Bx - Business Networking Reimagined.

8.00am - 8.25am - Open Networking

8.25am - 9.05am - 40 Second Business Introductions

events.venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBD,Level 5, 111 The Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

events.long_description:
Well Ahead: Put your health on the agenda

An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.

Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.

Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.




Click here to find out more.



“Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy

Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

About Conquer Health

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.

events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a hands-on Grass to Garden Workshop where we'll explore the practical skills and ideas you need to transform your patch of lawn or pasture into a thriving, productive garden space.

Through a mix of kōrero and hands-on learning, we'll dive into different approaches to garden establishment — from no-dig methods and sheet mulching to cultivation and soil preparation. You'll discover how to build healthy soil, manage weeds, make good use of organic materials, and create fertile growing spaces that work with nature.

Learn accessible, low-cost techniques you can take home and apply straight away, whether you're starting your first vegetable bed or expanding what you've already got going.

We will begin at Thu 12th November | 4:00pm at 108 Whitemans Valley Road (Garden).

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

Life and health insurance: rethinking the model

Customer expectations, product design, underwriting, claims and advice are all moving faster than traditional operating models can keep up with. At the same time, insurers are rethinking traditional products to meet the evolving needs of more New Zealanders, regulatory reform and a tough economic climate. That pressure is pushing insurers to rethink how they're built and to find new ways to support customers in sustainable ways.

Join the InsurTech community in Wellington on 12th November to hear how life and health insurers are innovating.

Then a panel of insurance and insurtech leaders will look at the big issues and trends shaping the sector into 2027. They'll cover how AI is being used in practice today, the opportunities Open Data could open up, and what makes partnerships between insurers and insurtechs work. Hear from Asteron Life, Deloitte, Life Direct, Monvia, Partners Life and Simfuni.

Register now to attend this event and connect with insurance and data professionals. Generously supported by Deloitte and Asteron Life.

Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

events.id: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War-National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Son of Satan or prophet of peace? Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga War
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
In his 1986 book 'The New Zealand Wars and the Victorian interpretation of racial conflict', James Belich noted that the nineteenth-century Bay of Plenty religious and military leader Hakaraia Mahika deserves more attention from historians.

Forty years later, Mark Derby’s forthcoming book 'Warrior Prophet – Hakaraia Mahika and the Tauranga Wars' proposes to provide that attention, along with an interpretive account of the New Zealand Wars in the Bay of Plenty, in which Hakaraia played a prominent and dramatic role.

Mahika was a key figure in the 1864 battle of Gate Pā, regarded by Belich as “arguably the most important battle of the New Zealand Wars.” He became a close and respected associate of Wiremu Tāmihana, Rewi Maniapoto and Te Kooti. Yet, today he is barely remembered outside his own tribal area of Waitaha-Tapuika, near Te Puke.

events.long_description:
‘He Has His Father’s Eyes’: Horror films and Cornelia Parker
Horror has long flickered at the edges of Cornelia Parker’s practice. This talk traces the network of horror references running through this exhibition, exploring how Parker mobilises classics Psycho and Rosemary’s Baby as found cultural objects—laden with symbolic charge, collective memory and anxieties that continue to haunt the present.

Speakers Aaron Lister (Head Curator Art, City Gallery Wellington, and co-curator of Cornelia Parker) and Chelsea Nichols (Senior Curator, The Dowse Art Museum) collaborate as Curator of Screams—an unholy entity dedicated to the twisted entanglements of contemporary art and horror cinema.

The talk will be followed by a screening of Rosemary’s Baby. Wear your best baby blue dress.

events.id: BWB Talk: Claire Charters in conversation with Carwyn Jones-57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: BWB Talk: Claire Charters in conversation with Carwyn Jones
events.venue: 57 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Please join us for a BWB Talk with Claire Charters (Ngāti Whakaue, Tainui, Tūwharetoa, Ngāpuhi), author of Sovereignty: The Case for Constitutional Transformation.

In her new BWB Text, legal scholar Claire Charters says the idea that New Zealand’s constitution protects the rights of everyone is a fairytale.

The Crown’s claim to sovereignty, she argues, met none of the legal tests that applied in 1840 under tikanga Māori, British law or international law. An illegal claim has produced an illegitimate state, and a constitution in which Parliament, the executive and the courts can each override Māori rights. Sovereignty makes the case for constitutional transformation, and sets out what it could look like.

Charters will be joined in conversation by Carwyn Jones (Ngāti Kahungunu), legal academic and author of Matangi Rau: The Enduring Potential of Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

When: Thursday 12 November, 7pm (doors open 6.30pm)

Where: Unity Books Wellington, 57 Willis St, Wellington Central

Speakers: Claire Charters and Carwyn Jones

Free event. No RSVP needed, but if you're planning to come we'd love to know – it helps us manage numbers. Please click RSVP to register your interest.

Promoted in collaboration with Te Tākupu, publishers of Matangi Rau.

events.name: Capital Blues Presents: BlueBerries
events.venue: 21 Blair Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
One of the great pleasures of Wellington's music scene is stumbling across exceptional talent when you least expect it. Earlier this year, a young group of musicians caught our attention while busking on Cuba Street. Their musicianship, energy and obvious enjoyment of playing together made an immediate impression.

A few months later, that chance encounter has become a Capital Blues debut performance.

For these emerging musicians, the journey has involved building a full-length set, refining their repertoire, and preparing for their first performance before a dedicated audience. It's exactly the kind of opportunity Capital Blues seeks to create; giving young artists a platform to grow their confidence, develop their craft, and connect with new listeners.

Join us in supporting what may well be the next generation of outstanding Wellington musicians. You might just discover your new favourite band before everyone else does.

Featuring:

Maddie Glossop - vocals

Noah Bryn - guitar

Oliver Livingstone - double bass

Reuben Stevens - drums

Georgina Willan - alto saxophone

Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

events.long_description:
Techno Echo: Fox Moss
Techno Echo is a meet-up for women and gender minorities to learn and share about audio and visual practices and technology. Featuring special micro performances and demonstrations by local artists/musicians followed by time for kōrero and connection.

Our guest artist Fox Moss is the solo musical project of Te Whanganui-a-Tara based multidisciplinary musician and artist Niamh Woollin. Fox Moss released her debut album: Eternal Veil in September 2026. The album explores ambient and dungeon synth genres, with an overarching narrative structuring the album. Fox Moss creates and performs using Ableton, conjuring her immersive experiences through layering electronic sounds and textures. Niamh creates all the visual elements to accompany her music.

Introduced to Wellington’s music scene through their band Maiden Name in 2023, Niamh began making music under Fox Moss in 2024 after releasing her first single In Between. Fox Moss first performed at 13 Garrett Street for Attic Sessions #001 in April 2025. She released her second single, A Thousand White Horses soon after. In early 2026 Niamh performed at POWER2PONEKE and TONIC002: Insula x Niph.

Koha entry
Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

events.name: Powell Hut Overnight Tramp
events.venue: Tararua Forest Park, Mt. Holdsworth Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Join the Wairarapa Walking Festival on this classic and epic tramp to Powell Hut.

The first day: we will walk from Mt Holdsworth car park up to Powell Hut. This is 5 to 6 hours of uphill tramping, with good tracks and steps. The hut is at the edge of the bush-line with glorious views (and cell phone access).

Powell Hut has (gas) stoves, a wood-burner and bunks with mattresses. There are long-drop toilets and a water tank collecting water from the roof.

The Wairarapa Walking Festival team have booked 20 bunks for this great adventure.

Bring water for the tramp, snacks (muesli bars, dried fruit, nuts, chocolate etc), picnic lunch for both days, dinner and breakfast, plus hot chocolate, tea or coffee. Also, basic toiletries, hut shoes, nightwear, sleeping bags and recommend earplugs.

The second day: depending on the group and the weather we will either return the same way of go onto the alpine tops, look at the alpine flowers and comeback down East Holdsworth track. We should be back at the car park by 3 or 4pm.

Essential to have tramping boots or solid walking shoes, wind and rainproof jackets and merino or fleece layers. A change of clothes to wear in the hut in case you get wet on the walk. Walking poles recommended if you have them.

D.O.C labels this walk an 'intermediate tramping track'. The car park is at 320m elevation and Powell Hut is at 1200m elevation.

Please note - once registered, you will be asked to provide Emergency Contact details of a friend / relative and whether you have been tramping in the last 6 months. The Walk coordinator for WWF will carry a PLB. There is good cell phone coverage from the Hut.

Ticket costs are only to cover bunk costs at hut. Tickets will go off-sale 2 days prior to enable logistics, check the weather for the trip.

Youth between ages of 12 - 16 require an accompanying adult to attend also.

Celia recommends downloading the free iNaturalist app before you go.

Overview

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

Read less

events.venue: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Every organisation holds stories that can build trust, support and momentum. But how do you find the stories already present in your mahi and use them with intent, both inside your organisation and out in the community?

In our final workshop of the year, brand strategist Heather Horswell will unpack what a storytelling strategy means in practice, what makes a story work, and the four kinds of stories most organisations already have.

You'll leave with prompts to use with your own team, whether you’re writing a funding application or welcoming a new volunteer. 

This session will suit volunteers, communications staff, managers, senior leaders, and board members of not-for-profits and charities. No prior storytelling or marketing knowledge is needed. 

What You’ll Learn

We'll be exploring:

Brand strategy – what is it?

What makes an effective story and why

Finding stories to tell

Telling stories within and outside your organisation

Take-home prompts to use with your team

Our presenter: Heather Horswell

Heather is the founder of Verrative, a brand strategy consultancy. She helps leaders strategically develop their brand identity, enabling organisations to market themselves authentically and consistently, rather than wasting resources on individual campaigns and approaches.

Originally from Luxembourg, her background spans documentary filmmaking, video production, marketing management and science communication. Heather previously ran a film production company for 10 years and holds a Media Studies degree from Queen Margaret University, Edinburgh.

RSVPs essential - so sign up today!

Koha gratefully received to help cover event costs.

Extra information

For out of towners or those who can’t make it on the day, this workshop will be recorded and shared on our website after the event.

This is a free Community Comms Collective workshop for not-for-profits and collective volunteers, hosted by Volunteer Wellington. We are grateful for their support and for our speaker for giving her time and talent pro bono.

Y Central is an accessible venue – please contact the office with any queries.

events.long_description:
Leading edge project management and leadership for engineers
An engaging session to hear about how engineering projects are being run in the USA, from the viewpoint of a 6th generation Kiwi who is helping lead the industry in that country.

Join us in Wellington or online for a short overview of leading-edge behaviours that result in increased profit, higher client satisfaction, and more sustainable growth presented by Warren Ladbrook.

Warren introduces himself as a reformed engineer. Warren has purposefully built broad experience in business cases, planning, surveying, engineering, construction, project delivery, program management, and business operations.

He has ~40 years of international industry experience in a progressive range of different roles, including work within New Zealand, the United States, and further abroad. He presently serves as Senior Director of Project Management at WithersRavenel, a growing consultancy firm based in North Carolina.

He also serves as an instructor for PSMJ, teaching Project Management to Architects and Engineers across the USA, and also Coaching & Leadership within our industry. Further, he still does targeted consulting work for certain New Zealand clients. Warren is a Chartered Professional Engineer in New Zealand, a Fellow of Engineering NZ, and he is also a Professional Engineer in six US states. He holds his PMP, and has numerous other qualifications.

events.name: This Is Grief: On the Road
events.venue: Unity Books, 57 Willis St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.
This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

events.name: "Sitting Pretty" at Ata Rangi
events.venue: Ata Rangi Winery, 14 Puruatanga Rd, Martinborough
events.long_description:
Remember the original Toast Martinborough? Multiple vineyard visits, beautiful wines, and those long, progressive lunches that became part of the tradition? At Ata Rangi, we’re bringing a little of that magic back for one special evening.

Join us for Sitting Pretty - a sunset session celebrating Ata Rangi’s place in the old Toast Martinborough story, when our site was a stop on the festival circuit and Ruth Pretty’s much-loved food was part of the experience.

In collaboration with Rose & Smith, we’re revisiting some favourite dishes from Ruth Pretty’s menus of years gone by. Think whitebait fritters, asparagus with hollandaise, long-stemmed chocolate dipped strawberries, white crockery, linen napkins, cutlery, and the pleasure of taking your time over good food and a glass or two of Ata Rangi wine. It’s a nod to the familiar flavours and fond memories of yesteryear, and a good reason to make a few new ones.

Settle in amongst the vines, as the afternoon gives way to evening, with a relaxed yet festive atmosphere. Enjoy Ata Rangi wines, delicious food, great company and live music from Pat For President.

Whether you’re joining us to revisit a piece of the Toast Martinborough of old, or simply looking for a fun way to kick start the weekend ahead of Toast Martinborough (at The Runholder the following day), Sitting Pretty is an invitation to relax, raise a glass and celebrate where it all began.

Friday 13 November 2026
4pm–8pm
Ata Rangi, 14 Puruatanga Road, Martinborough

No tickets required, simply pay on consumption for food and beverages
