events.name: BIMinNZ Wellington - Project Spotlight - Air NZ Hangar 4
events.venue:
Tonkin + Taylor
Wellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Join us in Wellington to hear from the design and construction teams that brought this innovative project to life.

Join us on 17 November at Tonkin + Taylor for our final BIMinNZ Wellington event of 2026, as we explore the technology, innovation and collaboration behind Air New Zealand's remarkable new Hangar 4 project.

Designed by Studio Pacific Architecture and constructed by NZ Strong, Hangar 4 is the Southern Hemisphere's largest single span timber aircraft hangar. This impressive 15,000m² facility features a 98 metre clear span, enormous prefabricated timber trusses weighing 38 tonnes each, and an innovative approach to sustainable construction that sets a new benchmark for aviation infrastructure.

We'll be joined by Patrick Thompson from Studio Pacific Architecture and Jimmy Corric from NZ Strong, who will take us behind the scenes of this extraordinary project, exploring the digital tools, innovative construction methodologies and collaborative processes that helped bring it to life.

From complex design coordination and prefabrication to the challenges of construction within an operational airport environment, this session promises valuable insights into how technology and innovation are helping deliver some of New Zealand's most ambitious projects.

Come along to connect with Wellington's digital built environment community, hear from the people behind this impressive project, and celebrate another fantastic year of BIMinNZ events!

events.long_description:
We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

Cut through modern noise with Sivananda. Explore practical philosophy to tame distractions, strengthen focus, and find inner stability.

Master Your Attention: Practical philosophy to cut through modern noise

events.long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Looking for a unique night out in Wellington? Join us for a beginner-friendly watercolour painting event where you’ll explore fluid colour mixing, delicate brushwork, and create your own watercolour artwork … in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step through the watercolour process, so absolutely no art experience is needed. You’ll be encouraged to add your own personal touch along the way, making each painting uniquely yours. It’s the perfect excuse to try something new, switch off, and enjoy a relaxed night of creativity and good vibes.

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality watercolour paper, watercolour paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a watercolour painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.long_description:
Overview

Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths
The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.

Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.

What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams




Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.

What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context
Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.

What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps




Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion
Real public sector examples
Practical leadership tools and frameworks
Small-group exercises and peer learning
Application to participants' own workplace contexts

Participants are encouraged to bring current challenges and opportunities from their own organisations.

Why This Programme Is Different

Many AI learning programmes focus purely on technology and software tools. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change focuses on the leadership challenge.

Successful adoption of new technologies depends on people. This programme equips leaders with practical approaches for helping teams adapt, engage, learn, and perform during periods of transformation.

About the Facilitators

Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

This programme combines deep expertise in change leadership and AI transformation. Cat Moody and Jarred Griffiths bring practical experience supporting public sector organisations through organisational change, workforce transitions, leadership development, and AI adoption.

Participants will benefit from real examples, lessons learned, and practical insights drawn from current, hands-on work across public sector agencies.

Jesus Christ Superstar explores the biblical events leading to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire.
The 1970s rock score features lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber. Well-known numbers include I Don’t Know How to Love Him, Gethsemane, and Superstar.

events.long_description:
Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change (November)
Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

About this Event


Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.


Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.


What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams





Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.


What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context

Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.


What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps





Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion
Real public sector examples
Practical leadership tools and frameworks
Small-group exercises and peer learning
Application to participants' own workplace contexts

Participants are encouraged to bring current challenges and opportunities from their own organisations.


Why This Programme Is Different

Many AI learning programmes focus purely on technology and software tools. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change focuses on the leadership challenge.

Successful adoption of new technologies depends on people. This programme equips leaders with practical approaches for helping teams adapt, engage, learn, and perform during periods of transformation.


About the Facilitators

Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

This programme combines deep expertise in change leadership and AI transformation. Cat Moody and Jarred Griffiths bring practical experience supporting public sector organisations through organisational change, workforce transitions, leadership development, and AI adoption.

Participants will benefit from real examples, lessons learned, and practical insights drawn from current, hands-on work across public sector agencies.

events.long_description:
[FREE] Michael Volkerling Memorial Lecture: Artificial Intelligence, Memory and Culture
Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies are already embedded in the communication of culture – they shape and touch on all aspects of culture. In the face of this, an intense debate is currently taking place in museums around the world: are AI technologies to be embraced and trusted or should they be approached with suspicion and resisted?

This lecture attempts to unpick this dilemma by drawing on contemporary examples of AI use in heritage practices, in and beyond the museum. The lecture critically reflects on the opportunities and challenges of AI technologies and ‘synthetic’ media for memory institutions, the knowledges they care for and their audiences. It further asks what kind of ethics and institutional futures museums should strive for when attempting to navigate this fast-evolving techno-cultural environment.

Professor Areti Galani is Deputy Head in the School of Arts and Cultures, at Newcastle University, UK. Areti has led theoretical, empirical and creative practice-based research on digital imaginaries of European heritage and she is a lead editor/author of the volume European Heritage, Dialogue and Digital Practices (Routledge, 2019). She is currently a co-investigator in the project Living Cultural Labs (LIL-ECHOES, 2026-30), which explores how virtual worlds and AI-enabled cultural environments can help Europe turn cultural difference into a shared resource for belonging.

This free public lecture marks the legacy of the late Dr Michael Volkerling, former Chief Executive of the Museum of New Zealand, who made a huge contribution to the local cultural heritage sector over 30 years. This event is presented in partnership with National Services Te Paerangi and the Stout Research Centre.

The lecture will be recorded and made available on the National Services Te Paerangi website following the event.

Upon arrival, you grab a badge to say if you're looking for dates OR mates.

events.venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Following acclaimed and sold-out runs in London as well as an extensive tour of North America, the UK, and Australia, the Olivier Award-winning reimagined production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber celebrated musical JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR will play in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch this October through to December, as part of a major international tour.

Featuring lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber, this production was reimagined by London’s Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, where it originated, and is helmed by director Timothy Sheader and choreographer Drew McOnie. Completing the creative team is design by Tom Scutt, lighting design by Lee Curran, sound design by Nick Lidster, and music supervision by Tom Deering.

A global phenomenon that has wowed audiences for decades, JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR is a timeless work that explores the biblical portrayal of the extraordinary events that led to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire. Originally released as a concept album, the iconic 1970s rock score contains such well-known numbers as ‘Superstar’, ‘I Don’t Know How to Love Him’, and ‘Gethsemane’.

events.long_description:
The Little Grimley Amateur Dramatic Society from Limelight Theatre returns in another hilarious comedy from David Tristram. With a membership of just four, the society has survived budget constraints, artistic disagreements, and countless theatrical disasters. This time, faced with the challenge of finding a suitable play, chairman Gordon decides there’s only one solution: an evening of Shakespeare.

After all, what could possibly go wrong when an amateur dramatic group takes on the world’s greatest playwright?

As Gordon’s ambitious vision collides with limited resources, Bernard’s enthusiastic improvisation, Joyce’s personal distractions, and Margaret’s diva tendencies, the production quickly descends into chaos. With tempers flaring, egos colliding, and Shakespeare being interpreted in ways he never intended, keeping the show on track becomes a performance in itself.

Packed with the witty dialogue, larger-than-life characters, and laugh-out-loud moments that have made the Little Grimley series a favourite with audiences, To Be Or Not To Bother is a delightful evening of pure comedy entertainment.

events.venue: Studio 73, 73 Main Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
‘Wheeler’s Luck’
by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews

Wheeler’s Luck is a rural NZ comedy set in the Wairarapa and will run for nine performances from 18th November at Studio 73, Greytown.
Auckland developer, Richard Lush, plans to build a seven-storey gaming and entertainment facility, swimming pool, hotel, health spa, and 18-hole golf course in a local town near you, all at the invitation of the Mayor (a keen golfer). The aim is to inject millions into the local economy and create 51.5 new jobs.

The trouble is, the land has been left to the people of the town according to the will of Nora Cox, not the council - a fact that Mayor Duncan Sanderson has tried to keep under wraps. But there’s no chance of secret machinations in this small town, with eccentric local postie Murray Dickie on the case.

To add to his woes, the Mayor is also having trouble with freak weather and regurgitating sewerage, an experience that will resonate with some Wairarapa residents. There’s a brawl in a local pub that conforms only loosely to legal opening hours, and an annual horse race held on the beach.
So the plot unfolds in this Greytown Little Theatre comedy production Wheeler’s Luck, set in Bell End (a small coastal community to be found in Wairarapa) and coming to Greytown’s Studio 73 in November this year.

The play was written by Nigel Collins, Toby Leach and Damon Andrews, each of whom have significant careers in film, television and theatre as actors and playwrights. Nigel and Toby first performed Wheeler’s Luck in 2004, playing all 52 of the characters of the hilarious and complex plot moving between 1882 and the present day.

Five characters will play all the parts, sometimes conversing with themselves, including the roles of animals and faxes and bells, and swiftly moving between genders. The actors are Egan Tearle, Josh Cameron, and three Kuranui College teachers of music, drama, and dance - Lisa McLeod, Juanita McLellan and Alena-Rose Burt.

events.venue: Taiawa - Wellington Tech Hub,33 Bunny Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
IP for SaaS - How to Protect Your Business
A practical session for SaaS founders on IP, ownership and protecting what you’re building.

About this Event



Your code, your product name, your brand, that clever bit of workflow you’re quietly proud of. It’s all IP, and most founders don’t think about it until someone else is using it. Savvy businesses protect their IP with trade secrets, trade marks, copyright and more.

Spend an afternoon with the team from IPONZ, alongside other founders asking the same questions. Leave knowing what you own, what you don’t, and what to do next.

Afternoon tea is provided from 3:30pm, with the event starting at 4pm. Stay afterwards for networking drinks with the experts and other founders.

The IPONZ experts -

Alicia Baxter is Principal Business Advisor (IP Strategy) at IPONZ, working across NZ's commercialisation ecosystem where she focuses on driving early engagement to make sure the value of IP is understood upfront, not after the fact. With a BSc(Hons) in Chemistry from the University of Auckland and a double major in chemistry and genetics from Massey University, Alicia joined IPONZ in 2021 as a patent examiner and progressed to Senior Patent Examiner before moving into business-facing roles, including Business Advisor at MBIE and Business Lead at IPONZ. Alicia is passionate about positioning IP as a core business asset and helping innovators turn great ideas into commercial outcomes.

Jeanette Singh is a Principal Trade Mark Examiner at IPONZ with more than 25 years’ experience in intellectual property law across the public and private sectors. She began her career at IPONZ before spending more than 15 years at Bell Gully, where she progressed to Senior Associate and advised across trade marks, copyright, designs and broader IP matters. Her experience includes drafting commercial IP contracts, leading IP due diligence projects and providing franchising advice. Jeanette has also run her own IP practice advising start-ups. While her expertise spans intellectual property, her particular passion is trade marks and the way this area continues to evolve.

Dr Penny Walsh delivers core IP services for IPONZ and is passionate about making intellectual property easier to understand and use. With a PhD in Chemistry and a background as a registered New Zealand patent attorney, Penny brings a strong combination of scientific and practical IP expertise. She has worked with clients across a wide range of industries to protect and manage their intellectual property, with experience spanning patents, trade marks, copyright and broader IP issues. Penny particularly enjoys contributing to IP education and helping people build the knowledge and confidence to make informed decisions about their intellectual property.

Join us for a special edition of ‘The African Book Club’, a regular monthly book club that celebrates Africa and its diaspora in art and literature. Every month our participants meet to discuss the books and art that is shaping the conversation around the continent that is often forgotten.

This event is proudly supported by Songs of Solidarity and Tender Press. It is part of the 2026 Songs of Solidarity festival - Anthems of Resistance which takes place from November 12 – 29.

Overview

Reset with hypnotic guidance and soothing sound in an immersive journey designed to release tension, restore calm and find clarity.

Hypno Sound Bath: Guided Healing




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




A 75-minute immersive journey I've created to help you reset your nervous system and step out of stress.

I'll guide you with hypnotic, subconscious language that works alongside sound healing, crystal singing bowls and gentle instruments, easing you into a deeply receptive, regulated state where your body can release tension and your mind can find clarity.

Your brain learns stress the same way it can learn calm. When your nervous system feels safe while you envision a stronger, calmer version of yourself, it starts wiring in new neural pathways, and that shift becomes your new normal.

You'll walk away feeling:

⁠ ⁠Calmer
⁠ ⁠Grounded
⁠ ⁠Back in control
⁠ ⁠Aligned with who you're becoming

This isn't just relaxation. It's a full internal reset.

Small group. Intimate setting. One-time only session.

Because your nervous system is the foundation for how you lead, perform, and show up in life.

We'll close the evening with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, a gentle space to connect and ease back into your evening.
Meet Krishnaloka, your hypno-healer

I'm a practitioner at Mindworks, dedicated to the study and mastery of the mind. As an Advanced Level Practitioner of Eutaptics/FasterEFT, I use one of the fastest, most effective methods for lasting change, working at the root of an issue, not just its symptoms. I bring warmth and genuine care to every session.

Meet Alexandra, your sound-healer

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

events.name: 30 Years With The Pūkorokoro Shorebird Centre - Forest & Bird Event
events.venue: The Garden Room at St Peter’s on Willis, 90 Ghuznee St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Keith Woodley has served as the Manager of the Pūkorokoro Shorebird Centre since 1993. Over more than three decades dedicated to coastal ecology and bird conservation, he has become a leading voice for shorebird protection in New Zealand.

The Wellington Branch of Forest and Bird invite you to join us as Keith shares insights into the world of New Zealand’s migratory shorebirds. Drawing on decades of observation and research, Keith will highlight the extraordinary migrations of species like the bar-tailed godwit and the unique adaptations of the endemic wrybill - the only bird in the world with a side-curved bill. He will discuss the seasonal rhythms of the Firth of Thames, and the work of Pūkorokoro Miranda Naturalists’ Trust in the East Asian Australasian Flyway, and how local community conservation efforts protect these critical coastal habitats.

Time: 6:30 p.m. Doors open/light refreshments
7:00 p.m. Presentation (ending 8:30 p.m. approx)
Venue: The Garden Room at St Peter’s on Willis St. enter from Ghuznee Street (behind St Peter's
Church in multi-story building)
RSVP: Please register via Eventfinda for seating/catering purposes
Queries: Email wellington.branch@forestandbird.org.nz

events.name: Beethoven 9 - Wellington
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Beethoven 9 - Wellington
The grand finale of the NZSO’s 2026 mainstage season features the grandest of symphonies: Beethoven’s Ninth.

Programme:
Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead Hoata
Beethoven Symphony No. 9

Its audacious juxtaposition of styles, sounds and forces, including the revolutionary inclusion of a choir, marked the Ninth as a landmark work, not just for Beethoven but for music itself. Its monumental achievement and undeniable emotional power will be brought to stunning life with the help of Orpheus Choir Wellington and City Choir Dunedin.

Our essential need for community and connection is also at the heart of Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead’s Hoata. Named for the Māori phase of the moon where the moon is barely visible, Hoata was written in 1979 during a cold northern hemisphere winter and evokes the icy blizzards and intense isolation that swirled around the composer as she wrote.

Come celebrate Rivering on the 19th of November with us. If you haven’t had a chance to catch us play yet, this gig is for you, and if you have already supported this project, come along, dance and grab a drink.

The collection of music entitled Rivering is written by saxophonist and vocalist Lily Rose Atu, and is deeply inspired by her love of jazz and neo-soul. It has been workshopped across the year with Jono Ben Zur (bass), Ranu Wijesuriya (drums), and Paulina Hernandez (piano) and has recently been recorded at Massey University.

Special features at this gig include Elisa Bird (clarinet and baritone) Frank Paton (trumpet) and Victoria Ferry (vocals). This will be our last gig with the incredible pianist Paulina who will be heading overseas just a few days after this show. Come and listen to the music we have created together for a final time!

Tickets from $10 at humanitix: https://events.humanitix.com/rivering-compositions-by-lily-rose-atu
Limited door sales: $15

events.long_description:
With a foot in both New Zealand and Australia, Stan Walker is one of Australasia’s finest pop/R&B singers. His show, Stan Walker: A Symphonic Experience Pōneke, brings him to the capital for an evening of his biggest hits. Accompanied by his full live band and a powerful orchestra, each song has been completely reimagined to create an unforgettable night of music. From Black Box and Take It Easy to I AM, Māori Ki Te Ao, and more, this is Stan Walker elevated into something cinematic, spiritual and powerful. 

Since winning the seventh season of Australian Idol in 2009, Stan Walker has gone on to release seven albums. The concert celebrates 17 years of music-making and cultural connection. It will be a night honouring the journey and the people who have been part of it every step of the way.

events.long_description:
Parent Support Group - Island Bay
Grab a free drink and chat with other parents and carers who know what it’s like to care for a disabled child, a neurodivergent child, or a child with health impairments.


Parent to Parent hosts regular Parent Support Groups in Island Bay to support carers and parents just like you. These groups are a safe space for family and whānau to share their experiences, their challenges, their triumphs, and to learn from each other in an open and 100% judgement-free environment. No topic is too ‘weird’, no question too ‘out there’. We get it, and we are here to help.


So if you’d like to share a struggle, celebrate a success, raise a concern, or simply have a cuppa and chat with other parents and carers in your area, you are always welcome at our Parent Support Group. Children are welcome too! Drop in for as long or as short a time as you want. And did we mention there’s free coffee??


Feel free to just show up on the day!


Contact Jack Baigent for more information:
| 027 808 3952

Come along to Fareham Creative Space for a fun, creative session painting your own piece of pottery.

Paint your gifts and decorations for Xmas!

Choose from a selection of handmade bisqueware, then make it your own using colourful underglazes. We’ll have ideas, examples and everything you need to get started, so no pottery or painting experience is needed.

Once you’ve finished, we’ll glaze and fire your piece in the Fareham kiln and let you know when it’s ready to collect.

Come on your own, bring a friend, and settle in for an easy-going creative session. You’re welcome to bring your own snacks and non-alcoholic drinks too.

Spaces are limited to 12
$30 for 1x large, and 1x small piece of pottery. Additional pieces available to purchase on the night.
email: registrations@farehamcreativespace.nz

Your booking also helps support Fareham Creative Space, our local not-for-profit community pottery studio and creative space.

events.long_description:
Come join us for a fun night of Speed Dating! It’s a fun and safe way to meet other genuine singles looking for a real connection. We will have a private function space for this event. Price includes a drink and delicious food at the break!

Speed Daters will be split into 2 age groups which will run simultaneously. There will be an opportunity to mix with the other group during the break.

When you arrive you will get a name label and your complimentary first drink, and will have time to settle in and mingle a little. You will be Speed Dating with around 10 people over the course of the evening. You will have 7 minutes to chat to each person. You then decide if you want to meet your Speed Dates again and tick interested on your form if you do. Only if the feeling is mutual will we email you each other’s contact details.

Speed dating does not have to be stressful or frightening; you will be pleasantly surprised how fun and positive it is.

Our event is designed to be inclusive and foster open, honest communication. Not everyone you meet will be your type, but we expect you to be polite. You only have to chat to them for seven minutes!

# Fargo (1996) | 30th Anniversary Screening

Friday 20 November 2026 | 7:30pm

Director: Joel Coen | Country: USA | Duration: 1h 38m | Genre: Comedy, Crime, Drama, Thriller | Classification: R18

*A lot can happen in the middle of nowhere.*

The Coen brothers’ darkly comic crime classic takes us to the snow-covered landscapes of Minnesota, where a desperate car salesman hatches a seemingly simple plan to solve his financial troubles: have his wife kidnapped and collect the ransom from her wealthy father.

But when the plan goes horribly wrong, a trail of violence leads to the unflappable and very pregnant Police Chief Marge Gunderson, whose quiet determination and sharp instincts bring her ever closer to the truth.

Blending pitch-black humour, suspense and unforgettable characters, *Fargo* is a brilliantly offbeat portrait of ordinary people making extraordinarily bad decisions.

Winner of two Academy Awards, including Best Actress for Frances McDormand, *Fargo* remains one of the Coen brothers’ most celebrated films.

95% on Rotten Tomatoes

Come and experience this modern classic on the big screen as we celebrate its 30th anniversary.

events.venue: Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Live Reading | New Pages: Mate by Regan Taylor
Join us for this live reading of a new script in development by Regan Taylor.

New Pages intentionally carves out space for the earliest phase of the creative process, inviting you into the room when characters and concepts are still fluid and shifting. It captures the essence of trusting the story before completely understanding it.

Mate is the new work-in-development by writer Regan Taylor (Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Pikiao), a Wellington-based theatre maker, director, actor, tutor, writer, occasional troublemaker and all-round theatre lover.

Regan is a graduate of the UCOL Theatre School, he's been making, directing, performing and teaching theatre across Aotearoa and Australia for the past 25 years. He's a regular director for Taki Rua and their Te Reo Māori seasons and Toi Whakaari – New Zealand Drama School, and is a founding member of Te Rēhia Theatre in Auckland. Next up, Regan is making a new touring show with The Māori Sidesteps, releasing Resilience, the latest children's album with The KaRs, and getting stuck into writing.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010.

Check out the full schedule here:
https://tawataproductions.com/breaking-ground/

Mate is presented from 7.30PM Friday November 20 2026 at the Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Tce, Te Aro, Wellington.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

events.long_description:
Four women; Siobhan, Louise, Annabel and Helen, sign up for The Pink Hammer – a women’s only woodworking course to learn carpentry skills only to find that the tutor, Maggie (who we never meet), has done a runner with their fees and left behind her disgruntled husband Woody, who finds his “man-cave” invaded by the four women.

We are very happy to present the wonderful Mexican double bassist Arturo Báez for two nights, playing solo and in improvised collaborations with a host of top notch local musicians.


Arturo Báez Velázquez is a Mexican double bassist and electric bassist whose music moves between jazz, free improvisation and spontaneous collective creation. Báez was born in Lázaro Cárdenas, Michoacán. He began playing folkloric music of the region at the age of 14, and moved to Mexico City at 19 to pursue his musical studies.

For more than 15 years, he has been an active presence in Mexico’s improvised music scene, collaborating with internationally acclaimed artists including Ken Vandermark, Joe Morris, Chris Corsano, Michael Zerang, Sam Newsome, Isaiah Collier, Dennis Gonzalez, Blaise Siwula, Brian Allen, Leo Genovese, David Borgo, Linda Briceño, Justo Almario, Víctor Mendoza, Remi Álvarez, Cristóbal López, Héctor Infanzón, Gabriel Puentes and Alejandro Campos, among others.

A prolific artist, Arturo is a regular member of many projects including Big Band Jazz de México, the Remi Álvarez Trío, Chocolate Smoke Gang, Carlos Marx and the Jorge Fernández Project. His international work includes performances at the No Idea Festival in Austin and across the United States, Europe and Asia. He leads Otrora un Simulacro, a creative jazz ensemble that features his original compositions.

events.long_description:
GOODNIGHT NURSE ARE BACK… AGAIN

New Zealand pop-punk favourites celebrate 20 years of Always & Never with one final run of shows




To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut album Always & Never, the band are coming out of retirement one last time for The Always and Never (Again!) Tour - three final shows across New Zealand before they hang up their studded belts for good.

For the first time ever, Always & Never will also be available on limited-edition purple vinyl, with pre-orders opening Monday 31 August.

Playing Auckland’s Powerstation on Friday 13 November, the band then head south for a show at Loons in Christchurch on Thursday 19 November before what promises to be a final show for the ages at San Fran in Wellington on Friday 20 November. Tickets for all dates go on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September from eccles.co.nz

Released in 2006, their debut album, Always & Never, has remained a favourite among pop-punk fans over the years. That album was the beginning of a nine-year career for Goodnight Nurse. They played hundreds of shows throughout New Zealand and Australia, released two NZ Top 5 albums and scored five NZ Top 40 singles.

“When we got back together in 2023 for the My Chemical Romance show, it felt like there was something special in the air,” says lead singer Joel Little, who has gone on to write and produce hit songs with artists including Taylor Swift, Lorde and Khalid. “So when the 20th anniversary of Always & Never rolled around, we thought, what better way could we possibly celebrate this than by reliving the glory days one last time?”

“We started making music to have fun with our friends, and just for the simple joy of doing it,” says drummer Jaden Parkes, now one of the lead singers of hugely popular band Leisure and the longtime Head of A&R at Sony Music NZ. “Playing these songs live again takes you right back to that feeling.”

And for day one fans, there’s one more reason to make this final tour a must-see.

Original bass player and fan favourite Paul Taite will be joining the band onstage for the tour, playing the songs he helped shape and bringing Goodnight Nurse full circle 20 years after Always & Never first landed.

The Always and Never (Again!) Tour will be Goodnight Nurse’s final three shows in New Zealand. For real this time. Tickets on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September

This is going to be a ridiculous evening of music. We have, in no particular order:

KING OYSTER

This is one of THE best bands in Wellington.

Driving grooves, classy funk, outstanding musicians. That’s what you get from King Oyster.

The band is Oscar Laven on sax, Blain Fitzpatrick on bass, Matthew Fitzpatrick on guitar, and Jacob Randall on drums. One look at those names, and you know you are in for some remarkable playing.

THE TEMPLE

The Temple is a trio composed of producer Jack Woodbury, drummer/percussionist Nathan Carter (aka Alter Natural), and saxophonist Peter Liley, based in Pōneke. The Temple’s broad palette of influences reaches into minimalism, electronica, ambient, jazz, funk, doom metal, new age, sound art, and jungle, creating a beguiling, kaleidoscopic sound. Their shows explore vast musical territories, and every performance is a ritual devoted to the present moment.

ISKRA

ISKRA are an otherworldly quartet hailing from Te Whanganui-a-Tara formed by saxophonist Josh Buckler and featuring Simon Grove (Niko Ne Zna) on helicon, Ato Kwamena (Culture Embassy) on percussion and David McGurk (Planet Hunter) on drums. Inspired by the likes of Sons of Kemet and the London jazz scene, they bring driving grooves, soaring melodies and the fire of afro-beat, Balkan music and brass-Hhuse.

Think dance party at the end of the world, when the last lights have gone out.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
One of the UK’s most beloved and enduring pop groups, SAINT ETIENNE, are heading to Australia and New Zealand for the very last time. Following the announcement that their 2025 album International would be their final studio release, the iconic trio will take their celebrated catalogue on a farewell tour across the region this November and December.
Released in September 2025, International was met with rapturous acclaim, returning Saint Etienne to the UK Top 10 and reaffirming their status as one of Britain’s most treasured musical institutions. Now, fans across Australia and New Zealand will have the rare chance to experience the band’s shimmering, genre‑blurring sound live, one final time.
With a career spanning more than three decades, Saint Etienne’s songbook is rich with classics including ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, ‘Spring’, ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’, ‘You’re In A Bad Way’, ‘He’s On the Phone’ and ‘Wood Cabin’ tracks that helped define an era of British pop and continue to resonate with audiences worldwide.
Formed in 1990 by Croydon natives Bob Stanley and Pete Wiggs, Saint Etienne struck gold from the outset with their debut single, a transformative cover of Neil Young’s ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, which quickly became a club anthem. The arrival of vocalist Sarah Cracknell in 1991 completed the definitive lineup, her debut on ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’ and the Mercury Prize‑nominated album Foxbase Alpha cementing the group’s place in UK pop history.
Their follow‑up album So Tough soared into the UK Top 10, leading to a landmark moment in 1994 when Saint Etienne became the first band ever broadcast live from Glastonbury Festival.
Now, after decades of innovation, reinvention and irresistible pop craftsmanship, Saint Etienne prepare to say goodbye to Australian and New Zealand audiences.
A final bow from one of Britain’s most cherished groups which is not to be missed.

You’ll learn a structured method of taking yourself into hypnosis (informed by scientific research), some of the classic applications of self-hypnosis and evidence-based skills that will convince you without doubt of your ability to hypnotise yourself.

• Define and discuss hypnosis
• Practice self-hypnosis

• Use the language of self-hypnosis
• Relax hypnotically to deep levels

The iconic Museum of New Zealand, Te Papa Tongarewa, will become a gathering place for investigators, storytellers, and dreamers from across the globe. events.id: 2026 Pūkaha Wairarapa Garden Tour-South Wairarapa, State Highway 2, Greytown-Event Finder
events.name: 2026 Pūkaha Wairarapa Garden Tour
events.venue: South Wairarapa, State Highway 2, Greytown
events.long_description:
Discover 12 spectacular gardens across South Wairarapa during one unforgettable spring weekend.

The 2026 Wairarapa Garden Tour invites you to explore a hand-picked collection of gardens located throughout Featherston, Martinborough, Greytown, Gladstone and surrounding areas. Over two days, you'll enjoy exclusive access to gardens that are rarely – if ever – open to the public, travelling at your own pace and creating your own itinerary.

This year's tour features an exceptional mix of historic country estates, contemporary landscapes and much-loved family gardens, each with its own character and appeal.
A major drawcard of this year's tour is the inclusion of two of Wairarapa's most significant heritage properties, both featuring on the Wairarapa Garden Tour for the first time. Fernside, a New Zealand Garden’s Trust listed property one of New Zealand's finest historic gardens, re-opened to visitors in 2025 after more than five years closed to the public, offering the rare opportunity to explore its magnificent grounds, heritage trees and rich history. Rototāwai, a remarkable country estate featuring beautiful gardens, a historic homestead and an on-site gallery, also makes its debut on the tour.

The Wairarapa Garden Tour celebrates gardens of every scale and style. Alongside the grand country estates, visitors will discover intimate town gardens, flourishing cottage plantings and thoughtfully designed contemporary spaces, each offering fresh ideas and inspiration. Many of the tour's most memorable moments come from seeing how passionate gardeners have transformed their own corner of Wairarapa.

The tour also features:
• The Market Fair – a vibrant garden setting showcasing local food, beverages, artisan goods and crafts, hosted at Fernside.
• Exclusive workshops hosted at selected gardens (details released in August).
• Opportunities to purchase plants, produce and small-batch products grown and made by garden owners.

The Wairarapa Garden Tour is a fundraising event for Pūkaha National Wildlife Centre. As Pūkaha's largest annual fundraiser, the tour helps support vital conservation work, including native species recovery, forest restoration, predator control and education programmes for local school children.

Gardens are open from 9.30am to 4.30pm each day.

Before starting your tour, you'll collect your wristband and printed map from designated collection points in Featherston, Martinborough or Greytown (locations to be announced).

Food trucks and coffee carts will be available at selected gardens, and visitors are welcome to bring a picnic and enjoy the beautiful surroundings.

Join us for a weekend celebrating exceptional gardens, passionate gardeners and the very best of South Wairarapa, while helping support the future of New Zealand's native wildlife.

Visitors should note:
• The tour goes ahead rain or shine.
• Pets are not permitted.
• Children are welcome but must be supervised at all times. Children 9 years and under do not require a ticket.
• Some gardens include natural hazards such as ponds and creeks.

Important visitor information:
Visitors enter all gardens at their own risk. While Pūkaha and participating garden owners take reasonable care to provide a safe environment, visitors are responsible for their own safety and personal belongings. Paths and garden surfaces may be uneven, slippery or contain natural hazards. Visitors should take care at all times and follow any instructions or signage provided by organisers, volunteers or garden owners. To the maximum extent permitted by law, Pūkaha and participating garden owners accept no liability for loss, damage or injury arising from a visitor's participation in the Wairarapa Garden Tour.

events.name: AI Masterclass: Going Further with AI
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
You’ve used AI – now make it work on your actual job. In this hands-on full-day workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through building a real AI system around your work: connectors, your own documents and tools, Anthropic skills, and Claude Design. Intake form required before class. (NZ Citizens and residents pay $250 with ID.)

You’ve been using AI for a while – maybe daily. You know how to prompt. But you’re still doing one-shot chats when your work deserves a proper system. This masterclass changes that.

Before you arrive, you’ll fill in a short intake form – what you do, what you want AI for, and what you can’t do (paste client data into public ChatGPT, work outside regulated tools, etc.). Jon reads every submission before class and shapes the day around the room. We won’t be doing a generic feature tour; the day is built to be a hands-on and customised workshop.

We’ll spend the day wiring AI into your actual work: the Claude desktop app, connectors to the tools you already use, a project built around your real documents and tasks, and Claude Design. You’ll leave with a working AI system to improve your life and work.

By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:

• Set up the Claude desktop app with Chat, Co-work, and Code – ready for real work

• Enable and use connectors (Gmail, Drive, calendar) – and know which ones to leave off

• Build a Claude project around your own documents and tasks, with voice input and plan mode

• Write operating rules for your workspace – constraints, verification triggers, what never goes in public chat

• Discover and run Anthropic-provided skills on your real task

• Stress-test your output with synthetic personas before you ship

• Produce polished visual artifacts with Claude Design

• Apply professional judgement: when to delegate, when to verify, when not to use AI at all

Please bring: A laptop (Co-work and Code need a keyboard). The Claude desktop app installed and signed in. A paid Claude subscription (Pro or Team) – required for connectors, Co-work, and skills. Your intake form submitted at least 3 days before class. One real task you want to work on.

A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Prerequisites
Have completed Getting the Most from AI (Tier 1) – or equivalent: regular Claude or ChatGPT use, basic security habits, and some experience with Projects or custom instructions. This is not a beginner class.

Predator Free Wellington presents Birdfest – Wellington's newest music festival celebrating the city's birdlife revival. We’re evicting the pests, backing the birds, and turning up the dawn chorus for our iconic feathery performers and musical manu.

events.name: Printing with Chine Colle
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Welcome to mixed media collage the printmakers way. Chine Colle is a printing process in which a thin sheet of paper is printed on and at the same time, mounted on a sturdier sheet, creating a subtle delicate backdrop to the printed image. Expanded on, this can include contrasting papers, graphic images, select colour shapes and fabric. The mission is just to have fun creating together in the fabulous Inverlochy print studio.

In this one day workshop people will:

Practice traditional and individual chine colle techniques
Explore the use of delicate papers more responsive to ink and hand printing
Test and practice mixed media chine colle with images, papers and fabric
How effective chine colle is as a method of adding colour to prints
Making and using a damp pack
Recipes for traditional glues
Materials are supplied and feel free to bring your own special bits and bobs to include and or share.

Minimum age to attend this workshop is 16 years.

Thirty minute lunch - bring a water bottle and packed lunch to enjoy in the historic Inverlochy or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.name: Watercolour Landforms Painting Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Dramatic landforms catch my eye and intrigue me and I desire to portray the forms in watercolour. Learn how to capture the light on the ridges and define the shadows in the valleys. I share my approach with my students by sharing the colours to use, how to start and how to proceed step by step. In this two-day workshop you will use the core techniques of watercolour to paint landforms. We will refresh our knowledge of washes and edges, then use them to create beautiful landscape paintings.

Charlotte will demonstrate her watercolour painting techniques using bright colours and good quality materials She uses an overhead camera projected onto a 42-inch TV for easy step by step instruction. .The course will cover strategies for building a composition, delicate washes and how to achieve spatial depth in landscapes.

Please note this is not a beginners class and you must bring your own materials. This workshop is for intermediate to advanced watercolour painters.

What to bring -

Paints: We will use the basics: Raw Sienna, Alizarin, Cobalt as primary colours, Burnt Sienna, Ultramarine, Viridian, Quinacridone Gold and Indigo - but bring all the other colours and brands you regularly use.

Paper: Bring 4 quarter sheets - quality 100% cotton paper 300gsm watercolour paper for good results. Buy a full sheet (76 x 56 cm) and tear into four quarter sheets for the four paintings we will make over the weekend, or good quality A3 pad is OK. Cold pressed, hot pressed or rough - I recommend Arches, Saunders Waterford. Bring extra paper for the exercises.

Brushes: Bring your favourite brushes including a large mop and Hake for wetting large areas quickly. There will brushes for purchase.

Bring all the usual paraphernalia for painting including water container, masking tape, pencil, ruler, rubber, cloth, tissues, spray bottle, hair dryer. I usually work flat on the table or prop up the board.

One hour lunch each day - bring a packed lunch to enjoy in our historic house or explore the local Te Aro cafes. Coffee and tea provided at lunch.

events.long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

events.long_description:
Live reading of The Black Woman of Gippsland play
Join us at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library for a live reading of The Black Woman of Gippsland by Andrea James. This event will be held in Ngā Pou Ruahine (Level 2), Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library.

Based on real events and set on Andrea’s grandmother’s country, The Black Woman of Gippsland is a poetic, emotionally rich and clever embracing of First Nations stories that have long been silenced. In 2026, Andrea's play The Black Woman of Gippsland was awarded Nick Enright Prize for Playwriting at the NSW Literary Awards, with judges praising it as an outstanding and extraordinary work that deftly reveals how colonial myths shape the way histories are recorded and believed.

This event is part of the Breaking Ground: International Indigenous Writing Festival, produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council, Creative New Zealand, Hannah Playhouse, Toi Aro and Te Haukāinga.

events.name: Stacking Bangles - Taster Class
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own set of stacking bangles!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished, solid silver bangle with their own preferred texture. You can finish your copper bangle too, and leave with a set!

We’ll begin by learning the basic technique on your copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using little hammers. Once you’re confident you’ll move on to your main project: a length of round solid silver wire, to be turned into a slender bangle crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with simple textures or leave it plain and give it a bright polish or a satin finish.

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio if you wish to make more.

events.name: By Hand + The Lord of The Rings: The Fellowship of The Rings
events.venue: The Circus Cinema, Bar and Cafe, 34 Jellicoe St, Martinborough
events.long_description:
By Hand + The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
25th Anniversary Celebration | Special Double Bill
Sunday 22 November 2026 | 3pm
Circus Cinema, Martinborough
See the films, meet the filmmakers.

Presented as part of the Te Waiwhakaata Wairarapa Film Festival Spring Sessions 2026, this special double bill brings together two films celebrating craftsmanship, creativity and the magic of filmmaking.

First, discover By Hand, a documentary by Wairarapa filmmaker Jane Ross, telling the story of Ali and Greg Lang, two remarkable local craftspeople whose traditional skills have contributed to some of the world's most celebrated films.

Then, celebrate the 25th anniversary of Sir Peter Jackson's landmark film The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, returning to the big screen for this special occasion.

It's a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the Wairarapa's own contribution to the world of Middle-earth and the extraordinary people whose craftsmanship helped bring it to life.

By Hand
Director: Jane Ross
Documentary short | 15 minutes

By Hand tells the story of Ali and Greg Lang, New Zealand's last working wheelwright and coach painter, respectively. Through their origins, love story and enduring legacy, the film celebrates their exceptional craftsmanship and the traditional skills they continue to preserve.

Ali and Greg also crafted props for The Lord of the Rings films and continue their relationship with Wētā Workshop.

The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring (2001)
Director: Sir Peter Jackson
Adventure, Fantasy, Action | PG | 2 hours 58 minutes

Celebrate 25 years of Peter Jackson's landmark adaptation of J.R.R. Tolkien's epic fantasy.

When Frodo Baggins inherits a mysterious and powerful ring, he discovers that its destruction is the only way to prevent the Dark Lord Sauron from conquering Middle-earth. Joined by an unlikely fellowship of companions, Frodo embarks on a perilous quest that will change the fate of the world.

Experience the beginning of this extraordinary cinematic journey on the big screen once again.

Tickets and Bookings

Tickets are available directly through Circus Cinema.

Visit the Circus Cinema online booking page and select the Book Tickets button, or phone 06 306 9442 to reserve your seats.

Venue: Circus Cinema, Martinborough
Date: Sunday 22 November 2026
Time: 3pm

events.long_description:
Sound Healing Experience with Claudio at Union Yoga
Sound Healing Experience at Union Yoga with Claudio

Join us at Union Yoga for a restorative evening of pure sound, inspiring music, mantra chanting, and deep relaxation.

Facilitated by multi-instrumentalist Claudio, this immersive journey combines the resonant power of Tibetan Singing Bowls, Gongs, Native American flutes, Drums, Harmonium, Esraj, and Bells. Supported by high-quality amplification, the vibrations allow you to feel the sound throughout your body, helping you release physical, mental, and emotional tension.

Give yourself a peaceful space to turn inward, reconnect with silence, and discover the calming power of your own voice and mantra. Bring an intention, get comfortable, and let the sound waves guide you into deep rest and contentment.

Event Details:

Date: Saturday, 21st November 2026

Time: 5:30 PM – 7:30 PM

Location: Union Yoga | Centre Walk, 133 Main St, Upper Hutt

Investment: $49

What to bring: Feel free to bring a pillow and blanket to ensure total comfort.

About the Facilitator: Claudio is a third-generation multi-instrumentalist from Mexico City, now based in Wellington. After graduating as a classical guitarist, his musical journey led him through Jazz, World, and Spiritual music in Montreal, before diving deeply into Indian Music and the Yoga tradition across Europe and Asia. Having studied the art of Tibetan Singing Bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, Claudio brings over a decade of dedicated sound healing and performance practice to this transformative session.

More about Claudio : www.claudioescutia.com

events.long_description:
Same Name Confusion - Wellington
Same Name Confusion are embarking on a trans-Tasman tour in support of their new album, SNC (out September 25 via Winegum Records).

SNC is a groove-focused record with a knack for finding the playful, romantic (and occasionally absurd) beauty in everyday life.

Praise for SNC so far:

‘Peculiar music… ace, wonky dance pop’ - Grant Smithes (Family Jewels Records/RNZ Nine To Noon)

‘Eccentric, unexpected and infectious’ - Hannah & Oli (RDU The Smoko Show)

Praise for Same Name Confusion live:

‘It’s raw, energetic and eccentric...Same Name Confusion should be leaders of surreal performances and one not to be missed’ - Radio 13

The band have appeared at Cubadupa, Cross Street, and Tora Bombora Festivals, and have supported Australians Skegss, Lime Cordiale and Spacey Jane.

Same Name Confusion is a trans-tasman collaboration, with formerly Christchurch, then Wellington co-writers Luke Courtney and Andrej Radosavljevic now split between Auckland and Melbourne. This is a rare opportunity to see the band live with a five-piece band.

Supports to be announced.

events.name: Ossia
events.venue: The Raumati Social Club,34 Poplar Ave, Raumati South, New Zealand, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Ossia
Ossia - Italian for “alternate musical passage” - is an ensemble exploring what happens when musicians step beyond the expected.

Following a warmly received debut earlier in 2026, Jess Deacon (vocals), Jessica Murphy (keys, melodica and vocals), Robert J. M. Kingi (guitar and bass), and Cam Steel (drums and percussion) bring their jazz festival set to Raumati Social Club.

Drawing on jazz, soul, folk, groove, meditation and songwriting, Ossia takes familiar material apart and rebuilds it in the moment. Songs become starting points rather than fixed arrangements, stretched through improvisation and reshaped through spontaneous interplay. Intimate, responsive and intuitive, Ossia creates performances where structure gives way to possibility, listening matters as much as playing, and no two journeys are ever the same.

events.long_description:
Back by popular demand, join us this November for Coven Saloon, a Coyote Ugly themed night. Don't fight the moonlight and be there! Cowboy boots are optional but the best dressed will be rewarded.

Wet t-shirt comp, body shots and surprises in store. Follow us on Instagram for more event info.

Coven is a party for Sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people. Tickets are pay as you wish or koha on the door.

More info about Coven:

Coven Kaupapa
For queer women and gender minorities, spaces like this are rare, vital, and sometimes, life-changing. In a world that constantly centers cishet norms, Coven offers a space where we are the default – where you can fully show up as yourself, be seen, celebrated and surrounded by YOUR community.

Coming Solo? You’re Not Alone.
Don’t be nervous if you’re planning to come on your own – Coven is built for connection. Whether it’s your first queer event or your hundredth, you’ll be surrounded by a community that gets it. From the moment you arrive, there’ll be friendly faces, welcoming vibes, and plenty of chances to mingle, and connect. Coven is about belonging – and there’s a place here for you.

For many in our Coven, this is one of the only opportunities we feel comfortable enough to experience nightlife free from the male gaze, tokenism, fear, or the need to shrink ourselves to fit in. It’s a space where sapphic, trans, nonbinary, and gender-diverse people aren’t just welcomed – we are centered. It’s for those who are often pushed to the margins, who rarely feel represented in “inclusive” spaces that still cater to the mainstream.

This night exists because we need it – and because we create it, together.

Accessibility
This event is located down a flight of stairs. Have specific accessibility needs? Reach out at coveneventswellington@gmail.com

We're back with another night of house, techno, disco, bass & more at Moon Bar with Funky Fridays (Saturdays) Vol. 11.
Created to revive and celebrate the underground electronic scene, Funky Friday is more than just a night out, it’s a space for music lovers, dancers, and creatives to connect through rhythm and energy. Each edition features a rotating lineup of talented DJs, both local and international, ensuring a fresh and unique experience every time.
Come with an open mind and leave with tired feet.
With a boiler room style, this edition features legends Ryan C, Fortuna and Not My Sister.
$10 Early Birds, 15$ First Release, 20$ Final Release, available now via UTR, or $25 on the door.
Get your tickets early before it gets sold out!

-------------------------------------------------------
NOT MY SISTER - HOUSE / TECH HOUSE
Hailing from Italy and now rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister quickly burst onto Aotearoa’s dance floors and has been on a rapid rise ever since. She’s lit up festivals like Twisted Frequency, Kiwiburn, Earthbeat, CubaDupa, Taniwha’s Den and Arkadien and supported international acts including KC Lights.
She currently holds a radio residency on Wellington’s iconic Radio Active, where her show dives deep into house and underground sounds.
Heavily influenced by funk and disco, and driven by a love for vocals, groove and infectious pulse of 90s House, Not My Sister delivers high-energy, uplifting sets that weave together melodic basslines with soulful, tech and deep house sounds. Expect pure passion and play from the moment she steps up to the decks.

SoundCloud: http://www.soundcloud.com/not-my-sister
Facebook: http://www.facebook.com/notmysista
Instagram: http://www.instagram.com/not.my.sister

FORTUNA - DEEP / PROGRESSIVE / MELODIC
A selector who knows exactly where the night needs to go:
Fortuna is the founder of Fortunes, a Pōneke event series devoted to the deeper end of the spectrum: deep, progressive and melodic house and techno.
Her selections run dark and sexy, all rolling momentum and slow-burn tension, the kind of set that rewards surrender. She doesn't chase the peak, she builds toward it, and the dancefloor follow.

https://www.instagram.com/for__tunes/
https://www.facebook.com/Fortuna89
https://soundcloud.com/for_tunes/sets/fortuna


RYAN C - TECHNO
Ryan C is a house and techno DJ based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), NZ.
He spent his formative years travelling solo around the desolate Southern African coast, the stars his blanket and the ocean his teacher.
After being missing for 14 years, he was ‘liberated’ by the Red Cross in Northern Africa ‘working’ on an Ethiopian pirate ship in the Gulf of Aden.
He was in desperate need of revitalisation, so was moved to their base deep in the Amazon basin, in Peru, near the border of Brazil, where he was healed by Amazonian Shamans using an ancient technique.
The Amazonian tribe then guided him by canoe through the Amazon river to the coast of Brazil where he found a group of underground tribal techno-heads living on an island and learnt the ways of techno. After finding out about an illustrious island in the South-Pacific where the earth moves and sky is painted with lava from deep inside the earth, he made his way to Aotearoa where he continues his search inwards, through music.
You'll also find me hosting the Midnight Marauders radio show on Radio Active Friday nights 11-1am!
https://soundcloud.com/ryancrawfordnz
https://www.instagram.com/ryanc.nz/

events.id: Finding Matariki: Their nature, and legends.-Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Finding Matariki: Their nature, and legends.
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Delve into the rich tapestry of Māori and Polynesian astronomy with our engaging evening tour at Stonehenge Aotearoa. While the sacred time for observing Matariki (the Pleiades) traditionally occurs with its early morning rising, these same stars grace the evening sky in November. This presents a unique opportunity for those seeking to explore the cosmos in a comfortable, warm setting as the night sky darkens.

Our tour begins as the sky transitions from twilight to night, creating an ideal environment for stargazing. Guided by knowledgeable astronomers, you will embark on a journey through ancient legends and the physical nature of the stars. This is a time of learning and understanding, where the mysteries of the heavens unfold through captivating stories and scientific insights.

Using laser pointers, our guides will illuminate the constellations, revealing the celestial patterns recognized by Māori and Polynesian navigators for centuries. You’ll learn how these constellations were used not only for navigation but also for marking seasonal changes and significant events. The stories behind these constellations are rich with cultural significance, offering a deeper appreciation for the ingenuity and wisdom of our ancestors.

As you gaze up at the night sky, you’ll discover the intricate connections between the stars and the stories woven into the fabric of Māori and Polynesian heritage. From the celebrated Matariki cluster to other important constellations, each star tells a part of the larger narrative that has guided and inspired generations.

This tour provides a perfect blend of mythology and astronomy, making it suitable for all ages and interests. Whether you are a seasoned stargazer or a curious newcomer, you will find something to fascinate and inspire you. The use of laser pointers enhances the experience, making the constellations easily identifiable and the stories even more vivid.

Join us for an unforgettable evening under the stars at Stonehenge Aotearoa. This is more than just a tour; it’s an immersive experience that connects you to the ancient traditions and the celestial wonders that have shaped our world. Book your spot now and embark on a journey of discovery and enlightenment, where the past meets the present in the most spectacular way.

Please note: All guided tours must be booked in advance.
Tours do not run without prior bookings, and walk-ins cannot be accommodated. These are shared tours, meaning multiple groups may join the same session.

Chippy Nonstop is a versatile DJ, rapper, and producer whose high-energy sets seamlessly blend global club, rap, and bass-driven sounds. Australian singer-songwriter Courtney Barnett is heading back to New Zealand five years after her last sell-out tour. The ‘Creature of Habit’ tour coincides with the release of her fourth studio album of the same name. The album is emotionally resonant and explores the central question: how to get out of your own way so you can truly feel your life. With singles Stay in Your Lane, and Site Unseen’ setting the tone, the album and concert mark a decisive new chapter in her musical evolution. Along with the latest music, she will delve into her extensive back catalogue.

She is known for a style that incorporates intimate storytelling with indie rock and bursts of raw grunge-like energy. Her blend of moody guitar, witty, anecdotal lyrics and laconic talk-singing has cemented her as “one of the most distinctive voices in indie music” (The Mancunion).
