events.long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This three-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.

You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.

In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.

This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to Ōtaki looking for a creative experience.

What's Included:
All practice materials (copper or brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).
Use of all tools and equipment.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

events.long_description:
Dungeons & Dragons - An All Ages Adventure
Are you an adult who really wants to introduce your kid to Dungeons & Dragons?

Or are you a kid who wishes your parents would play?

Or are you whānau who want to adventure together?

Then All Ages Dungeons & Dragons is for you.

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s brand-new space for gamers, Titahi Bay Studios and Lounge, is for you.

Parents and kids can turn up together and be guided through a fast-paced adventure by a professional Dungeon Master. Choose your hero — a silver-tongued bard, a fire-flinging wizard, a sword-swinging fighter, a sneaky rogue, or something else entirely, with all characters, dice, and rules provided.

Parents, this isn’t a drop-off and run situation - you’re at the table too.

Expect laughs, ridiculous moments, and whānau bonding as you sling spells, swish swords, and roll dice together.

No prep. No pressure. Just a great location and a story you’ll still be talking about afterwards. All done in time for dinner!

This is an all-ages event (although we’d suggest that kids under 10 might struggle), but anyone under 18 MUST be accompanied by the holder of an adult ticket. So you can’t just purchase a ticket for a child.

If you don’t have a kid but want to play afternoon D&D, that’s fine too. Just make sure you’re prepared to share a table with some folks who know what 6/7 is about, and that it’s not really cool to reference it anymore.

events.name: Silver Clay Taster

events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

A Stunning Tribute To The Music, The Sound & The Energy of Phil Collins and Genesis
Performed by The Acclaimed International Tribute Artist, Andrew James, The Easy Lover.

This highly acclaimed International show will be touring New Zealand for the first time from October d to November 2026

All About The Easy Lover

Andrew James from Nottingham, England has been a singer/performer since 1994, Starting his Tribute to Phil Collins and Genesis at the end of 2006.

From the smallest venues to cruise ships and theatres, Andrew brings a wealth of talent and multiple experiences to every performance. Anybody who hears him sing, knows that they are hearing something very special indeed, he has a range and power in his vocal abilities that very few people have and is perfectly suited to the words and music of the great man himself, Mr Phil Collins !

Andrew was recently reviewed by The Stage newspaper,

“Swaggering around in the style of Collins the Thespian, in his movie Buster, this superb vocalist proved staggering......."
"I kept glancing at the stage in case Collins himself had popped over from his Swiss tax haven to entertain us. Complete with hairline, an exact vocal match and a great impersonation of mannerisms, this remarkable tribute artist gave us a segued set which was straight out of the tribute top drawer.”
(October 2011)

The Show itself comprises some of Phil's best songs from his solo career through the 80's and early 90's, also featuring some of his massive hits with Genesis. The show is a high energy, non-stop feast of great music and great visuals featuring no less than 7 costume changes and even a few little slices of Phil's anarchic humour !

Andrew has performed for many leading Hotel & Holiday chains in the UK, including Park Resorts, Haven, Butlins, Pontins and numerous smaller venues, private & Public. Andrew has also performed for Millennium Hotels & Grand Millennium Hotels in Dubai & Abu Dhabi & also recently, for the Dragon Hotel & Resort in Bahrain with a recent return visit to Bahrain, Andrew was performing at the famous Dilmun Club.

events.venue: Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Live Reading | On The Edge: The Boy From Vaiala by Victor Rodger
In this intimate session, we hold space for a live, raw reading of a vital new play in development. This is your invitation to sit beside the flame of creation before the ink is fully dry.

We welcome our community, arts audiences, and potential venue and festival partners to witness this latest work, and celebrate new Indigenous scriptwriting in development.

The Boy From Vaiala is the new work-in-development by award-winning playwright and producer Victor Rodger (Samoa (Iva), Scotland (Broughty Ferry)). Known for his bold and provocative works that delve into race, identity, and sexuality, Victor is a graduate of Toi Whakaari New Zealand Drama School.

Victor’s first play, Sons, premiered at The Court Theatre in Ōtautahi Christchurch. A revised version of Sons was subsequently produced by Taki Rua Productions, winning four Chapman Tripp Theatre Awards, including Most Outstanding New Writer and Most Outstanding New Zealand Play. Under his FCC banner, Victor has produced award winning productions of The Mountaintop by Katori Hall as well as Wild Dogs Under My Skirt and The Savage Coloniser Show by 2020 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate Tusiata Avia. The Boy From Vaiala will premiere at ASB Waterfront Theatre with Auckland Theatre Company in 2027.

The Boy From Vaiala is presented from 4PM Sunday November 22 2026 at the Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Tce, Te Aro, Wellington.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

Check out the full programme here:
https://www.iticket.co.nz/events/2026/nov/breaking-ground-on-the-edge-the-boy-from-vaiala-victor-rodger

events.long_description:
Arturo Baez / Blair Latham Quartet w/ Tyson Smith (gtr), Rick Cranson (dms) and special guest Anton Wuts (sax)

Arturo and Blair began their musical journey together when Blair moved to Mexico
City in 2010 and became an integral part of the jazz and improv scenes. Both being
in demand players, they were inevitably thrown together in many of the top
creative projects that performed at the main jazz clubs of the day (El Zinco,
Jazzatlan, Jazzorca). Since Blair moved back to NZ in 2014 they have maintained a strong musical connection, and look forward to sharing their original compositions and improvisations played with local legends Tyson and Rick with New Zealand audiences.

Arturo Báez is a Mexican double bassist and electric bassist whose music moves between jazz, free improvisation and spontaneous collective creation. For more than 15 years, he has been an active presence in Mexico’s improvised music scene, collaborating with internationally acclaimed artists including Ken Vandermark, Joe Morris, Chris Corsano, Michael Zerang, Sam Newsome and Isaiah Collier. His international work includes performances at the No Idea Festival in Austin and across the United States, Europe and Asia. He is a member of the Remi Álvarez Trio and leads Otrora un Simulacro, an original jazz ensemble that features his compositions.

Music from 5pm, FREE ENTRY - Koha for the band appreciated

events.long_description:
Hi Wellington Community,

We are the Wellington Circus Hub, a not-for-profit charity dedicated to preserving the art of circus here in Wellington. 

We are currently fundraising to continue to secure the funding needed to keep our space running. This includes equipment, staff, rent and more, we would love your support. Every little bit helps us secure our future here in Wellington.

For many of us The Circus Hub isn’t just a space, it’s a second home. A place to grow strength, confidence, creativity, and real connection. 

Thank you for your support, and every little bit counts.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping:

Revisit the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, starting on the morning of the reaping of the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell.

events.id: Goodnight Nurse - The Always and Never (Again!) Tour | SECOND SHOW-San Fran, Wellington -Ticket Master
events.name: Goodnight Nurse - The Always and Never (Again!) Tour | SECOND SHOW
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
GOODNIGHT NURSE ARE BACK… AGAIN

New Zealand pop-punk favourites celebrate 20 years of Always & Never with one final run of shows




To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut album Always & Never, the band are coming out of retirement one last time for The Always and Never (Again!) Tour - three final shows across New Zealand before they hang up their studded belts for good.

For the first time ever, Always & Never will also be available on limited-edition purple vinyl, with pre-orders opening Monday 31 August.

Playing Auckland’s Powerstation on Friday 13 November, the band then head south for a show at Loons in Christchurch on Thursday 19 November before what promises to be a final show for the ages at San Fran in Wellington on Friday 20 November. Tickets for all dates go on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September from eccles.co.nz

Released in 2006, their debut album, Always & Never, has remained a favourite among pop-punk fans over the years. That album was the beginning of a nine-year career for Goodnight Nurse. They played hundreds of shows throughout New Zealand and Australia, released two NZ Top 5 albums and scored five NZ Top 40 singles.

“When we got back together in 2023 for the My Chemical Romance show, it felt like there was something special in the air,” says lead singer Joel Little, who has gone on to write and produce hit songs with artists including Taylor Swift, Lorde and Khalid. “So when the 20th anniversary of Always & Never rolled around, we thought, what better way could we possibly celebrate this than by reliving the glory days one last time?”

“We started making music to have fun with our friends, and just for the simple joy of doing it,” says drummer Jaden Parkes, now one of the lead singers of hugely popular band Leisure and the longtime Head of A&R at Sony Music NZ. “Playing these songs live again takes you right back to that feeling.”

And for day one fans, there’s one more reason to make this final tour a must-see.

Original bass player and fan favourite Paul Taite will be joining the band onstage for the tour, playing the songs he helped shape and bringing Goodnight Nurse full circle 20 years after Always & Never first landed.

The Always and Never (Again!) Tour will be Goodnight Nurse’s final three shows in New Zealand. For real this time. Tickets on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September




Limited-edition vinyl avalible for pre-purchase

events.id: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

events.long_description:
Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

1 or 2 Day Presentation Skills Workshop

Limited tickets available. Get in now so you don't miss out!

When effective presenters speak, they do more than inform - they influence, persuade, and inspire. That isn’t down to magic or your personality; it’s method. With the right tools, anyone can build genuine connection and move a room.

This workshop is for leaders, emerging leaders, technical specialists, and professionals who want practical tools and techniques for speaking in both formal and informal settings.

Short on time? Attend 1 Day (Foundations) for all the core skills. Ready for a bigger shift? Choose 2 Days (Advanced) for one on one coaching and deeper transformation. Pick what’s right for you.

You’ll leave with the tools to present more clearly, confidently, and with the influence your role demands. This is not just for the stage. You will use these skills everyday.

The workshop format

Small group format for maximum practice and feedback (no massive groups).

Learning is adapted and personalised for maximum value (no cookie-cutter approach).

Hands on, practical learning, with easy to apply tools and techniques (no sitting around listening to theory).

The Effective Speaker - One Day Workshop (Foundations):

Tuesday 24th November

A hands-on day where you’ll learn our step-by-step SpeakerMap™ system to plan valuable presentations quickly and with ease.

You’ll learn the principles behind useful visuals, how to manage nerves, and three delivery techniques you can use immediately.

Foundations is best for technical experts who know their stuff but struggle to get it across, and nervous presenters who want a safe, practical reset.

What you’ll learn

Plan engaging content (fast)

Use the SpeakerMap™ to develop a clear Key Message and structure that keeps audiences attentive without overload.

Plan faster, make better decisions about what to include (and what to ditch).

 

Design useful slides (not wallpaper)

A simple but revolutionary way to design slides that support - not sabotage - your message.

Practical guidance on using AI to fast-track draft slides and create supporting documents (and how to avoid creating AI slop!)

How to use PowerPoint to keep you on track without putting your audience to sleep.

 

Keep nerves under control

A proven psychological approach to calm the mental chatter that causes waffling, speed talking, and blank moments.

Build a personal plan to shift focus from “me” to the audience and the outcome you want.

 

Deliver in a natural, engaging way

Three delivery techniques that help you look credible, be engaging and feel confident.

(For more intensive delivery coaching, check out Day Two)

 

Plenty of practice

You’ll practise each technique in pairs or threes - supportive, safe, and highly practical.

All food and drinks during the workshop

The Effective Speaker workbook

30minute one on one follow up session

Gain all the skills from Day One - and then take them further. If presenting is central to your career growth, this is the coaching workshop you need.

Over two full days, you’ll create a significant shift in your communication skills.

Day One gives you the foundations to make presenting easier and more effective.

Day Two consolidates and extends these skills. You’ll go deeper into content planning, adapt the tools to your real work presentations, and get personalised coaching to develop your own authentic style.

You’ll also learn strategies for handling even the toughest audiences. The workshop is practical, hands-on, and focused on learning by doing - presenting, receiving coaching, and observing your peers.

If you’re ready for lasting, transformative change in your communication skills, the two-day option is the best choice.

Everything from Day 1 (Foundations) PLUS

Go deeper with planning

Apply the SpeakerMap to plan an actual presentation that you can give. 

Dive deeper into crafting valuable messages that you can use in the future. 

Rehearse in a way that actually works

A practical way to prepare when time is tight — so you own your words.

Shift from competent to compelling

One-on-one coaching targeted to your specific needs.

Video feedback plus our inside-out coaching methodology to reconnect you with the techniques you use naturally in conversation.

How to use silence, pace, notes, and the remote without looking stiff or artificial.

How to speak with energy and authenticity, not speed and panic.

Eliminate “ums” and “ahs”, look confident (even when you’re not), and create a sense of commitment that audiences feel.

An understanding of your personal communication strengths and the areas you need to focus on for growth.


Handle audiences like a pro

Strategies for side chats, interruptions, distractions, disagreement, and the odd angry voice - while staying calm and in control.

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore anxiety as a signal for growth through timeless yoga wisdom and psychology.

Inspire Me!
Lessons from Anxiety: Using Difficult Situations for Growth




“A crisis is a terrible thing to waste” said famously by economist Paul Romer

Anxiety gets a bad reputation, but it's not actually the enemy. Anxiety is an internal alarm system, letting us know something in our life needs attention. We tend to respond by chasing the next fix that will soothe uncomfortable emotions, hoping the feeling will just go away. But if the underlying thing never gets addressed, the anxiety doesn't either. It just bubbles up in different ways and different situations.

This workshop isn't about adding another technique to your list. Instead, we'll look at how yoga lifestyle and yoga psychology approached this exact feeling long before self-care was a trend, and why that ancient framework still holds up today. Sometimes the answer isn't something new, it's remembering what already worked before and was simply overlooked.

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Rasesvari

Rasesvari is an events co-ordinator who loves to bring people together and create a warm and memorable experience. She thrives on connection with others and has a deep desire for a lifestyle of yoga, meditation and holistic healing.

Read less

events.long_description:
Forty Years Below - Antartica Show - Fundraiser for Coastguard Mana
The rugged beauty of the Old Man Range in Central Otago is a long way from the expanse of Antarctica, but for a young boy Roger Lusby, the two worlds were connected by the sight of American orange tailed aircraft soaring over his parents apricot Orchard and Roxburgh, Central Otago.

These childhood moments sparked a curiosity that lead Roger to spend a year at Scott base in 1969.

Now almost 60 years later he is touring his show called “40 Years Below” to communities who will have the unique opportunity to hear his stories first hand.

Roger offers a glimpse into what it was like to live and work as a base mechanic for a year and Sir Edmund Hillary's original base.

The evening also features are moving trip tribute to Sir Ernest Shackleton's legendary 1914 endurance expedition, celebrating one of histories's greatest stories of survival.

A seasoned balladeer Roger’s audiovisual show includes pictures, stories, songs, poems and humour to share his experience.

All funds collected from Rogers show go to help fund your local community needs.

Feedback from earlier shows.

Enthralling, inspiring, superb. Informative and enlightening.
I felt like I had been to Antarctica.
I have been to many presentations of time spent in Antarctica over the years, but none have evoked such a feeling for the unique place of peace and solitude, yet mixed with extremely tumultuous and unimaginably harsh conditions.

There will be a $15 charge for this show that will be collected in cash at the door.

events.long_description:
One of the top singer-songwriters to come out of the United States’ 60s music scene was none other than Neil Diamond. With a career spanning five decades, Neil is behind many hits that have stood the test of time and still woo listeners around the globe. Now you get to hear a tribute to him at The Opera House this November. 
Imbuing long-loved hits with new energy, The Sweet Caroline Tour recreates the feel of the famous man with careful attention to detail. It focuses on recapturing the sound, look and charisma of one of the world’s greatest entertainers. 
At the concert, you’ll hear songs that made numerous top ten lists, won Grammy awards and earned an induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. Zac Coombs steps into the shoes of the original performer and brings his own musicality and showmanship to the stage. Don’t worry, you’ll hear all the timeless hits like Sweet Caroline, Song Sung Blue, Red Red Wine, Cracklin’ Rosie, Cherry Cherry, Crunchy Granola Suite, Shilo, Solitary Man, Kentucky Woman, I Am… I Said, and more. 
Relive an era when songs were written with heart, soul and honesty, and melodies stayed with you for a lifetime.

events.long_description:
NZ Photographers of Cultural Collections is a group of photographers and imaging professionals working across Galleries, Libraries, Archives, and Museums across Aotearoa. We photograph cultural collections from paintings through to scientific specimens, and from intangible culture, through flat copy digitisation to 3D scanning. 

The forum is a chance to share knowledge and build professional networks. It provides valuable professional development that is otherwise hard to come by for this specialised field. We specifically aim to help smaller institutions by democratising specialist knowledge and building a network of support across the country. This year we have hybrid capability, and welcome physical event (paid) online-only (free) registrations.

This event relies on volunteers and institutional support. Thanks to Te Papa Tongarewa for donating the venue and kaimahi time, and National Services Te Paerangi for funding and administrative support and additional travel support for eligible attendees. Kaimahi from NZ maritime Museum, Auckland University of Technology, Auckland City Libraries, Puke Ariki and Archives NZ/National Library have collaborated to organise the event this year.

These contributions help keep costs down, the physical registration fee will help to cover a venue set up fee and a catered morning tea and lunch for in-person attendees.

Online attendees will receive an email with the zoom link closer to the date.

We intend to record the event via zoom. If we decide to distribute recordings in any form, we will seek the permission of speakers before doing so.

We'll be closing registrations for in-person attendees at 4pm Friday 6th Nov.

We have an online network here: https://groups.io/g/NZPCC
For any pātai please email us at: nzpcccommittee@gmail.com

Overview

Join us for the return of the PENZ Big Day Out series – our annual opportunity to connect, learn, reflect, and be inspired!

Big Day Out 2026 – Phase 4 PE Curriculum

Every November, we hit the road and bring kaiako together from across Aotearoa for a day of connection, learning and practical PLD.

This year, we're getting you ready for the new Year 9–10 (Phase 4) PE curriculum, rolling out in 2027. You'll leave with a clear understanding of what's changing, hands-on strategies to try in your classroom, and a plan to put it into action.

How the day works

1. Understand the curriculum
A quick look across Phases 1 to 4, then a closer focus on Phase 4: the key changes, structure, progressions and capabilities.

2. Explore it through the strands
Three hands-on workshop rounds, one for each strand:

Workshop A – Movement
Workshop B – Active Participation
Workshop C – OED

Each workshop previews Phase 3, then digs into the knowledge and practices in Phase 4. You'll take home a printed resource from every session (also available after the day).

3. Apply it to planning
Map your current programme onto the new curriculum using a large-format planning canvas, with a focus on flexible planning and a knowledge-rich framing.

Please bring a copy of your current year plan.

events.venue:
22 Ballance Street
Wellington, Wellington Region
events.long_description:
Overview

Many of us have financial questions we've been meaning to ask for years but never get around to. This is your chance to ask them.

We're surrounded by financial information. Social media, podcasts, news articles, online calculators, investment commentary, and endless opinions from friends and family.

With so much information available, it's easy to feel overwhelmed or unsure about what's actually relevant to your situation.

That's why I'm hosting a small group discussion for people who have questions about their financial future, whatever stage of life they're at, but aren't sure where to start.

We'll explore some of the questions that keep many people awake at night:

Am I making the right financial decisions?
What happens if life doesn't go to plan?
How do I balance enjoying life now with preparing for the future?
What financial risks am I not seeing?
Will I have enough to retire comfortably?
I'm earning an income, so why does it feel so hard to get ahead?

And perhaps most importantly:

What's one financial question you've always wanted answered but never asked?

Join us for an open, relaxed conversation where no question is too simple, and the discussion is driven by what matters most to the people in the room.

Read less

events.venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Special guest: Joe Cole

events.venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

events.long_description:
Haere mai for the cheekiest fundraiser known to femmes/thems - Butch Auction 2026 🔥

A handful of butches are donating their services to fundraise for InsideOUT Kōaro and Gender Minorities Aotearoa. The services range from chefs, barbers, writing workshop facilitator, waiata performer, cocktail bartender etc,

Here's what you need to know before you come along, during the auction, and what happens afterwards.

Before the Auction -

Butch profiles will be uploaded on this event page and 04BC instagram page so you know who you'd want to bid for. The profiles will show terms and conditions such as

if the service is available for a group setting,

how long is the offer valid for,

additional costs may apply to certain services;
For example, you bid on a chef and win (congrats!). You have your first sit down and plan out a 3-course meal for a special event for you and 4 other friends. The chef may only offer to cover the first $100 of the groceries so you will need to reimburse them for the rest of the grocery bill.

how much notice to give your butch before redeeming the service,

any other conditions or boundaries attached to the offer.

Make yourself a paddle to use on the night for bidding purposes only, if you don't have a ready-to-go one. Please do not use the paddle on anything or anyone at the event, even if it was consented! This is not the space for it.

Please consider what you are comfortable paying for a butch. You can also consider financially teaming up with friends to bid on a particular service.

Due to limited venue capacity, please let us know if you're no longer able to attend so we can offer your spot to someone else.

During the Auction -

Our MCs will introduce each butch, what they're offering, and a reminder of the butch's terms and conditions before opening the floor to bids. 

At the end of the bidding, the contact details of the top two bidders will be collected.
The full terms and conditions will be shown to the top bidder on the night. They will have 24 hours to decide to accept the T&Cs.

If T&Cs are agreed to -- a group chat between 04BC, bid winner, and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the second top bidder will be notified and be given a chance to review the same T&Cs.

If the second top bidder agrees to the T&Cs -- a group chat between 04BC, bidder and the butch will be set up.

If not -- the offer will not proceed.

After the Auction -

The successful bidder will have a 7-day window to finalise the payment to 04BC.

04BC will facilitate an initial meet and greet between the successful bidder and the butch. This is an opportunity to connect, clarify expectations, and make sure everyone is comfortable with the arrangement before moving forward.

If a disagreement or concern arises, 04BC can help facilitate communication.

If an issue cannot be resolved, or either the butch or successful bidder feels unsafe or uncomfortable proceeding, the offer may be withdrawn. Any refund considerations will be assessed in line with the circumstances, but please be aware that a full refund may not be possible as this is a fundraising event.

A VERY IMPORTANT REMINDER


You're bidding on a specific service not purchasing a person.

Winning a bid does not entitle you to anything beyond what the butch has explicitly offered and agreed to. There are no implied romantic, physical or sexual expectations attached to any winning bid.

Every butch has their own boundaries and conditions, and these must be respected throughout the process. Consent is ongoing, and either party can choose not to proceed.

No SWERFs, No TERFs.

Let's keep it cheeky, respectful and safe for everyone ❤️

Venue is wheelchair accessible with lift access and accessible bathrooms.

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore your creativity through intuitive Neurographic Art and a soothing sound bath, blending mindful expression with deep relaxation.

Meditate & Create
Neurographic Art & Sound Bath experience

 

Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

 

Neurographic Art is a simple, intuitive art practice that invites you to slow down, soften the mind, and turn your thoughts and feelings into lines, shapes, and patterns. There’s no right or wrong way to create, and no artistic experience is needed.

Alongside the art practice, you’ll be guided through a deeply relaxing sound bath featuring singing bowls, chimes and flutes. Let the sounds create space to settle, listen inward and connect with your creative flow.

Come as you are, explore without expectation, and leave with your own unique piece of art.

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!
Meet your Artist Rowena

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’

Meet your Sound Healer Alexandra

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

events.long_description:
Overview

Pause, soften and turn inward with Yoga Nidra, a gentle journey of deep rest, reflection and trusting the quiet process of becoming.

Yoga Nidra: The Art of Becoming




Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




As late spring unfolds around us, nature offers a gentle reminder that growth does not need to be rushed.

The buds open when they are ready.
The light returns in its own rhythm.
And beneath the surface, so much is quietly becoming.

This Yoga Nidra is an invitation to pause, soften and listen inwardly.

To honour where you have been.
To rest in where you are.
And to gently welcome all that is beginning to unfold.

You do not have to know exactly where you are going. Perhaps, for now, it is enough to trust the becoming.




After the event is over, enjoy an amazing plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host Nicola

Nicola of Namaste Nicola is a dedicated yoga teacher with over 20 years of experience teaching across Australia and New Zealand. With more than 300 hours of training with international teachers, her approach is gentle, soulful, and deeply grounded in yoga philosophy. Nicola creates a calm and nurturing space where students can slow down, rest deeply, and reconnect with themselves through practices such as Yoga Nidra, Hatha, and Yin Yoga.

Following a breakout run of releases, international touring, and millions of streams across Spotify and social media, PRINS returns for her biggest headline shows to date.
Now based between Los Angeles and New Zealand, the Auckland-born pop artist has spent the past two years building momentum across New Zealand, Australia, Europe, and the United States, developing a reputation for emotionally charged alternative pop, razor-sharp visuals, and a live show that punches far above its weight. With multiple chart placements, national radio support, and over 8 million Spotify streams to date, this marks the beginning of PRINS’ boldest chapter yet.

events.long_description:
Overview

Reel Rock 20 brings a new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

Reel Rock 20 brings the world’s greatest climbing stories back to the big screen with a thrilling new collection of films celebrating ambition, resilience and the relentless pursuit of the impossible.

This year’s program follows four extraordinary climbing journeys: Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on Bibiliographie; Michaela Kiersch’s historic quest to achieve the ultimate climbing double of 5.15 and V15; Colin Haley’s legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre; and Ben Mayforth’s determined pursuit of 5.13 as he continues to redefine what is possible in adaptive climbing.

JANJA GARNBRET
Olympic champion Janja Garnbret sets her sights on the legendary climb Bibiographie
Featuring: Janja Garnbret

MICHAELA KIERSCH
Michaela Kiersch sets out to make climbing history by becoming the first woman to complete the ultimate climbing double: sending both 5.15 and V15.

Her pursuit demands extraordinary strength, precision and perseverance as she pushes the limits of performance across two of climbing’s most difficult disciplines.
Featuring: Michaela Kiersch

COLIN HALEY
Elite alpinist Colin Haley lays everything on the line in a legendary winter solo push on Cerro Torre - one of Patagonia’s most iconic and unforgiving peaks.
Alone in extreme conditions, Haley takes on a bold alpine challenge where speed, commitment and survival are inseparable.
Featuring: Colin Haley

BEN MAYFORTH
Ben Mayforth redefines adaptive climbing through an intense and resolute pursuit of 5.13.
Driven by determination and an uncompromising approach to progression, Mayforth challenges expectations and expands the possibilities of adaptive climbing.
Featuring: Ben Mayforth

Tickets are on sale now at reelrockfilmtour.com.
NO REFUNDS OUTSIDE OF ADVENTURE ENTERTAINMENT'S CONTROL

The concert won’t just showcase this seminal album — it’ll sit alongside favourite songs from Cat’s catalogue over the past three decades. events.id: The Great Southern BioBlitz 2026-ZEALANDIA Eco-Sanctuary, Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Great Southern BioBlitz 2026
events.venue: ZEALANDIA Eco-Sanctuary, Waiapu Road, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
From Friday the 27th to Monday the 30th of November, the tracks of Zealandia will be teeming with citizen scientists (that’s you!) taking part in the Great Southern BioBlitz.

A bioblitz is a great way for communities to get involved in the natural world, learning more about the fauna, flora, and fungi living right under our noses. Spend the weekend taking photos of as many different species as you can to upload to iNaturalist, and watch as experts come along behind you and identify what you have found!

And how can we make that even more exciting? By making a friendly competition out of the event with neighbouring cities by having the most observations recorded! Look out Christchurch!

Anyone can participate and contribute to the wider data base of species in Aotearoa New Zealand. We can’t wait to see your observations from all across the Wellington region, whether that’s here at Zealandia or in your own backyard.

Learn more about the Great Southern BioBlitz.

Regular entry fees to the sanctuary apply. Members go free!

Photo: Lynn Freeman x Fujifilm

events.long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!


DINNER MENU:

STARTER: gf/v

Sashimi cut Akaroa salmon and yellow fin tuna, preserved lemon, harissa, coriander

MAIN COURSE: gf/v

Corn fed Chicken supreme, truffled portobello plin ravioli, ajo blanco, spring asparagus, chardonnay jus

VEGETARIAN MAIN COURSE: gf/df

Risotto prima vera Aged Acquerello rice, asparagus, green beans, peas, parmesan fondue

DESSERT: gf/v

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout. 

BOOKING YOUR PLACE AT A TABLE: 

You will be seated around tables of 10. If it is likely that friends will be coming along too, it is best to book all your places at the same time to ensure you are all on the same table.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event.

info@cluedunnit.com.au

cluedunnitwellington@ihg.com 




0450 511 945

CAT POWER
THE GREATEST. ON TOUR.
Brought to you by Banished Music, Strange News, and Love Police.

This November, Cat Power returns to Aotearoa, New Zealand for the first time since 2014 for three special shows: Thursday 26th November at Auckland’s Bruce Mason Centre, Friday 27th November at Wellington’s Opera House and now Saturday 28th November at Christchurch's James Hay Theatre. Cat Power will be performing her seminal album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular songbooks of the last three decades.

Twenty years on, Cat Power’s Memphis soul stirrer The Greatest is still one of the most astounding records ever to be heard, a late-night classic that still feels as intimate two decades after it first blew our minds and broke our hearts.

Support for these three shows will be Canterbury’s finest, Lawrence Arabia, performing an intimate solo set. Expect to hear some old favourites and new treats from his forthcoming album.

events.id: Cat Power. The Greatest. On Tour.-The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Cat Power. The Greatest. On Tour.
events.venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Twenty years on, The Greatest still sounds like midnight.

This summer, Cat Power returns to New Zealand for a run of special shows performing her seminal 2006 album The Greatest in full, alongside songs spanning one of the most singular catalogues in contemporary music.

Recorded in Memphis with members of the legendary Hi Rhythm section, The Greatest remains a defining statement from Marshall: smoky, soulful and heartbreakingly intimate. Featuring enduring tracks including “The Greatest”, “Living Proof” and “Lived in Bars”, the album cemented Cat Power as one of the most influential voices of her generation.

To mark the album’s 20th anniversary, these rare performances will revisit the record front to back, a chance to experience its quiet power, emotional depth and timeless beauty in the live setting it deserves.

Support for these shows will be Lawrence Arabia - the acclaimed musical project of Christchurch-born singer-songwriter James Milne, one of New Zealand’s most celebrated and influential contemporary artists. Across a career spanning nearly two decades, Milne has released a string of critically acclaimed albums, earning an APRA Silver Scroll for his song Apple Pie Bed, the inaugural Taite Music Prize, and multiple Aotearoa Music Awards.

There are few artists who can hold a room the way Cat Power can. Experience the magic of The Greatest and re-enter the orbit of the early millennium in these raw, hypnotic shows in November.

events.id: Yīn Yīn - New Zealand Tour | Wellington-San Fran, Wellington-Ticket Master
events.name: Yīn Yīn - New Zealand Tour | Wellington
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.


San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.id: Marcellus Pittman (detroit)-Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Marcellus Pittman (detroit)
events.venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
events.long_description:
Few DJs understand a dancefloor quite like Marcellus Pittman. A cornerstone of contemporary Detroit dance music, Pittman brings decades of experience, deep musical knowledge and an unmistakable sense of groove to Meow Nui on Friday 27 November.

A true master behind the decks, Pittman is known for sets that move effortlessly between rolling, low-slung house, high-tempo disco, raw techno, funk, post-punk and deeper late-night selections. His approach is instinctive and unpredictable, built around meticulous mixing and an ability to read a room and take it exactly where it needs to go.
Pittman first came to prominence alongside Theo Parrish on Essential Selections Volume 1 before becoming one quarter of the legendary Three Chairs, alongside Parrish, Kenny Dixon Jr. (Moodymann) and Rick Wilhite. He later founded his own Unirhythm imprint and released music through labels including Omar-S’ FXHE, while also collaborating as part of the T.O.M. Project and Rotating Assembly.

His productions carry the same raw, spacious and deeply human quality as his DJ sets, pairing tough drum programming with subtle, unexpected detail. It is a sound rooted firmly in Detroit while remaining completely his own.

From intimate basements to major clubs and festivals across the world, Marcellus Pittman has built a reputation as one of dance music’s most respected selectors. This is a rare chance to experience a true Detroit heavyweight on the Meow Nui system.

Support from Benny Salvador, one of Aotearoa’s most exciting young selectors, blending house, techno, electro, disco-funk, dub, boogie and beyond.

Don’t miss your chance to be in the room.

events.long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

events.long_description:
The Christmas Tui Express
Christmas should feel like a genuine celebration, and this year you can enjoy it aboard a train journey that is truly unforgettable. Due to huge demand, we are running a second Christmas Tui Express trip, giving friends, families, social groups, and festive adventurers another chance to enjoy this full day scenic rail experience.

Step into our premium carriages and settle in for a relaxed, cheerful journey through some of the lower North Island’s most beautiful landscapes. With great company, stunning views, and a festive onboard atmosphere, the whole day feels like a Christmas treat.

🌄 Manawatū Gorge — The Highlight of the Day
The standout moment of the trip is our exclusive passage through the Manawatū Gorge, now accessible only by train. From the open air viewing platform, breathe in the crisp gorge air and capture photos that look straight out of a travel magazine. It is a rare experience and one of the most memorable parts of the journey.

☕ Licensed Café Onboard
Your celebration begins the moment you board. Our licensed café carriage serves alcoholic and non alcoholic drinks, coffee, and sweet treats throughout the day, making it easy to relax as the scenery rolls by.

🍻 Destination: Tui Brewery
Once we arrive at Mangatainoka Station, enjoy a gentle 15 minute walk or hop on one of our transfer buses to the iconic Tui Brewery.

Your ticket includes a hearty BBQ lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage, with a non-alcoholic alternative available if you prefer. It is the perfect way to toast the festive season and enjoy the laid back Mangatainoka atmosphere before the return journey home.

🎟️ Seats Are Limited
With demand already high enough to add a second Christmas trip, now is the perfect time to secure your place aboard The Christmas Tui Express. Whether you are celebrating with friends, family, or simply treating yourself to a special day out, this is a Christmas experience you will not forget.

events.name: Bike Maintenance for Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.
Bring your pushbike along on the day.  If you have the following, please bring them as well:  A multi-tool and pump; chain oil and rag; lightweight close-fitting gardening or rubber gloves.
Note: A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
(Please note this course is not exhaustive and is not a professional training course).
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Name most parts of a bicycle correctly
- Perform a quick safety check on any bicycle
- Fix a flat tyre
- Adjust your bike to fit your body
- Oil and clean your chain
- Identify and fix some common brake problems
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.name: Eco Dye Workshop
events.venue: Waikanae Arts and Crafts Society Inc,27A Elizabeth St, Waikanae 5036, New Zealand, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Eco Dye Workshop
Impressions of Nature on Silk

Eco dyeing, also known as leaf or eco print, is a gentle, alchemical process where the natural pigments of leaves are transferred directly onto fabric, creating one-of-a-kind botanical imprints.

Join me for a full day of slow making and discovery as we explore this beautiful dialogue between nature and cloth. In the morning, we’ll forage around the hall, gathering leaves and foliage that speak to us. You’ll learn how to prepare and bundle silk with plant materials, drawing out colours and patterns from the landscape itself.

In the afternoon, you’ll design and dye your own silk scarf — a wearable memory of place and season, marked by the delicate traces of nature’s touch.

You will learn

• which plants and fibres work best for this method
• how to use an iron mordant to enhance colour and detail
• different bundling techniques and approaches

All materials and tools will be provided for use during the workshop.

Your workshop fee includes silk fabrics to explore and experiment with, one silk scarf to design and dye, and a detailed handout with information on mordants, dye plants, tips, and useful resources.

A ‘what to bring’ list (including suggestions for clothing and optional items) will be sent out closer to the workshop date.

Booking through my website (see link above)

Location

27A Elizabeth Street (Art and Craft Society)
Waikane
Kāpiti

AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

events.long_description:
🤖 AI, MARK MY WORDS!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

Whether you're writing an email to your teacher, applying for a job, preparing an essay or studying for IELTS, this workshop is for you!

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

✍️ What will you do?

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

You'll also receive practical take-home resources to continue improving your writing.

🎯 Who should join?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

No advanced writing or AI experience required!

The workshop is delivered in English, with Vietnamese-language support available where needed.

📅 Event details

Date: Saturday 28 November 2026

Time: 1:00–3:00 PM

Location: Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub

Address: 203 Willis Street, Te Aro, Wellington

Cost: FREE

Spaces: Limited to 25 registrations

📱 What to bring

A fully charged smartphone with internet access

A free AI chatbot app, if you already have one

Your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

Don't have an AI app? No worries! You can follow the live demonstrations or work with a partner.

💛 Why we're doing this

At Viet Hub NZ, we want to create more opportunities for young people to lead, share their knowledge and contribute to their communities.

This workshop is about more than writing. It's about encouraging independent thinking, building confidence and showing that technology works best when we remain curious and critical.

AI can suggest the words. But you decide what they mean.

🎟️ Reserve your FREE place today.

Organised by Viet Hub NZ, with venue support from Te Tai Ohinga Youth Hub.

Please note: This is a practical learning workshop, not a formal IELTS assessment or band-scoring session.

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Mini mosaics are really quick and simple to make - but can create a really popping design with beautiful coloured glass and fun shapes to decorate.

We will use gorgeous coloured glass pieces to create our designs on small flat backings - this is a very beginner-friendly method, and allows for several pieces to be made within the class time.

This class runs over two sessions; this means you have time to do all the parts of a mosaic. The planning, the glueing, and then your pieces have time to dry so you can then do the grouting and finishing off. A fantastic course that's super fun as a one-off experience - or to dip your toe into working with glass mosaics.

You can have the finished items as either:
A set ready to hang on a wall as singles
On a large sturdy jumpring ready to hang as a cute pendant set (or earrings).
On a cord for an heirloom Christmas ornament.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.

In the second session we will continue finishing off your mosaics, selecting the grout you like, and learning how to apply and clean up this essential part of a mosaic.

Finally we will look at what mounting options and special additions you might want to add to your piece that will complete the design.

You are welcome to continue creating more mosaics and can purchase additional materials to do so. Any that require grouting after the class is completed can either:
Be completed by our team (for a small fee)
Be grouted by you later, we can supply the grout and some sealant for you to take home.

This is a warm, friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to start working with hand-cut glass terraria.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Your materials for the class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

events.name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
events.venue: Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Coastlands Theatre, 34a Raumati Rd, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

For accessibility seating information and wheelchair space bookings please email kiaora@teraukura.nz or call 04)9740535 during office hours.
Door sales are only available if the event doesn't sell out prior.

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.

A warm author talk and community conversation about endometriosis, lived experience, self compassion and connection.

events.long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Photo by Charlie Jewell

MATRESCENCE is a new documentary theatre work, set to premiere at BATS Theatre as part of NZ Fringe 2027.
