events.long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

events.long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Unsung Heroes!

Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley -with special guest Angela Fox- share songs, stories and a slideshow from NZ's distant past. Together, they bring to life the characters and stories of our past - the quirky and macabre - that shaped who we are today.

Chris Priestley is a singer, songwriter & NZ historian. He has recorded eight albums and his musical spans over 40 years. As a hospitality entrepreneur he was co-founder of Real Groovy Records & café/music venues Java Jive, Kerouacs, Atomic and Café One2One in Ponsonby.

Cameron Bennett is a storyteller, singer songwriter and plays guitar and lap steel guitar. Journalism is his day job - he currently produces a weekly tv current affairs programme and is director/writer of the ongoing NZ Land Wars documentaries. New Zealand colonial history is in his blood; from the Wairau Affray to the Western Front, his forebears have borne witness - miners, gamblers, union organisers, shopkeepers and servicemen.

Saturday Nov 28

Music 7:30pm

$20 ($15 unwaged)

Tickets available online and at the door!

events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Space Academy in Christchurch

events.id: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Relive the highs and bitter lows of one of the most beloved comedians and writers of all time. Eric Idle sits down to tell his incredible life story, live on stage at the St James Theatre in Wellington. From the giddy heights of Monty Python success to the trauma of childhood — this is unscripted and candid. The audience will also get the chance to put their own questions to him live on stage.

An Evening of Idle Conversation covers sixty years of show business. Eric will recall memories of the friends he has loved and lost including Graham Chapman, George Harrison, and Robin Williams. He’ll also cover fortunes made and squandered, feuds, reunions, a brush with cancer, and why, at 83, he is still looking on the bright side of life.

Along with five other comics Eric formed Month Python in 1969. The troupe’s absurdist sketches continue to influence comedy more fifty years later. Eric is perhaps most famous for writing the song Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, The Rutles (the world’s first mockumentary), and the musical Spamalot.

There's more to you than you think.

Sometimes we get so caught up in the stories we tell about ourselves that we lose touch with what we're actually experiencing.

*Beyond the Story* is an invitation to step out of our heads and into a different kind of exploration.

Through movement, breathwork, music, conversation and shared experiences, we'll explore what becomes possible when we spend less time analysing and more time experiencing.

This is an experiential workshop rather than an introductory programme. It is particularly suited to men who have some experience of men's work or personal development, or who feel ready to explore themselves and their connections with others in a more embodied way.

You don't need to have all the answers. Curiosity and a willingness to participate are enough.

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Advanced

The Advanced workshop is for musicians who already have some experience with improvisation and jazz playing, or players with more advanced technique looking to dive deeper into the language of jazz.

Participants will take an in-depth look at playing jazz standards with the rhythm section, explore different styles and traditions, develop listening skills, and gain musical insights from the professional musicians leading the workshop.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

events.id: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Catherine Chidgey: The Starving Bride
events.venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Described by the 2026 Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate panel as "without a doubt one of New Zealand's most important living writers", internationally bestselling author Catherine Chidgey returns to Verb to discuss her tenth enthralling novel. The Starving Bride is an urgent and searing story set in near-future England.


Dumped by her boyfriend, fired from her job and estranged from her parents, Hazel Whitlock signs up for a sideshow act in Blackpool. The seaside resort has revived all the cancelled old favourites and she will be the Starving Bride. On display in the iconic Blackpool Tower, with a ravenous lion prowling the enclosure, Hazel must lie in silence while strangers view her body.

Join Catherine and Kate Camp for a special one-night event as they discuss the many layers of The Starving Bride, writing female experiences and the questions the book raises about spectacle, desire, survival and society's obsession with beauty.

Unity Books will be at the event bookselling and Catherine will be book signing.

Cover artwork by Max Thompson. Cover design by Todd Atticus. Author photo by Ebony Lamb.

Catherine Chidgey’s novels have been published to international acclaim. Her first, In a Fishbone Church, won Best First Book at the New Zealand Book Awards and at the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize (South East Asia and South Pacific). In the UK it won the Betty Trask Award and was longlisted for the Orange Prize.

Her second, Golden Deeds, was a Notable Book of the Year in the New York Times Book Review and a Best Book in the LA Times. Catherine has won the Prize in Modern Letters, the Katherine Mansfield Award, the Katherine Mansfield Fellowship, the Janet Frame Fiction Prize, and, for her 2016 novel The Wish Child, the Acorn Foundation Fiction Prize.

Her 2020 novel, Remote Sympathy, was shortlisted for the DUBLIN Literary Award and the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction. The Axeman’s Carnival (2022) won the Jann Medlicott Acorn Prize for Fiction. Catherine's two most recent novels are the critically acclaimed Pet (2023) and The Book of Guilt (2025), also published by John Murray.

Catherine lectures in Creative Writing at the University of Waikato.

Kate Camp is the author of many collections of poems, including The Mirror of Simple Annihilated Souls (winner of the 2011 NZ Post Book Award for Poetry) and How to Be Happy Though Human: New and Selected Poems (2020), and a collection of essays, You Probably Think This Song Is About You (2022). Her most recent book is Makeshift Seasons (2025), a new collection of poetry. Kate was born in 1972 and lives in Wellington.

events.long_description:
DOORS OPEN 6:00pm

Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over eighty. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. 
David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth’s largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special Documented for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow up Cultural Appreciation in 202, and his award winning show Shelf Help in 2025. He has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix is a Joke Festival, RTE’s Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 800 million views and a social following of over 2 million people. More info: davidnihill.com

events.name: DECEITS AOTEAROA TOUR 2026
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

events.long_description:
Join us for Professor Tristram Ingham's Inaugural Professorial Lecture, titled "Ōritetanga | Equity. One principle. One journey among many." If you'd like to attend, either in person or via the livestream, please register via the link above. This lecture will be followed by light refreshments.

About Professor Tristram Ingham's research:

Tristram (Ngāti Kahungunu ki Heretaunga, Ngāti Porou) is a clinical epidemiologist with decades of experience in healthcare research. His work advances equity across respiratory health, tāngata whaikaha Māori (Māori disability) and health services’ governance. He uses kaupapa Māori and mixed-methods research to translate evidence into policy and system change in Aotearoa.

Tristram led the development of Whāia Te Ao Mārama, the Māori Disability Action Plan 2018-2022 and is Chair of the Te Ao Mārama Aotearoa Trust, a nationwide organisation representing Tāngata Whaikaha Māori. He was made a Companion of the King’s Service Order (KSO) in the 2025 New Year Honours for services to survivors of abuse in care. In 2024, he received the ONZM for services to the disability community.

Tristram is an honorary fellow of the New Zealand College of Public Health Medicine, a member of the Institute of Directors New Zealand and a member of the Royal Society Te Apārangi.

Conference Theme:
At the Confluence: Communities, Catchments, and our Freshwater Futures - Ngā Rerenga E Tūtaki Ana

Our 2026 conference explores the confluence: the place where flows meet, merge, and reshape one another. In freshwater science, confluences are dynamic hydrological junctions which create unique habitats and environments. For this conference it represents the meeting of people, knowledge systems, innovations, and aspirations that shape the future of wai in Aotearoa.

Hosting the conference in Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara/Wellington, where urban streams like Waimapihi and Kumutoto meet the great harbour Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara provides a powerful metaphor for integration across urban waters, catchments, and communities. As Aotearoa navigates changing climate pressures, evolving policy landscapes, disruptive technologies, and growing community involvement, this confluence becomes a space for meaningful collaboration and forward‑thinking action.

We look forward to welcoming you to WLG!

Overview

Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

About this Event


Executive Briefing for CIOs, Strategy, Digital and Transformation Leaders



AI, transformation, cyber resilience and cost optimisation continue to dominate executive agendas, yet many organisations still lack a connected view of how these priorities impact the broader enterprise.

Join Kapish and Ardoq for an executive briefing exploring how leading organisations are making better decisions through greater visibility across strategy, business capabilities, technology, risk and investment.

Using a fictional organisation facing familiar business challenges, our consultants will walk through a series of executive scenarios involving transformation, AI adoption, technology risk, application rationalisation and operational resilience. We'll demonstrate how leaders can better understand impacts, dependencies and risk through a connected enterprise view enabled by Ardoq.

You'll gain practical insights into how organisations are:

Understanding the impact of strategic and technology decisions
Identifying hidden dependencies and risks
Reducing complexity and unnecessary duplication
Prioritising transformation and technology investments
Strengthening governance for AI and business change

The session includes practical use cases, a live demonstration of the scenarios within Ardoq, and opportunities for questions with our consultants and enterprise architecture specialists.

Lunch and refreshments provided. Places are limited.

events.name: Book Group: Chess Story by Stefan Zweig
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Chess Story (also published as Chess or, more poetically, as The Royal Game) is a novella by the Austrian author Stefan Zweig published in 1942. Written in exile in Brazil, Zweig examines Nazism, and he does so with (Penguin Books tells us) "his signature psychological insight". The story is set on a ship from New York to Buenos Aires and features a gripping chess match. This novella would be Zweig's final work. In exile in Brazil and despairing of the future for Europe, he and his wife committed suicide. He had sent the manuscript of Chess Story to his American publisher just days before.

There's a link to a translation on a website dedicated to the author -
http://www.stefanzweig.de/assets/pdfs/schachnovelle_english_complete.pdf - or, if you prefer to listen and because the novella's under 100 pages, there are audiobooks on YouTube etc that run a couple of hours.

At this Christmas session, we'll also choose what we're reading in the first half of next year. See you there!

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

Finding Ground in an Uncertain World: Ancient Wisdom for Modern Turbulence

Inspire Me!
The world feels increasingly chaotic—from economic pressure to global political shifts and an unpredictable future. When external conditions are completely out of our hands, how do we keep from feeling overwhelmed?
This interactive workshop bridges contemporary psychology with timeless philosophy to help us build unshakeable internal resilience and stay anchored in times of uncertainty. We’ll look at the big picture, unpack what it means to live with the unknown, and share practical tools to maintain clarity amidst the noise.

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

events.long_description:
Join Wellington pianist Michal Cihelka for an inviting and varied musical journey, bringing together some of the most beautiful and exciting music from the classical repertoire, alongside favourites from the world of musical theatre and popular music.

A particular highlight of the programme is Michal's performance of the first two movements of Shostakovich's beloved Piano Concerto No. 2, uniquely accompanied by his own Unreal Orchestra – a hand-crafted backing track that brings the sound and scale of a full orchestra to the experience.

Also featuring is Chopin's dramatic and deeply expressive Ballade No. 1, Debussy's ethereal Clair de Lune, and a selection of brilliant Preludes by Rachmaninoff.

And, for lovers of musical theatre and popular music, Michal brings together a selection of beautiful and familiar favourites, reimagined through his own distinctive arrangements.

Come along and enjoy a memorable and most beautiful piano recital. Pay-what-you-can tickets start at just $5. Tickets are available online, or at the door on the day (subject to seating availability).

Recital duration is approximately 75 minutes.

events.long_description:
Celebrate, connect and be inspired as we bring the Wellington Women in HealthTech community together to close out 2026.

Join us for an evening of conversation, connection and festive celebration, featuring a panel discussion with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy from Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora Digital Services. They will share insights into their roles, the different pathways that brought them into digital health, and their experiences working at the intersection of strategy, design and delivery.

Date: Wednesday, 2 December 2026
Time: 5.00 pm–7.30 pm
Venue: Fujifilm, Level 9, 20 Ballance Street, Wellington

Evening programme

5.00 pm–5.30 pm: Arrival and networking

5.30 pm–6.30 pm: Panel conversation with Kelsey Schwynn and Eileen Duddy

6.30 pm–7.30 pm: Festive networking and end-of-year celebration

Meet our speakers

Kelsey Schwynn is a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand, with experience spanning health strategy, product leadership, service design and digital transformation. Before joining Health New Zealand, she was Chief Product Officer at Optimal Workshop and held senior strategic design roles in Australia and the United States. Her career has included supporting government agencies, not-for-profits and Fortune 500 companies through human-centred design, product strategy and large-scale digital change.

Eileen Duddy is a strategic digital health leader with more than 20 years’ experience in the health sector, including over a decade working across complex, cross-government initiatives. As a Digital Health Partner at Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, she connects Digital Services with health sector stakeholders, translating clinical, operational and strategic priorities into aligned digital roadmaps and investment pathways. Eileen brings a pragmatic, forward-thinking approach to defining problems, aligning priorities and progressing initiatives that deliver meaningful outcomes for people, whānau and the wider health system.

Come along to hear two compelling career stories, exchange ideas with others across the HealthTech community, and celebrate the people and progress that have shaped another year for WiHT in Wellington.

events.venue:
The Great Hall
Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

A concert in three circles moving between installation, sound and performance.

Curated by composer-artists Elliot Vaughan and Noel Meek, STROMA transforms Massey’s Great Hall into a space for listening, wandering and encountering music from different perspectives.

The evening unfolds in three circles.

From 7:00pm, arrive at your own pace for an open, self-guided installation in the Great Hall. Wander through a collection of intimate works, sounds and performances, taking time to explore the space before gathering at 7:30pm.

At 7:30pm, the space transforms for Gordon Monahan’s Speaker Swinging, as performers set speakers into motion, sending sound and circles of light through the Great Hall.

Then, at approximately 8:00pm, the audience gathers in the round for a seated concert of chamber music, bringing together works by composers from Aotearoa and beyond, including a new commission by Eve de Castro-Robinson.

From open exploration, through sound and movement, to a concert in the round, the evening moves between different ways of listening, experiencing and inhabiting the space.

events.venue: Valhalla, 154 Vivian Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
Inside a cabin in Te Aroha, songwriter and former IvyBlue frontman James Brodie created "Yellow"- his first solo album under the Stillwater Lines persona.

Designed as a way to understand the events of his past in order to move forward into his future while recovering from a near-fatal car crash; James set about using his guitar, voice, and MIDI Keyboard to use music as a way to put his heart back together.

And in support of Yellow's release (August 14th, 2026), James is hitting the road to share the stories of his recovery and share the songs from the album using only his voice and his guitar.

This promises to be an intimate evening of stories and songs about faith, hope, recovery, and joy through all seasons of life.

events.long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

events.name: Allegra Krieger
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
New York based songwriter and composer Allegra Krieger brings her singular blend of folk, rock and indie pop to San Fran on 3 December, joined by special guest Elly Mae.

Known for songwriting that is intimate, understated and deeply observant, Krieger pairs soulful vocals with raw, vulnerable lyricism, moving through themes of love, loss and self-discovery with a striking sense of emotional clarity. Her work has earned praise from the New York Times, who described her as a “deceptively understated songwriter,” while Paste has celebrated the distinctive poetry running through her music. 

Having shared stages with artists including Jana Horn, Fust, Johanna Samuels, Shalom and Charlotte Cornfield, Krieger has steadily carved out a space of her own within contemporary indie songwriting, creating music that feels equally at home in moments of quiet reflection and full-band intensity. 

Opening the evening is Pōneke songwriter Elly Mae, whose dreamy guitar-led folk-noir draws from the textures of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, PJ Harvey and Mazzy Star. Since first appearing on Wellington stages in early 2025, she has gone on to perform at Newtown Festival, CubaDupa and Flying Nun’s A Month of Saturdays live series, with RNZ describing her sound as a “woozy ethereal slice of dreampop.” 

Together, the two artists make for an evening of evocative songwriting, atmospheric guitars and music built around the power of close listening.







San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.name: Timeline - 300 Years of Music for Saxophone
events.venue: St Michael's Anglican Church, 81 Upland Rd, Kelburn, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us as we explore the history of the saxophone through 300 years of music performed by an exciting yet subtle chamber duo.

This concert explores a broad range of music, from pieces by J.S Bach which predate the saxophone by over 100 years, to modern compositions which push the limits of the instrument. Between these moments you will hear some of the greatest works for saxophone, from the popular showcase Pequeña Czarda to the elegant staple Tableaux de Provence.

Hear the many moods and timbres of the saxophone, from delicately soaring melodies, to dark, enchanting arias and joyful, raucous moments.

Programme:
J.S. Bach - Partita No. 2 for Solo Violin: IV. Gigue
Robert Schumann - 3 Romances
J. B Singelée - Concertino Op. 78
Eugène Bozza - Aria
Pierre Lantier - Sicilienne
Pedro Itturalde - Pequeña Czarda
Paul Bonneau - Caprice en Forme de Valse
Paule Maurice - Tableaux de Provence
Steven Banks - Surrender

$25 pre-sale
$35 door sales
$10 student/concession

About the performers:
Alex Trask is a saxophonist based in Pōneke. He has a keen interest in the classical saxophone and has studied with some of New Zealand's leading player such as Simon Brew and Reuben Chin. He is a member of the Royal New Zealand Air Force Band and has performed with many other significant organizations such as Gallery Orchestra, Saxcess, Wellington Youth Orchestra, and Wellington City Symphonic Band.

Alex is also an accomplished jazz player, and has performed all over the country. In 2026 he appeared with the Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra, as well as playing lead alto for the RNZAF Jazz Orchestra. Alex helf the lead alto chair in the Rodger Fox Big Band from 2024-2025 and has performed as a guest with that band since 2022. In 2026 he recorded his first studio album, which will be released in 2027.

Gabriela Glapska is a Polish-born, Wellington-based pianist celebrated for her expressive artistry, versatility, and collaborative spirit. An accomplished soloist, chamber musician, and sought-after accompanist, she brings clarity, depth, and nuance to a wide range of musical settings.
 
Gabriela holds a Master’s degree with Distinction from the Feliks Nowowiejski Academy of Music in Bydgoszcz, where she studied under renowned pianist Ewa Pobłocka, and a PhD in Music Performance from Victoria University of Wellington. She currently works as a collaborative pianist at Te Kōkī – New Zealand School of Music.

Whether performing in concert halls, schools, or contemporary music spaces, Gabriela Glapska is known for her refined musicianship, intuitive ensemble playing, and passionate advocacy for music in all its forms.

Photo by Hayden Hockly

events.name: Yoga Nidra
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.long_description:
Summer Tour - Kāpiti
Don't miss some Baroque French and Italian delights with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen and Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese.

It is astonishing to consider the musical impact Giovanni Pergolesi made, considering he died of tuberculosis at the age of 26. Like Mozart, his early demise quickly became the stuff of legend — hundreds of works were (often falsely) ascribed to this Italian late-Baroque genius, while rumours swirled that his death was the result of murderous jealousy from musical rivals.

Led by NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen, we survey some of Pergolesi’s most brilliant opera — La serva padrona, Adriano in Siria, L’Olimpiade and Il prigionier superbo. We are delighted to have Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese join us as we delve into music that glories in resplendent Italian Baroque colours and textures.

We complete this magnificent concert with a detour into the French-Baroque, with a suite from Jean-Philippe Rameau's Platée. C’est magnifique!

Generously supported by Ainsley Walter

events.long_description:
Get your festival crew together – COME TOGETHER is rounding out 2026 with a massive end-of-year celebration, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS, bringing some of New Zealand’s most celebrated musicians together to recreate the songs and performances that have defined the world’s greatest music festivals.

From Bob Dylan going electric at Newport and the mud-soaked magic of Woodstock, to the monumental performances of Led Zeppelin and Pink Floyd at Knebworth and the modern-day spectacles of Glastonbury and Coachella, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS is a journey through the music and moments that made festival history.

Pre-sales for the Auckland and Wellington events open at 9am today, with all remaining tickets on sale to the general public from 9am tomorrow via Ticketmaster. Come Together’s end-of-year bashes are always hugely popular, so fans are encouraged to get in quickly – these tickets won’t last.
Taking to the stage for this huge celebration is an all-star line-up featuring Jon Toogood, Milan Borich, Jennie Skulander and Seamus Johnson, backed by the powerhouse Come Together band – Jol Mulholland, Brett Adams, Mike Hall, Matthias Jordan and Alistair Deverick.
Together they’ll tackle an incredible catalogue of festival-defining music from artists including Jimi Hendrix, The Who, Pink Floyd, Led Zeppelin, R.E.M., The Killers, Pulp, Radiohead, Queen, U2 and Arcade Fire, and more.

These are the artists and songs responsible for those unforgettable festival moments – performances that transcended the stage and became part of music history.

From the counterculture revolution of the ’60s and ’70s, through the defining alternative anthems of the ’90s and into the stadium-sized festival performances of today, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS will celebrate the music that has united generations of fans.

Since its inception, Come Together has earned a reputation for bringing classic music spectacularly to life on stage, assembling extraordinary line-ups of New Zealand musicians to perform some of the greatest songs and albums in rock history.

Now, Come Together is taking that spirit out to the festival fields.

Expect huge songs, exceptional musicianship and plenty of moments guaranteed to have audiences out of their seats and singing at the top of their lungs.

And best of all? It’s the ultimate festival experience without the mud, the rain or the portaloo queues.

Gather your festival crew, relive the moments that defined generations and celebrate the end of 2026 with an unforgettable night of live music.

These are the artists and songs responsible for those unforgettable festival moments – performances that transcended the stage and became part of music history.
From the counterculture revolution of the ’60s and ’70s, through the defining alternative anthems of the ’90s and into the stadium-sized festival performances of today, FESTIVAL ANTHEMS will celebrate the music that has united generations of fans.

events.long_description:
Manawa Ora Mirimiri - The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork WELLINGTON
OUR LAST EVENT FOR 2026

Nau mai, haere mai ki Manawa Ora – The Foundations of Māori Healing and Bodywork.

Experience traditional Māori healing practices grounded in cultural knowledge in this 2-day Foundational workshop with Manawa Ora.

We invite you to reconnect with the wisdom of our tūpuna and explore the foundations of traditional Māori healing through a holistic, hands-on approach to wellbeing. Grounded in mātauranga Māori, this workshop provides an introduction to the principles, values and practices that underpin Māori healing.

Throughout this workshop, participants will be introduced to mirimiri and romiromi (Māori bodywork), exploring intention and connection in the healing process. We will consider cultural aspects such as whakapapa, tikanga, manaakitanga and wairuatanga.

The workshop offers a supportive space to learn, reflect and develop an awareness of how Māori healing traditions can inform our approach to wellbeing, both for ourselves and for those we care for. Participants will be encouraged to pay attention to their own bodies, deepen their connection with others and appreciate the responsibility that comes with engaging in the healing process.

Over the last 10 years, these workshops have welcomed people from all races and backgrounds. Wānanga/workshops are safe spaces for people to come together for the pupose of learning and healing, guided by tikanga.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

Whether you are beginning your journey into Māori healing or seeking to strengthen your existing understanding, this workshop provides a foundation from which to grow with respect, aroha and intention.

PLEASE NOTE THIS WORKSHOP IS NOT A QUALIFICATION TO PRACTICE.

The 2-day workshop includes:
- Cultural philosophies
- Whatumanawa (intuitive diagnosis)
- Self-awareness and insight
- Waiata, karakia and takutaku
- Spiritual hygiene
- Introduction to mirimiri and romiromi
- Group interaction & hands-on practice
- Selfcare and tools to maintain wellness

Facilitator Jolie Davis has over 30 years experience in Rongoā Māori; mirimiri and romiromi. Educator, advocate, founder and lead practitioner at Manawa Ora; the largest provider of Rongoā Māori in the Wellington region.

WHO THIS WĀNANGA IS FOR:
This wānanga welcomes all with an open heart and an open mind
Individuals on a personal healing journey, ready to discover their inner potential.
- Māori seeking reconnection with whakapapa, culture and self-identity.
- Those drawn to indigenous healing modalities and philosophy.
- Bodyworkers, healers and mainstream practitioners seeking to expand their knowledge and enrich their practice.

At Manawa Ora, we believe that healing begins with connection – connection to ourselves, to one another, to our whakapapa and to the ancient knowledge of Rongoā Māori passed down through generations.

events.long_description:
Frame your favourite work of art for a holiday gift. Bring along a painting and a suitable frame, either a cheapo from Briscoes or a good second hand frame. We will provide all the tools, process and materials to frame your piece of art.

It’s a practical course where you will learn to prepare the frame, cut with a knife, measure and cut a matt with the matt cutter.
You will walk away with your painting framed, ready to hang and some useful knowledge about framing ready for sale, exhibition standards, D rings, swing tags, acid free archival materials, tape, and how to hang a painting on the wall.

What’s included in this workshop:

Demonstration steps to framing your work
assembling the tools you need
choosing and cleaning frames
how to size and cut an acid free mat
what sort of tapes to use for each task
various fixings for hanging and D-rings
replacing acid leaching materials with foam board
cutting techniques
making and attaching labels and swing tags
how to photograph your art

This is a hands-on session where you will learn to cut card, cut a window in the matt board, present, secure, tape, screw in D-ring, tie knots etc. All materials will be provided including: knives, metal ruler, cutting board, crescent board for the mat, mat cutter, tape, d-ring, string.

What to bring along:

your artwork to frame
a suitable frame for the artwork A4 or smaller
enthusiasm

Thirty-minute lunch - bring a packed lunch to have in our historic home or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.name: Glass Bead-making - Christmas Drink Holder Charms!
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Christmas is coming, and what better way to celebrate than with beautiful, colourful glass creations? Come into Workspace Ōtaki and make your own unique wine glass charms in a festive palette, creating tiny decorations that will add a personal touch to your celebrations.

In this fun introduction to lampworking, you’ll work with Sarah Brock, the magician of colour palettes, to explore the art of shaping molten glass into miniature creations. Think warm golds, deep greens and rich reds, alongside the classic combination of red, green and white. You’ll learn the basic techniques for working with glass, then let your creativity take over!

There’s no need to make your charms match – embrace the colours, experiment with different combinations and create a collection that’s uniquely yours. Your finished glass pieces will be turned into wine glass charms, with charm holders provided. They’re perfect for adding a playful, handmade touch to your festive table, summer drinks or seasonal gatherings, and make lovely gifts for friends and family.

No previous experience is needed, although some existing skills will help with more intricate projects. Everyone is welcome – just bring your imagination and get ready to play with glass!

Teens aged 12+ are welcome; however, participants under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Kāpiti Food Fair 2026
Make a day of it. Gather your friends and whānau, plan your destination getaway, secure your accommodation and VIP parking early, and get ready to savour the flavours, sounds, and spirit of summer at Kāpiti Food Fair 2026.

Kāpiti Food Fair is where great food, great people, and great summer memories come together. As one of the Wellington region’s most anticipated food festivals, it offers a vibrant celebration of New Zealand’s food culture, bringing together the very best producers, artisans, chefs, entertainers, and food lovers for an unforgettable destination day out.

More than just a food event, Kāpiti Food Fair is a lively summer festival that celebrates the incredible talent and diversity of New Zealand’s food and beverage industry. Visitors can sample and shop their way through an exciting United Nations of flavours, discovering artisan products, boutique beverages, handcrafted treats, international street food, fresh produce, specialty ingredients, and unique home and kitchen products. It is a place to try, buy, eat, drink, relax, and uncover new favourites.

On the menu for 2026 ……. up to 10,000+ visitors, 250 vendor sites including a Kāpiti Artisan Producer Zone, an off-licence Liquor Zone, a Licenced Bar & Main Stage, the Seriously Pickled Kāpiti Kitchen, the Kāpiti Ice Cream Dining Room, FREE kid’s zone, ZEAL Zone buskers, roving street performers and much more!

Mazengarb Reserve Paraparaumu Kāpiti Coast
10am to 5pm RAIN or SHINE

TICKET COSTS
EARLY BIRD by 8 Nov:
$18 Adults | $13 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

STANDARD from 9 Nov:
$23 Adults | $18 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

AT GATE:
$30 Adults | $25 Gold Card or Student ID (Eftpos ONLY)

FREE up to 12 years ANYTIME

PARKING OPTIONS: $13 VIP & Gold Coin

MERCH (not sold online): $3 Bags

Tickets sold online at Humanitix – OPENING in EARLY September.

Booking fees will be added to the cost of your ticket and paid at check-out. Booking fees cover Humanitix costs, and everything else goes to their education projects that help to change lives. Kāpiti Food Fair has chosen to support Manaiakalani Education Trust that supports Māori, Pasifika, and disadvantaged learners in Aotearoa to increase student outcomes and get equal access to digital education.

TOP TIPS for a FANTASTIC DAY at the Kāpiti Food Fair:

1. Have your VIP parking and gate entry tickets ready for scanning.

2. Bring a gold coin for parking koha donations if VIP parking is not purchased.

3. Pack a hat and sunscreen – complimentary SPF is available if you need it.

4. Bring a picnic blanket to relax, enjoy the ambiance, and savor treats, plenty of seating and a shaded picnic zone under the trees!

5. BYO your own chair and a chilly bin for purchases.

6. Plan your foodie route with the Site Map – Browse the Site Map now >> https://kapitifoodfair.co.nz/visitors/visitor-site-map

7. Visit the Licenced Bar (EFTPOS ONLY) & Main Stage and relax over a local craft brew, wine, cocktails and delicious cider while enjoying the party vibe of the rhythmic grooves all day long! Children welcome with parent or guardian.

8. MOST vendors accept EFTPOS or bank transfer. BYO cash as there is no ATM.

INFORMATION FOR VISITORS:
#KāpitiFoodFair #FoodFestival #KFF2026 #SomethingForEveryone #VisitKāpiti

VISITOR PARKING MAP
Go to our website to view full >> https://kapitifoodfair.co.nz/visitors/visitor-info

GATE ENTRY
BUY tickets ONLINE BEFORE arriving to streamline entry and save money upfront and spend more on delicious food at the Fair! Have your tickets ready to scan at Gate Entry. Skip the queue, walk straight in with your ticket – no waiting in line at Gate Entry to buy a more expensive ticket on the day!

OR ON THE DAY, scan our ticket QR CODE on site to purchase ONLINE at Standard ticket prices:
$23 Adult, $18 Gold Card or Student ID, FREE up to 12 years.

AT GATE on the day for last minute purchase at PREMIUM prices – best option, park off site in a GOLD COIN parking zone and walk to Gate Entry if wanting to buy a ticket on the day:
$30 Adult, $25 Gold Card or Student ID, FREE up to 12 years (EFTPOS ONLY).

TRANSPORT & PARKING
Allow extra travel time as the roads will be busy with many others making their way to the Fair.

BUY VIP parking online when purchasing your tickets to access VIP parking on site at Mazengarb Reserve. Your VIP parking ticket will be scanned once you have entered Scaife Dr and will let you conveniently park all day for just $13!

NO VIP parking ticket? Head to a managed GOLD COIN parking zone shown on our PARKING MAP. Walk the short distance to the Fair and enjoy the vibe along the way with many other visitors arriving and departing!

DISABLED/MOBILITY parking is FREE and near Gate Entry 2, with parking marshals ready to assist. Let VIP parking scanners at the Scaife Dr Barrier Arm know that you need disabled/mobility parking and they will wave you through.

LOCALS: We recommend walking, running, biking (plenty of bike racks and lock-up options on site) – Or catch the train from Waikanae or Paekākāriki and board the FREE bus from Paraparaumu Station (timetable below).

HEADS UP: MEADOW COURT entry will be CLOSED, and Realm Drive car park will be OPEN as a GOLD COIN site with a fenced pathway to tarmac near Gate Entry 2.

FREEDOM CAMPING options in Kāpiti as Mazengarb Reserve is locked each night and camping is not permitted – click here >> https://www.kapiticoast.govt.nz/explore-kapiti/recreation/freedom-camping/

FREE Bus Schedule (no dogs permitted except guide dogs)
CATCH the TRAIN to Paraparaumu Station and board the FREE Bus on the half hour for a short ride to and from the Fair.

Depart Paraparaumu Station Intercity Bus Stop, Main Rd, Southbound:
10.13am, 10.43am, 11.13am, 11.43am, 12.13pm, 12.43pm, 1.13pm, 1.43pm, 2.13pm, 2.43pm, 3.13pm, 3.43pm, 4.13pm.

ENTERTAINMENT
ENJOY LIVE MUSIC all day on the Main Stage performed by exciting Kiwi bands that will have you partying to rhythmic grooves all day long! Love cooking? Visit the Seriously Pickled Kāpiti Kitchen Stage for live demos, or head to the ZEAL Zone for local talent and circus acts. There’s also a supervised FREE kids’ zone for families and plenty of roving street performers.

ON SITE
BYO cash as there is no ATM. MOST vendors accept EFTPOS or bank transfer.

Kāpiti Food Fair bags available at Gate Entry or INFO HUB for $3.

INFO HUB will operate to answer ALL visitor questions, and for LOST property, and free BAG STORAGE.

On-site paramedic for any emergency.

Flush portaloos near Gate 1 & 2 and two disabled toilets (one inside Pavilion and another accessed externally from Scaife Dr). Flush wahine/tane toilets available inside Pavilion and at some GOLD COIN parking zones (see PARKING MAP).

Crowd friendly dogs on lead are welcome – FREE water for pets and humans at the INFO Hub and Licenced Bar.

Kāpiti Food Fair Site Map is smoke & vape FREE.

LICENCED BAR
Relax in the Licenced Bar (EFTPOS ONLY) & Main Stage with a local craft brew, wine, cocktails and delicious cider. Children welcome with parent or guardian. CHEERS to that!

ENTERTAINMENT

Whether attending with friends, whānau, workmates, or a foodie tribe, there is truly something for everyone. Families can enjoy the welcoming festival atmosphere, food enthusiasts can explore emerging culinary trends, and Christmas shoppers can get a head start on seasonal gifting while stocking the pantry for summer entertaining.

The festival experience extends well beyond food. Visitors can soak up the summer vibe with live performances from exciting Kiwi bands on the Main Stage, watch talented local wahine showcase their culinary skills during inspiring cooking demonstrations, and unwind in the licensed bar before heading back out to continue their delicious adventure. Every corner of the event is designed to create joy, spark curiosity, and encourage people to connect through shared experiences.

events.name: Pinhole Photography
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Did you know that any object that can be made light tight can be turned into a camera? Come along to this Saturday workshop and work with one of our existing pinhole cameras (made from boxes, jars, teapots…) to create evocative photographs.

We’ll work in the darkroom and explore the process of loading your camera with silver gelatin paper, before making exposures in the garden around the historic Inverlochy house & garden, testing different angles and perspectives. We’ll then return to the darkroom to develop your photographic negative, and print it as a positive. You’ll leave the course with some atmospheric pinhole photographs and knowledge of how to build your own pinhole camera.

Bring a packed lunch to have in the historic Inverlochy house or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

events.long_description:
How to get people to your comedy shows using organic social media

A workshop for Wellington comics!

Most of us got into comedy to be funny on stage, not to run a social media account. But these days, getting people along to see you in person usually involves doing a bit of both.

Samantha Hannah (2026 Billy T nominee) is a stand-up comedian at night and a social media specialist by day. She's keen to share what she's learned about using organic social media to sell out shows, and to swap ideas with other comics in Wellington who are doing the same.

This is a relaxed, practical session where we'll chat about:

Ideas of what to post
Leaning into community when posting online
Turning your existing material into clips
Finding a posting rhythm that fits around your busy life and schedule
How to avoid social media burnout
Nurturing and building an audience long before telling them you have a show you want them to come watch!

All levels welcome! Advanced questions can be submitted by sending a DM via fb or Instagram (@samanthahannahcomedy). You’ll also get lots of opportunities to ask questions on the day.

All proceeds go to the Humorous Arts Trust, supporting the 2027 Wellington Raw Comedy Quest.

events.long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026
Matinee: 2:00 PM
Evening Performance: 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio and Musical Direction by Cesar Capistrano.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

Enquiries: vineyardhouse.nz@gmail.com

It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

events.name: Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mozart Requiem (Duncan Druce Completion)

Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir join forces with orchestra and soloists for a powerful performance of Mozart's final masterpiece.

When Mozart died in 1791 at the age of 35, he left the Requiem unfinished. Within months, his student Franz Xaver Süssmayr completed the work on behalf of Mozart's widow Constanze. His version became one of the most famous and beloved works in the choral repertoire and remains the version most often performed today.

Yet Mozart's surviving sketches continued to raise questions. For more than 200 years, composers and scholars have revisited them, searching for clues to how Mozart himself intended to complete the work.

This concert presents one of the most fascinating answers to that question: the Duncan Druce completion. Created in 1984 by the English composer, performer and musicologist Duncan Druce, it draws on Mozart's surviving manuscript while revisiting parts of the traditional completion. The result offers a fresh perspective on one of the defining works of the classical repertoire.

This special collaboration brings together the combined forces of Kāpiti Chorale and Capital Choir, four outstanding soloists and orchestra for two performances: Saturday 28 November at Te Raukura Performing Arts Centre, Paraparaumu, and Saturday 5 December at the Riley Centre, Wellington High School.

The programme opens with a diverse selection of choral music, including works by Mozart, Salieri, Haydn, Princess Te Rangi Pai and William Dawson, before culminating in Mozart's Requiem.

Soloists

Barbara Paterson, soprano
Ruth Armishaw, alto
Richard Taylor, tenor
Joseph Haddow, bass

This collaboration will be presented in both Kāpiti and Wellington.

Duration: Approximately 2 hours including interval.

Saturday 5 December, 7pm

Wellington Cathedral of St Paul, 2 Hill Street, Thorndon


General admission $35 (early bird price $30 until midnight 29 Nov)

Concession $30 (early bird concession price $27 until midnight 29 Nov)

School-aged children free


Nota Bene presents: Christmas Fantasia

From centuries-old texts to traditional carols given new musical life, this concert explores the many ways composers across different eras and cultures have interpreted the Christmas story.

Our programme brings together music from England to Appalachia, with works by Vaughan Williams, Warlock, Dalglish and Ešenvalds. The music ranges from reflective settings and rich harmonies to folk-inspired carols and familiar Christmas melodies.

Vaughan Williams’ Fantasia on Christmas Carols weaves together traditional English carol melodies, some emerging in the choir and others in the accompaniment. In contrast, Malcolm Dalglish’s Star in the East sets three Appalachian Christmas songs for choir and harp, drawing on a different folk tradition.

Joined by baritone Joe Haddow, harpist Michelle Velvin and organist Rachel Malcolm-Swindells, Nota Bene presents a programme that moves between familiar carols and less familiar musical settings.

And what better way to finish than by singing some favourite Christmas carols together? As is our tradition, we hope you’ll stay and join us for refreshments after the concert.

Rachel Malcolm-Swindells - Organ

Michelle Velvin - Harp

Joe Haddow - Baritone

events.long_description:
Celebrated songwriter Kristin Hersh will return to New Zealand this November / December for a run of four main centre intimate headline shows in support of her forthcoming new album Sugar On Blackstone, out 18 September via Fire Records.

Renowned for her fiercely emotional performances and uncompromising songwriting, Hersh’s New Zealand dates will see her bring songs from Sugar On Blackstone to audiences across the country alongside highlights from her extensive catalogue.

Following on from 2023’s Clear Pond Road, Sugar On Blackstone is a darker yet delicately rendered collection exploring life and death, memory, survival and human connection. Deeply personal and emotionally expansive, the album reflects on the lasting bonds between musicians, family and friends, and the way certain sounds and places can suddenly bring someone vividly back into focus.

New single ‘Dark-Eyed Junco’ offers another striking glimpse into the album, pairing lucid melodies with deeply autobiographical storytelling. Recorded at Stable Sound Studios, the album features longtime collaborators Rob Ahlers (50FOOTWAVE) on drums and Pete Harvey (Throwing Muses) on cello.

Long celebrated as one of alternative music’s most singular voices, Hersh continues to deliver performances that are both intensely intimate and disarmingly powerful - a rare opportunity to experience one of modern music’s most influential songwriters up close.

KRISTIN HERSH Sugar on Blackstone New Zealand 2026 TOUR

South Island /Te Waipounamu shows with ‘On The Door Dunedin’
Sat 28 Nov – Ravensbourne Hall Dunedin 8pm
Sun 29 Nov – A Rolling Stone Christchurch 5 pm

North Island / Te Ika-a-Māui Shows with Plus1:
Fri 4 Dec – Kāhui, St David’s (70 Khyber Pass) 8 pm
Sat Dec 5 - Meow, Wellington 8 pm

Tickets on sale via onthedoor.nz & www.plus1.co.nz

Tui Brewery Express: The Ultimate Christmas Party!
Climb aboard The Tui Express for the ultimate end of year office Christmas party! This is the perfect workplace celebration that beats the standard corporate dinner, making it an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages. It’s the ultimate way to reward your hardworking team, swap out the boring boardroom, thank your favorite clients, and celebrate the year's wins with a spectacular Sunday on the rails.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to capture an epic, casual end of year team photo than from our open air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for ditching the laptops, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.

The festive celebrations start the second you step on board! Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. Your crew can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non alcoholic refreshments to toast to your Q4 wins, along with hot espresso coffees and plenty of food, sweet treats, and snacks right from the rails as the stunning scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15 minute walk to the world famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for your group. Once at the brewery, relax and toast to your team's successes in the iconic historic grounds. Forget the awkward office Secret Santa and the sad boardroom sausage rolls, your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non alcoholic alternative) to celebrate a successful year together!

Your ticket covers your return journey from your chosen departure station in beautifully appointed premium carriages alongside exclusive rail only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open air viewing platform for unbeatable team bonding, sightseeing, and staff photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling drinks, coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared festive BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

events.name: Sea Glass Jewellery Workshop
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Design and create a unique ring with foraged sea glass ‘gems’ while learning and developing core jewellery fabrication techniques. An opportunity to engage in creative recycling by turning seaside flotsam into precious wearable treasures. Experiment with ring textures and forms in silver, brass and/or copper, then set your unique glass ‘gemstone’. Finish up with your choice of polish, including high lustre gloss, steel brushed satin, or darkened antique finishes.

If you can, please beachcomb and bring along some sea glass options - ideally around 1cm wide, and with a flat back. Glass provided if you are in need.

Techniques:

Create a ring with one bezel set foraged sea glass ‘gem’
Use jeweller’s callipers to measure and prepare metal
Use jeweller’s saws or snips to cut and shape metal
Use files and sanding to refine and smooth metal edges and surfaces
Use jeweller’s flame torches to solder join metal pieces
Use Dremel & bench polishers to refine & finish metal casts into wearable jewellery

Materials: Sea Glass, Copper, Brass, Sterling Silver

Project : 1 Ring with sea glass

Includes Silver, Brass and Copper options

events.long_description:
Finish the year feeling grounded, energised, and ready to shine your light through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

Celebrate the completion of our Journey Through the Chakras with a special afternoon dedicated to the Aura (the Eighth Chakra) through the transformative practices of Kundalini Yoga and the deeply restorative sounds of a Gong Bath.

The Aura is your energetic field—the subtle electromagnetic energy that surrounds your body. A strong, balanced aura helps you feel grounded, confident, resilient, and protected, allowing you to move through life with greater vitality and ease. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll strengthen this energetic field, leaving you feeling centred, uplifted, and radiant.

Whether you've joined us throughout the chakra series or this is your first workshop, you're warmly welcome. Come and finish the year feeling grounded, energised, and ready to shine your light into the world.

Kundalini Yoga | 1:30pm – 3:00pm | Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to strengthen and balance your aura through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.
Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm | Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.
Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm | Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.

Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.

Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.
Bring an open heart, a yoga mat, blanket, water bottle and anything you need to feel cozy + supported.
Whether you're joining the entire afternoon or just one session, you'll leave feeling calmer, clearer, and more deeply connected to yourself.

Spaces are limited, so bookings are recommended.

Investment:

$35 Yoga | $30 Gong Bath | $55 Both

Special discounted ticket option: $100 two person special - bring a friend with you to attend the yoga and the gong session. Must select this ticket option for the discount to apply (i.e. both people must book together)

If you want to pay by cash on the day or by bank transfer, please send an email to mel@prosperityyoga.co.nz to book your place.

events.name: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel
events.venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
events.long_description:
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice
