events.name: Arahina Mai Tour - Hine + Jullekke + Casual Healing
events.venue: St Peters Village Hall, Cnr Beach Rd and Ames St, Paekākāriki
events.long_description:
Nau mai to this special triple line up collaboration between soulful songstresses Julia Cooper (Jullekke & Dr Reknaw) and Gigi Crayford (Hine) alongside Nikau Te Huki (Casual Healing) in a stripped back, intimate and spellbinding solo setting. Sit back, take a breath and ground into a night of medicine music.

Julia Cooper is an Aotearoa singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Best known as the front woman and co-founder of Aotearoa’s well loved band ‘Dr Reknaw’. Julia has recently birthed her solo project ‘Jullekke’. She is recognised for her smooth, velvety & sultry vocal tones, catchy trance bass and guitar riff. Her lyricism features an ethereal quality mixed with messages of empowerment, consciousness and healing. With flavours of roots, soul, world tastes and funk. Julia describes her music as “vibrational food for the soul of listeners. Melodies to gift and uplift”.

CASUAL HEALING - Nikau Te Huki is a unique composer, producer and multi-instrumentalist based in Pōneke, Aotearoa - and his soulful solo project goes by the name of Casual Healing. As a true sonic missionary, Nikau is creating a soothing “golden-era sound” as part of his mission to heal with his music. The songs of Casual Healing emphasise life lessons of aroha, peace and unity through powerful lyrical scribe woven into smooth reggae, soul rhythm. This infusion creates a unique nostalgic vibe, creating a captivating and comforting essence that evokes recollections of moments shared with friends and whānau. Casual Healing's goal is to create songs that “make people feel like they want to be better people”, drawing inspiration from Bob Marley, who showed us the power of compassion and simplicity.

Nau Mai ki te Ao o HINE - A Māori witch folk noir weaving of Taonga Pūoro, sonic storytelling & poetry. This enchanting songstress radiates strength through vulnerability & the connections awakened from returning to our roots. A blend of Te Reo Māori & English, this powerful set will echo through your bones & reverberate your soul. HINE recently released her debut EP 'KA MUA KA MURI' with a national tour, leading the EP to place #1 on the Aotearoa Official Top Charts. This will be HINE’s last tour of the North Island before a move to Ōtautahi and then travel internationally.

Arahina Mai meaning ‘Guide Me” speaks to the artist's devotion to spirit through their craft and devotional practice of music & art as ritual & medicine. This show will be a deeply intimate, intentional & community centric setting of heart & healing.

Shows include:

5th Dec - Pōneke Wellington at a secret location
6th Dec - Paekākāriki at St Peters Village Hall
8th Dec - Whanganui at Private Residence
10th Dec - Raglan Arts Centre
11th Dec - Thames - Buddhist Church
13th Dec - Tāmaki - Auckland Unitarian Church
17th Dec - Oakura - Dawn
18th Dec - Napier (Gigi & Aslan) Paisley Stage (No Julia)
19th Dec - Opunake Playhouse Theatre

Ali Whitton is a New Zealand-born, Yorkshire-raised singer-songwriter whose music is deeply influenced by the landscapes of both countries. events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

About the Liner Shipping Game

The Liner Shipping Game is a cutting-edge, simulation-based training solution that provides hands-on insights into the intricacies of liner shipping operations. It simplifies real-world processes, making it suitable for both industry newcomers and seasoned professionals.

Participants navigate realistic, customisable scenarios reflecting operational disruptions, key decision points, and challenges.

Key features include:

Booking Uptake: Manage dynamic booking requests while balancing capacity constraints and customer expectations.

Vessel Stowage: Plan and optimise vessel space, considering cargo types, weight distribution, and voyage schedules.

Terminal Operations: Coordinate port activities, manage container flows, and ensure efficient cargo handling.

The game's interactive nature provides practical experience and enhances skills in teamwork, revenue management, and process optimisation

.

For a closer look at the LinerGame experience, watch our official highlight video on YouTube.

Why Attend?

The Liner Shipping Game offers a rare opportunity to learn from top-tier industry experts while collaborating with peers from across the logistics sector. By attending, you will:

Understand Complex Operations: Experience the decision-making process of running a liner shipping service, covering end-to-end operations.

Enhance Your Skills: Improve your teamwork, strategic thinking, and revenue management capabilities in a fast-paced, risk-free environment.

Navigate Real-World Scenarios: Encounter challenges like port strikes, equipment shortages, weather disruptions, and overlapping booking regions, gaining critical insights into effective problem-solving.

Network with Industry Peers: Connect with like-minded professionals in a collaborative setting, exchange ideas, and explore new opportunities within the shipping and logistics sector.

Who Should Attend?

This workshop is ideal for:

Logistics & Supply Chain Professionals: Individuals involved in operations, planning, and management.

Importers & Exporters: Professionals managing supply chain activities and interested in gaining a broader understanding of liner shipping dynamics.

Freight Forwarders & Shippers: Those seeking to enhance their service offerings by understanding carrier operations better.

Port & Terminal Operators: Professionals responsible for terminal management and coordination.

Shipping Lines & Carriers: Executives and teams who want to refine their strategies and processes.

New York hardcore that’s been flipping off the purists for nearly 20 years.

Blast it with jazz horns. Get it plucked to buggery by banjo (yes, hardcore banjo!). Have a good old stomp in the riff swamp and chug out an irrefutable melody. Keep it dynamic and stab it with venom.

Formed back in 2009, Show Me The Body put the sludge back in the morass of modern life.  

Wielding a clash of banjos, bass, drums and electronics, each song seems to gain gears. From slow burners to crashing crescendoes, and a fresh album in tow that ups the ante and draws a new line in the sand.

Dancing at the end of the end. Under the overpass, down the alley, in the basement.

Joining Show Me The Body at all headline shows is Evanora: Unlimited is a multi-medium project from Oakland, California artist Orion Ohana.

Emerging from South Central Los Angeles in the early '90s, they rewrote the rules with their wit, originality and unmistakable chemistry, delivering two of the most influential albums of the era.
From the platinum-selling Bizarre Ride II the Pharcyde to the genre-defining Labcabincalifornia, classics like "Passin' Me By," "Runnin'," "Drop," "Otha Fish" and "Ya Mama" continue to inspire generations of artists and remain essential listening more than 30 years later.
The Pharcyde's legacy extends far beyond their own catalogue. They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.
Secure your tickets early and don't miss the opportunity to see true pioneers of alternative hip hop when they return this December.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Former Haas F1 boss Guenther Steiner brings his new live show, ‘No Team Orders’, to The Opera House in Wellington. The 2026 season gave Formula 1 new cars, new rules, and new teams on the grid. Days after the final race, Guenther unpacks it all. He shares his take on which teams cracked the rule changes first and which young drivers stood out. Expect blunt opinions and stories from inside the paddock. 

Guenther has spent more than 30 years in motorsport. He started in rallying, working with drivers such as Colin McRae, a three-time Rally New Zealand winner. He later ran Jaguar Racing in Formula 1. Then he built the Haas team from scratch and led it for a decade. You might have seen him on the Netflix series ‘Formula 1: Drive to Survive’, where his colourful honesty made him a fan favourite. He famously claims he has never watched it. He has also written two books, ‘Surviving to Drive’ and ‘Unfiltered’. Today, he is CEO of the Red Bull KTM Tech3 MotoGP team. 

The evening is a live conversation on stage, followed by an audience Q&A. Bring a question of your own and put it to Guenther directly. Join whether you’ve just discovered him or you’ve followed Formula 1 since you were a wee one. Book your seats, and leave with enough insider secrets to impress at the work Christmas party.

Grief touches every life, yet each person's journey through loss is unique, and Christmas can be a time when we feel loss most acutely. Whether you have experienced a bereavement, the end of a relationship, or a significant shift in your life, this gentle weekend retreat offers a sacred space to pause, reflect, and find companionship on the path of healing.

Drawing on the Exploring Seasons of Grief programme, participants will explore grief as a natural and evolving process, much like the changing seasons of the year.

Through reflection, guided conversation, quiet time, and the peaceful surroundings of the Home of Compassion, we will consider the many ways grief can affect our hearts, relationships, faith, and sense of identity. Whether your loss is recent or long ago, this retreat invites you to acknowledge your experience with compassion, deepen your understanding of living with loss, and discover sources of hope and renewal.

UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

Build Your Own Bánh Mì: Creative Vietnamese Fillings

What makes a great Bánh Mì? Is it the crispy baguette, the fresh herbs, the tangy pickles, or the delicious fillings?

In this hands-on workshop, you'll discover the endless possibilities of Vietnam's most famous sandwich by learning how to prepare a variety of popular Bánh Mì fillings, including:

🥖 Pan-Style Eggs (Bánh Mì Chảo)
🥖 Pork Meatballs (Xíu Mại)
🥖 Canned Fish in Tomato Sauce
🥖 Grilled Pork
🥖 Fish Cakes
🥖 Fresh herbs, pickled vegetables, and flavourful sauces

Mix and match different ingredients to create your own perfect Bánh Mì while learning the techniques and stories behind this beloved Vietnamese street food.

Whether you're a long-time Bánh Mì fan or trying it for the first time, this workshop is a fun and interactive way to explore the flavours, creativity, and culture behind one of Vietnam's most iconic dishes.

What you'll get

✔ Hands-on cooking experience
✔ Recipes to take home
✔ Your own customised Bánh Mì creations
✔ Insights into Vietnamese food culture

Facilitator

This workshop is facilitated by Yung Nguyen from I Love Vietfood, in partnership with Viet Hub NZ.

Supporting Community Through Food

Your registration fee helps provide a koha for our facilitator and supports Viet Hub NZ's community initiatives, including free community meals, cultural activities, and educational programmes.

Come hungry, get creative, and build your perfect Bánh Mì!

events.long_description:
Whitireia Park Community Snorkel - FREE
Dive in with us this summer! 🌊

Discover the underwater world of Whitireia Park at our free community snorkelling event! Explore beautiful seagrass beds, rocky reefs and the marine life that calls them home — you might even spot a seahorse!

🐠 Everyone welcome, including beginners!

We provide all the snorkelling gear and experienced guides to help you enjoy a safe and memorable experience in the water.

A few things to know:

Participants must be aged 8+ and confident swimmers.

Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an adult who also takes part in the snorkel.

Bring your togs, towel, refreshments and anything else you need to enjoy a day by the coast.

🤿 How to take part

Registrations open at 9.45am on the day. Come along to book your snorkel time — spots may fill up quickly!

Each tour takes approximately 1 hour and 30 minutes, including getting ready, snorkelling and returning your gear afterwards. The last tour departs at 1.45pm.

Make a day of it and enjoy exploring the coast and taking part in other activities!

This free event is brought to you in partnership with Greater Wellington Regional Council.

📍 Getting there

By bike: Why not enjoy the beautiful coastal track? It's approximately 5km from Titahi Bay Boat Club to the snorkel site.

By car: The road to the snorkel site is narrow and can be challenging when traffic is busy. Where possible, please carpool and drive carefully. Clearly signposted parking will be available throughout the day.


🌦️ Weather and event updates

Snorkelling is weather-dependent, and events may be cancelled, postponed or moved to another location. Please check this Mountains to Sea Wellington Facebook event listing for updates before heading out.

................................................................................................................................

This snorkelling event is delivered under the national Mountains to Sea Conservation Trust's Experiencing Marine Reserves programme.

The programme is Adventure Activity Certified (AA0534).

Photo Credit: Red Beanie Photography

events.name: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington

events.long_description:
Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington
Celebrate the richness and wonder of Christmas with Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington, as they join forces for an evening of music that spans centuries, crosses continents and brings together joyful celebration and quiet reflection.

Conducted by Ingrid Schoenfeld, who directs both, the two choirs will be accompanied by well-known organists Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting. Together, they bring a wealth of musical experience to a programme filled with colour, contrast and seasonal spirit.

At the heart of the concert is Cantata V of J.S. Bach’s Christmas Oratorio, opening with the chorus Ehre sei dir, Gott, gesungen. This part of Bach’s great Christmas work follows the journey of the Magi, exploring their search for the newborn Jesus and the image of light shining through darkness. Its combination of exuberant choral writing, storytelling and reflection offers a vivid encounter with the Christmas narrative.

Felix Mendelssohn’s Die deutsche Liturgie brings another dimension to the evening. Its Kyrie, Gloria and Sanctus move from prayerful appeal to praise and adoration, revealing the composer’s gift for expressive melody and beautifully shaped choral textures. These three movements offer moments of warmth, grandeur and stillness.

Music from Aotearoa New Zealand has a special place in this concert. Jonathan Berkahn’s Four Christmas Songs brings together Unto us a Son is given, Meditation – rorate coeli desuper, And art thou come with us to dwell? and How sweet the angels song. The sequence invites listeners to consider Christmas through proclamation, contemplation and a sense of wonder. With Berkahn also appearing as one of the evening’s organists, the concert offers a particularly personal connection between the music and its composer.

Jenny McLeod’s Vulcan and Indigo II, from her Sun Festival Carols, add further New Zealand colour.

Philip Stopford’s Lully, Lulla, Lullay provides a tender, haunting contrast. Drawing on the Coventry Carol text, it captures both the intimacy of a lullaby and the poignancy beneath the Christmas story. John Gardner’s Tomorrow shall be my dancing day brings buoyant rhythm and infectious vitality, while Mykola Leontovich’s Carol of the Bells sparkles with its familiar repeating motif and gathering excitement.

From Bach’s joyful praise to the delicacy of a lullaby, this programme offers much to discover and enjoy.

St James’ Anglican Church in Lower Hutt provides a welcoming setting, with comfortable seating and a crisp acoustic in which to savour the combined voices and accompaniment.

Make time in the busy December season for an evening of shared listening, musical discovery and festive warmth. Join Festival Singers of Wellington, Cantoris, Ingrid Schoenfeld, Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting for Bach, Bells and Christmas: a celebration of the season through the expressive power of choral music.

[Children 18 years and under enter free when accompanied by a paying adult.]

Dementia Wellington invites you to celebrate the 80th anniversary of Frank Capra's inspiring Christmas classic It’s a Wonderful Life with your whānau and friends in the lavish Embassy Theatre.

Proceeds from this event will help Dementia Wellington provide community-based specialised support services for those experiencing dementia across the wider Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington area.

A fundraising afternoon tea will be served from 2:30pm. Seasonal, Tiered Cake Stands containing goodies and treats can be purchased to take into the Movie for sharing and enjoying. Your stand will be disassembled, wrapped and bagged for you to take home.

"My thanks go to you, young and old, for supporting Dementia Wellington with our work. Your generosity, as always, makes such a difference. Our team looks forward to seeing you on 13 December at this celebrated Christmas holiday tradition. My very best wishes."

Stephanie Clare, Chief Executive, Dementia Wellington

We look forward to enjoying this very special film with you and your loved ones this December in support of Dementia Wellington and encourage you to spread the word!

Two great events, one festive Sunday at Trentham Racecourse!

We've combined our Christmas Picnic at the Races with the Upper Hutt Night Market, bringing you an afternoon and evening packed with racing, Christmas cheer, local shopping, delicious food and entertainment for the whole family.

The racing kicks off at approximately 1pm, with a relaxed afternoon of thoroughbred racing, lawn games and plenty of free family fun. Bring a picnic or grab a bite from the food trucks, find a spot on the front lawn and enjoy all the festivities, including a visit from Santa, lolly scramble, tug of war and sack races.

Then, from 4pm to 8pm, the Upper Hutt Night Market comes to life!

It's the perfect opportunity to support local and tick off some of that last-minute Christmas shopping! Browse a fantastic range of local vendors offering everything from handmade jewellery, candles and homewares to artwork, clothing, plants and unique gifts.

You'll also find a great selection of food trucks serving up a variety of delicious options, alongside live music and entertainment to keep the festive atmosphere going into the evening.
Whether you're joining us for the racing, the Night Market or making a full day of it, there's something for everyone!

events.long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

The calendar year is nearly done, the dashboards are probably still open, and your Q4 pipeline has either been heroic, character-building, or both. Either way, it’s time to down tools and come hang with the SaaS squad.

Join us for our SaaSmas Party in Wellington — a relaxed, mildly ridiculous, very well-earned night with the people building, scaling, funding, selling, marketing, supporting and generally holding together SaaS companies across Aotearoa.

Location: Dockside bar, Wellington

events.name: Somatic Breathwork Journey
events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Amy Webber and Mangaroa Farms for a journey into your breath.

Somatic Breathwork™ is a full embodiment experience designed to help you release stress, trauma, emotions and stuck energy from the body. This is a modality that utilizes your own breath to help shed the layers of yourself that no longer serve, making room for you to call in what will help facilitate change within your life.

Somatic Breathwork™ uses a consciously connected breath pattern to help you tap into your body's innate inner intelligence and find the areas that need clearing. Coupling the breath with immersive music may result in different forms of cathartic emotional releases such as laughing, moving, crying, yelling, and shaking. All forms of expression are encouraged as it allows the body to move any pent up energy and create space for the second half of the breathwork journey.

A gentler breathing technique is used in the second half of the session to help you connect with who you truly are. Together we can use the breath to call in how you want to show up in the world, the changes you want to make, and allow you to see clearly what it would be like to live your best life.

Join Amy Webber and Mangaroa Farms for this immersive journey into your mind and heart. Any questions, please email amy@mangaroa.org

North Pole Express Kapiti: 10am - Saturday, 19 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis

events.name: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky
events.venue: Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton
events.long_description:
Spend an evening under one of the world’s finest dark skies and learn how to photograph the Milky Way, constellations and deep-sky objects. This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.

events.venue: Paraparaumu Train Station,Amohia St, Paraparaumu, New Zealand
events.long_description:
North Pole Express Kapiti: 1pm - Sunday, 20 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis

events.venue: Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Race Of Champions is an internationally renowned event. Winners from a range of racing disciplines go head-to-head on a purpose-built tarmac circuit constructed inside Hnry Stadium. Unlike traditional motorsport events, every driver competes in identical cars, putting the focus firmly on skill behind the wheel. 

The first drivers confirmed for Wellington include four-time Formula 1 World Champion Sebastian Vettel and Formula 1 race winner Valtteri Bottas. Supercars champion Chaz Mostert and New Zealand rally star Hayden Paddon are also coming. More competitors are to be announced for this Wellington exclusive event. 

Since its launch in 1988, Race Of Champions has brought together stars from Formula 1, World Rally Championship, IndyCar, NASCAR, Le Mans, and other top-tier racing series. Previous competitors have included Fernando Alonso, Lando Norris, Valentino Rossi, Mika Häkkinen, and Michael Schumacher.

events.venue: 27 Hillary Court, Naenae, Lower Hutt 5011,27 Hillary Ct, Naenae, Lower Hutt 5011, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | Vietnamese New Year Rice Cake Workshop
🧧 GÓI BÁNH XUÂN 2027 | VIETNAMESE NEW YEAR RICE CAKE WORKSHOP

🍃 Wrap a cake, share a story, and celebrate Vietnamese traditions together!

Tết không chỉ là dịp đón năm mới mà còn là lúc gia đình sum vầy, cùng nhau gìn giữ và trao truyền những nét đẹp văn hoá Việt Nam.

Have you ever wondered how traditional Vietnamese rice cakes are made? Or perhaps you miss the familiar feeling of preparing bánh chưng and bánh tét with your family back home?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a hands-on cultural cooking workshop where we come together to discover the stories, traditions and flavours of Vietnamese Lunar New Year.

🌸 WHAT WILL WE EXPLORE?

🍃 Bánh Chưng – Traditional square sticky rice cake, symbolising the Earth and gratitude to our ancestors.

🍃 Bánh Tét – A cylindrical sticky rice cake commonly enjoyed during Tết, particularly in Southern Vietnam.

🍃 Bánh Ú – A pyramid-shaped sticky rice cake wrapped in leaves, representing another beautiful part of Vietnamese culinary heritage.

During the workshop, you will:

🌱 Discover the cultural stories and meanings behind traditional Vietnamese rice cakes.

🌱 Learn about ingredients and traditional wrapping techniques.

🌱 Enjoy a hands-on experience guided by our facilitator, Yung Nguyen.

🌱 Connect with families, friends and community members through food and storytelling.

🌱 Create meaningful memories while helping pass Vietnamese traditions to the next generation.

No cooking experience needed! Whether you're Vietnamese, have children curious about their heritage, or simply love exploring different cultures, everyone is welcome.

📅 EVENT DETAILS

Date: Saturday, 16 January 2027

Venue: Te Mako Naenae Community Centre, Lower Hutt

Facilitator: Yung Nguyen

Organiser: Viet Hub NZ

🎟️ Spaces are limited. Registration is essential.

💛 MORE THAN JUST A COOKING WORKSHOP

For many Vietnamese families living overseas, the scent of sticky rice, the sound of leaves being folded and the joy of preparing food together bring back precious memories of home.

For our younger generation, this is an opportunity to discover where they come from, connect with their roots and create their own Tết memories.

And for our wider New Zealand community, it's an invitation to experience the warmth, stories and traditions of Vietnamese culture.

Because traditions are not only something we remember. They are something we share, practise and pass on.

Come wrap a cake, share a story and welcome Tết 2027 with us! 🧧

Viet Hub NZ | Registered Charity CC64272

Uplifting Culture. Creating Opportunity. Empowering People. Together.

#VietHubNZ #GoiBanhXuan2027 #VietnameseNewYear #Tet2027 #VietnameseCulture #LowerHutt #WellingtonEvents #VietCuisine

events.long_description:
Tora Bombora - 2027
The Return of Tora Bombora.

Wellington Anniversary Weekend, 22 - 24 January, 2027

After five incredible festivals and a four year hiatus, Tora Bombora is returning for the sixth edition - Tora Bombora Ono

For four summers, the paddocks sat quietly. The stages slept, the winds kept moving across the hills, and the coast returned to its familiar rhythm. But some things never really leave. They simply wait.

————————————————————

Ticket System and Key Dates

'Tora Bombora Whānau'
To keep the community close and the kaupapa even closer, if you have attended Tora Bombora in the past, you are already 'Tora Bombora Whānau' which gives you first access to tickets (keep an eye on your inbox). The remaining tickets will be released to people who sign up via our website to become a part of the 'Tora Bombora Whānau'.

How it works
1. Enter 'Tora Bombora Whānau': Sign up to the Tora Bombora waiting list and join the whānau before the link closes.
Link opens Monday, 6th July.
Link closes Sunday, 9th August.

2. Keep an eye on your inbox: Once the link has closed, you'll receive an email with a 'Tora Bombora Whānau' access code that gives you access to purchase tickets to Tora Bombora before they are released to the general public. Each whānau member may purchase up to four tickets.
Whānau ticket access and lineup out 10th August

3. General ticket release
Tuesday, 11th August - If any tickets remain after the whānau link has been sent out, they will be released in a public sale.

If this sounds like your kind of gig, put your name in the hat. The coast will do the rest.
All other info can be found at www.torabombora.co.nz

————————————————————

CAMPING: This is included in your ticket price. The festival begins at 3.00 pm Friday the 20th Jan. The camping zone will be situated on-site, right on the Pacific Ocean where you can swim, fish, surf, play and chill out.

FOOD AND SHOPS: Tora is isolated. This means no shops for 45 minutes so please make sure you bring more than enough food and gear as Martinborough is the nearest town. There will be plenty of food trucks at the event.

————————————————————

Festival Terms & Conditions:

*THIS IS AN R18 EVENT & RIGHT OF ADMISSION IS RESERVED.

**WASTE POLICY IS BRING YOUR OWN, TAKE YOUR OWN.

————————————————————

LOCATION

313 Te Awaiti Road, Tora Beach, Martinborough, South Wairarapa, Wellington, 5782

Drive time from Wellington: 2 hours 15mins.

events.long_description:
Summer Meltdown '27

SUMMER MELTDOWN - We're set to ignite your summer with an unforgettable fusion of sound, energy, and culture.

﻿

Bringing you a powerhouse lineup featuring Aotearoa's most iconic artists, SIX60, Katchafire, The Black Seeds, Troy Kingi, Ria Hall and Tiki Taane. This is the moment music fans have been waiting for - and the countdown to one of summer's biggest festivals starts right now!

﻿

TICKET DATES

Pre-sale: Thursday 10th Sept, 8am

Public Sale: Friday 11th Sept, 8am

﻿

SIX60

Returning to Wellington for the first time in 2 years to headline Summer Meltdown, SIX60's story has always felt larger than life, and their music even more so. What began as Dunedin flatmates jamming for fun has evolved into a sound that's unmistakably their own. Get ready for a full-scale spectacle of inescapable anthems.




KATCHAFIRE

Katchafire's journey from the mighty H-Town to the world stage is rooted in pure Māori pride and classic reggae spirit. Blending vibrant rhythms and uplifting grooves with cultural depth, Katchafire bring an authentic, soul-soaked reggae experience to Summer Meltdown.




THE BLACK SEEDS

Returning to their Wellington roots, The Black Seeds bring their reputation for irresistible grooves, signature warmth, rhythm and world-class energy to the Summer Meltdown stage with a live show that hits with big-beat funk, dub, soul and roots-reggae.

﻿

TROY KINGI

One of Aoteraroa's most creative artists, Troy Kingi's 10/10/10 project - ten albums, ten genres, ten years - has earned major accolades and cemented his position as a fearless creative force. Performing with his live band, The Cactus Handshake, Kingi brings a genre-shifting, bold and boundary-defying show to Brewtown.




RIA HALL

One of the country's most compelling voices, Ria Hall effortlessly blends hip-hop, reggae, soul, dancehall ragga and modern beats into a sound that's vibrant and fearless. A powerful live performer shaped by kapa haka and dedicated to elevating te reo Māori, Ria delivers a fierce and deeply soulful set.




TIKI TAANE

With a career that has been defined by innovation, creativity and a deep connection to live performance, Tiki Taane is undoubtedly one of Aotearoa's most influential and versatile artists. When Tiki steps onto the Summer Meltdown stage he'll unleash an immersive, live looping, high-energy one man band set that showcases the iconic energy that has made him a cornerstone of New Zealand music.




Summer Meltdown 2027

Huge anthems, massive performances, and a full-throttle celebration of the music that makes New Zealand unique.




Saturday 23rd January.

All Ages.

Afterpay available.




﻿

events.long_description:
A recent review by 13thfloor.co.nz of a Pachyman set at Whammy celebrated the way Pachy used his magic sound to "immediately create a space nobody wanted to leave". We didn't want him to leave either, so we're bringing him back to Aotearoa this January. On Sunday 24 January he takes over Pōneke's hallowed San Fran for a double header with Trans-Tasman supergroup The Lahaar.

Over four albums, Pachyman has proven himself a dedicated craftsman in the lineage of dub reggae. He has mastered the methods of King Tubby and Scientist: vintage gear, glorious walls of sound, and an intuitive grasp of the power of repetition. Since his triumphant last visit in early 2025, Pachy "Pachyman" Garcia has released what critics are calling his most adventurous record yet, the dubtastic Another Place. On it he brings together the many scenes that have recontextualised dub, from the synth-pop of William Onyeabor and Yellow Magic Orchestra to Basic Channel's amniotic dub techno. With even stronger Latin flavours running through his sublime Lovers Rock and Studio One-inspired sounds, this will be a supercharged version of the Pachyman shows we've seen before.

Standing toe to toe with him are The Lahaar. The band brings together some of the brightest lights of the Australian and New Zealand jazz and electronic soul scenes: Julien Dyne, Horatio Luna and Lachlan Stuckey (Surprise Chef), and a revolving cast featuring members of Fat Freddy's Drop, The Circling Sun and Avantdale Bowling Club. Their self-titled debut on the UK's Soundway Records draws on late-'70s New York proto-rap disco instrumentals, Nigerian boogie, Jamaican dub and vintage cop-movie funk. Live, they're a full-blown big band of horns, flutes, vibraphone and congas, moving from high-energy percussive dance-floor heat into deep, meditative dub. It's the perfect match for Pachy's dubwise science.

Two headline acts and one very big night. Don't sleep on it.

"Pachyman is not to be slept on" – Aquarium Drunkard




San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

The good times man is back! One-man Puerto Rican dub-reggae soundsystem Pachyman is making his way down for four beautiful shows this January. And, if you missed out on Tora Bombora tickets, this is your chance to catch two of the big names on the bill on the capital’s favourite stage.

“What Pachyman is doing is too fresh to ignore, crossing enough lines that even the most cynical reggae skeptic will find plenty to enjoy here” - POPMATTERS

Over four albums, Pachyman has proven himself a dedicated craftsman working in the lineage of dub reggae while mastering the methodology of masters like King Tubby and Scientist, using vintage gear, constructing glorious walls of sound, and developing an intuitive understanding of the power of repetition. With Another Place, he synthesizes the myriad scenes that have recontextualized dub, from the synth-pop of William Onyeabor and Yellow Magic Orchestra to Basic Channel’s amniotic dub techno. Featuring even stronger Latin flavours infused through his sublime Lover’s Rock and Studio One inspired sounds, this will be a supercharged version of the Pachyman shows we’ve seen in the past.

events.name: An evening with David Sedaris
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
He’s been referred to as the God of the comic essay. Author David Sedaris is a savant of sardonic wit. Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   
In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Doors Open: 5:30pm

Show Start: 6:30pm




Granted furlough from the gulag, Daft Rocket is crossing the ditch in 2027 and heading to Auckland for the first time with riffs in tow. His first trip Down Under was a sold out scorcher across Sydney, Brisbane, and Melbourne in 2025. Now, The Boy Who Riffed is bringing his frenetic, spellbound optimism to the information chamber of this haunted planet we call home. This month-long trek will span 17 shows across 11 cities throughout Australia and New Zealand - creating a rift in the space time continuum that may take decades to amend. Mostly improvised, rarely sanctified, and remarkably canonized, this mercurial hour of standup comedy is sure to bring families together around a yule log of proficient proletariat rhetoric that neither holds firm a universal truth or chooses to establish a solid foundation as to the nature of words in general. Ultimately: it's riffing, it's good for us, and we're just as happy with a good book - we shudder to consider it any other way.

events.name: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington
events.venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Home Alone Music is proud to announce the Aotearoa and Australian tour in celebration of Timothy Blackman's new album 'Between the Islands' (HAM050) in January/February 2027.  

In Aotearoa, there will be full band shows in Wellington and Palmerston North. 

For the full band shows, Timothy's backing band will consist of Tessa Dillion on bass/backing vocals (Mystery Waitress and Tessa de Lyon) and Olivia Campion on drums (Mystery Waitress and Yumi Zouma).

Between the Islands was recorded with a live studio band consisting of Blackman, Tessa Dillon (Mystery Waitress), and Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (French for Rabbits, Dateline). Lee Prebble recorded and mixed their performances at The Surgery Recording Studio in Omāroro, Newtown, Wellington over three days in May 2025. Additional overdubs were performed and recorded by Blackman’s longtime collaborator Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) at her home in Wellington. The album was mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago, Illinois.  Album artwork by Alex Thornton.  


----

Timothy Blackman is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington based singer-songwriter, recording artist and founder of independent Aotearoa New Zealand record label Home Alone.

Since his first EP in 2006, Blackman has released a string of acclaimed records such as Modern Sprawl, I've Never Lived, Everyone Needs Something to Hold On To and Brightest Days. Blackman grew up in the Wellington region, began playing violin at five and guitar at ten, and was performing in bands around the Lower Hutt/Wellington area as a teenager. 

His music has since taken him from the bedrooms and small venues of Aotearoa to stages across Europe, the UK, United States and Australia, where he has performed alongside artists including The Mountain Goats and Scout Niblett. His music sits in an intimate space, flitting somewhere between the introspective songwriting of Bill Callahan and Bonnie Prince Billy, and the DIY spirit of New Zealand icon Chris Knox. His songs are personal and unvarnished: thoughtful, melancholic and often quietly funny, with a fascination for place, memory, displacement and the strange details of everyday life.

In January 2025, Alex Cameron exploded his life in a controlled detonation largely ignored by the universe. No one was safe. And nobody noticed. The charred remains of Cameron’s life fragmented and reassembled into 9 synthetic rock songs detailing his world’s deep confusion and regret. He continues to find pieces of his own reflection in the shattered characters he creates and embodies. Their yearnings and their humiliations. The promised Messiah. Agamemnon’s appetite for war. Mel Gibson’s ransom note. Humanity’s Pro-War destiny. A cold war breakup. This is the sound of a man walking out on somebody else’s family. Into a new world afraid to remember what it used to be. These are songs of protest against life itself. This is the world our fathers feared. And here is its soundtrack.




ALEX CAMERON

US comedy legend, Josh Wolf, returns to NZ with his brand-new show, Touring Hard!

His fourth time touring Aotearoa, Josh will be bringing his hilarious stories and unbelievable yarns to Wellington’s Meow Nui this February for one-night-only! Promising a night of absolute mayhem and non-stop laughter, Josh will be accompanied by his son, Jacob – with the two delivering their latest show that will entertain the sweaty summer pants off you!

A stand-up comedian for more than three decades, Josh Wolf is also a heralded writer, actor, and New York Times best-selling author. His comedy roots trace back to Boston and Seattle, eventually leading him to open for the likes of industry pillars such as Larry the Cable Guy and Chelsea Handler. After years of touring, writing, and performing, Josh has established himself as one of the most respected comedians in the industry, continuing to headline sold-out theaters across North America, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe.

Fresh off the heels of his “High On Life Tour”, Josh rolled out his most recent special, “The Campfire Special” which blends music and comedy and features an array of special guests. The special marked his fourth in the past six years, further solidifying his prolific career and rabid fanbase. Josh’s brand-new show now sees him touring internationally through 2026 & 2027, hitting the US, Canada, Europe, UK and now Australia and NZ. In addition to touring, Wolf has a weekly residency at Jimmy Kimmel’s Comedy Club in Las Vegas where he performs every Sunday and Monday night to a packed house.

With over 7.4 million followers across social platforms, and more than 280 million views on his YouTube channel alone, Josh continues to further expand his reach and deepen his connection with fans.

events.long_description:
Presented by: SBM
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.
The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.
The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins.
“But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”
Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.
New album "At Peace" out now Propagandhi.com

events.name: The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
If you‘ve ever said “I‘m a feminist but...”, The Guilty Feminist Podcast: Live is for you. Host and comedian Deborah Frances-White returns to Wellington with her new series, ‘The Road to Gilead Project‘. Settle into a seat at The Opera House to watch a podcast happen live on stage. In this series, Deborah talks with comedians, artists, authors, academics, and activists. Expect equal parts comedy and deep-dive discussion. 

The Road to Gilead Project takes its name from Gilead, the nightmare state from Margaret Atwood‘s ‘The Handmaid‘s Tale‘. Deborah thinks some of today‘s headlines are starting to read a lot like the book. Around the world, hard-won rights for women and LGBTQ+ communities are being challenged. So how do you get off the road to Gilead? Deborah‘s answer is a joyful resistance, with plenty of laughs along the way. 

Since 2015, Deborah has turned the fear of being a ‘bad feminist’ into a multi-award-winning podcast with more than 200 million downloads. Guests confess the gap between their principles and their everyday habits. Nobody is perfect, and that‘s the point. Come along to experience everything you love about The Guilty Feminist, with a new focus.

events.long_description:
KYLESA have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand. After more than a decade away, the legendary American group brings their iconic blend of stoner rock, psych, sludge, metal and punk to venues across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington.

Tickets here

Kylesa is a force of nature, a band whose sonic range and primal heaviness stunned & awed listeners for 15 years before they went dark in 2016. Formed in Savannah, Georgia in 2001, the group made their name with a series of EPs and records and relentless touring schedule. They gained a legion of fans from all over the world and dipped their toes into several different scenes as “Stoner Metal” or “Psych Metal / Indie Sludge” wasn’t necessarily on the menu. Pulling from indie rock, punk, classic heavy metal, doom, death, psychedelic and kraut rock, the band really sound like no one else.

Journalist David Peisner of Spin described them as dark psych-metal titans, practicing an aggressive, but hazy, stoner vibe...a strange amalgamation of Black Sabbath, Black Flag and early Pink Floyd.
Lead by guitar and vocal duo Laura Pleasants and Phillip Cope, Kylesa have picked up where they left off with a legendary new rhythm section in tow featuring Roy Mayorga ( Nausea, Soulfly, Stone Sour, Ministry, Jerry Cantrell ) & John John Jesse ( Nausea) rounding out the lineup.

Kylesa cemented their place as key figures in creating the Georgia metal scene by bringing forth a unique, unmatched, experimental wall of sound that is as relevant today as it was at the time.

They returned to perform at the 2025 Roadburn Festival, followed by announcements from ArcTanGent Festival, Inferno Fest and A Colossal Weekend. Since then they have made selective appearances at festivals and theatres across the globe and will finally descend on Australian and New Zealand shores in February 2027.

Created and spearheaded by French multi-instrumentalist Gautier Serre, the IGORRR name has expanded from one man's pseudonym to become a full group identity, which has brought a new level of intensity into the live representations.

Initially influenced by the likes of Meshuggah, Chopin, Cannibal Corpse, Bach, Domenico Scarlatti, Taraf De Haidouks And Aphex Twin, traces of these artists can be found littered across IGORRR's discography, but Serre has never been interested in remaining static or merely recycling ideas, and his work has dramatically evolved accordingly. With a truly unique sound blending a multitude of complex layers, Serre excudes total musical freedom by combining all of his disparate tastes into one chaotic, cohesive universe.

events.long_description:
A blend of Irish-language rap and sharp social commentary has built an international following for Kneecap . The hip-hop trio, made up of Mo Chara, Móglaí Bap, and DJ Próvaí, made a name for itself with raucous live performances. Formed in Belfast in 2017, Kneecap’s popularity skyrocketed following the release of the 2024 biographical film ‘Kneecap’ in which the group’s members each played themselves. Their previous visit to Wellington in 2025 was described by The Post as “explosive”, with the crowd eating out of the palm of their hand from the moment they took the stage. 

That tour was followed in 2026 by the release of third album ‘Fenian’ which has seen the group expand its sound to something darker and even more controversial. The trio will be joined in Wellington’s TSB Arena in February by Aotearoa’s own DJ, producer, and artist Lady Shaka. Expect a night of high-energy hip-hop, razor-sharp lyrics, and one of the most talked-about live shows on the touring circuit.

events.long_description:
Local Library reprised season
Local Library is an affectionate comedy about libraries, loneliness, local bodies, busy-bodies and the bloody city council.

Paul Homewood is a grumpy retired widower who enjoys walking dogs and reading the speeches of Winston Churchill. Uptight and separated Helen Nielsen prefers E Annie Proulx. When Helen, a senior librarian, catches Paul ripping off the system at her suburban library, she bans him. He can only return if he reads a book that she recommends. Could a friendship develop from this book war? And who are the shady figures threatening to disrupt Helen’s drag story time?

Review:
“Armstrong’s ability to write a drama that is both contemporary and universal puts him at the top of the league table of Kiwi playwrights” New Zealand Listener

Written by Dave Armstrong
Directed by Conrad Newport
Starring Peter Hambleton and Jude Gibson
Design by William Smith – Tungsten Projects
Produced by Armstrong Creative

Sat 13 Feb- Sat 14 March
CIRCA TWO
$25 -$60
Duration: 90 minutes no interval
Audience Care: Contains some swearing and serious discussion of literature 🙂

events.long_description:
It’s billed as the biggest and boldest show of his career. Paul Smith’s show Happy is set to visit Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre in February 2027. Happy takes Paul’s trademark crowd work, razor-sharp observations, and laugh-out-loud true stories to an entirely new level. This is stand-up at full throttle: fast, fearless, and relentlessly funny. 
The show is packed with outrageous audience interaction and stories pulled straight from real life. It’s about finding joy in the chaos, laughter in the everyday, and comedy in absolutely everything. 
Liverpool-born Paul Smith is known for his quick wit and unrivalled ability to roast audience members. With over 5,000 videos online, he holds the unofficial record for the most online stand-up content and has amassed a massive global following. Happy will be his sixth stand-up tour.

events.id: The Human League — Generations: The Greatest Hits Tour-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: The Human League — Generations: The Greatest Hits Tour
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
A fresh and influential sound dominated the charts in the 1980s — synth-pop. The Human League were one of the first bands to find success with this new sound. Now they are bringing decades of catchy hits to Wellington fans. Expect an unforgettable night with timeless classics like Don’t You Want Me, Human, Love Action (I Believe in Love), The Lebanon, Mirror Man, Being Boiled, and more. 
Long before electronic music became mainstream, the band was successfully using computers and sequencers to create rhythm and melody. In the process, they redefined modern pop. Their stylish, forward-thinking sound remains relevant today as ever. In 1982, The Sydney Morning Herald described them as “one of the first futurist bands.” Join founding members Philip Oakey, Joanne Catherall, and Susan Ann Sulley on an electrifying journey through four decades of stylish synth-pop brilliance.

events.name: K Motionz: Crowd Control
events.venue: TSB Arena, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
If Wellington had a theme song, it might just be a drum and bass banger. The city can’t get enough of the spine-tingling scene. Lucky for us, one of the industry’s biggest names is visiting our shores. K Motionz has established himself as a major player in modern drum and bass, known for high-energy sets and some of the scene’s most explosive shows. 

Hailing from Birmingham, UK, K Motionz has risen from breakthrough producer to global drum and bass heavyweight. He’s delivered anthems including ‘High Note,’ ‘Hack It,’ ‘Only You’ and ‘Vino Bandit,’ while collaborating with some of the biggest names across drum and bass. 

At the centre of his live shows is ‘Crowd Control’ — K Motionz’s interactive headline concept that puts the audience in control. Throughout the show, the crowd gets the chance to influence what happens next. Built around huge drops, unreleased music and the unpredictable energy of a show, ‘Crowd Control’ is a completely unique experience that has become one of the most talked-about concepts in drum and bass.

events.id: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman-Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Awakening the Subtle Body with Joan Hyman
events.venue: Level 1/175 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
About the training

This immersive training invites you to awaken the subtle body through the practice of yoga. The subtle body is the energetic field that connects body, breath and mind.

Over the course of this 3-day training, we explore how movement, breath and awareness shape the flow of prana. Through asana, pranayama and meditation, you will deepen your connection to the more subtle layers of your practice and refine how you move, breathe and sequence with intention.

What you will explore

The foundations of yoga energetics including prana, nadis, bandhas and chakras

the relationship between physical alignment and the energetic flow

Sequencing as a tool to guide prana through the body

Pranayama and meditation as gateways to the subtle body

Safe and intelligent progressions toward more advanced postures

Any questions? Head to our FAQ at the bottom of the page.

SCHEDULE

The training is 3 full days with each day designed to lead on to the next. Lunch break is from 12-1:30pm.

Friday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards arm balances

We explore sequencing as a roadmap for practice and learn how arm balances support lightness, strength and flow. Themes include prana, the five koshas, bandhas and biomechanics as a gateway to the subtle body. The day ends with pranayama practice.

Saturday 9am - 4pm - Sequencing towards inversions and inner body awareness

A deeper exploration of inversions and their effect on the inner body. We study the nadis and sushumna and how sequencing supports inward awareness. The day closes with restorative postures and meditation.

Sunday 9am - 3:30pm - Sequencing for backbends and subtle body integration

Backbends to uplift prana and access the more subtle layers of practice. We will explore the chakras as the most refined energetic layer and integrate everything through sequencing, meditation, and pranayama. A quiet inward ending to conclude the training.

THE VENUE: BHAKTI LOUNGE

The Bhakti Lounge is located in the heart of Wellington CBD, at level 1, 175 Vivian Street. It has been operating for twenty plus years and is 100% volunteer-run, community first events space.

YOUR TEACHER

Joan Hyman, Senior Yoga Teacher and founder of the School of Yoga (USA)

Joan Hyman is the director and founder of The School of Yoga, an authentic international teacher training program focused on continuing education. Her grounded teaching style seamlessly supports her students as they emerge from their practice with the rich and bright energy that yoga has to offer.

Joan’s teachings come from an organic and intuitive place, as she draws upon the combined studies of Ashtanga and Iyengar yoga as well as Ayurveda and meditation. An authentic modern-day yogi, Joan's love and devotion show up in her practice and throughout her teaching. You will leave her class feeling transformed and deeply aligned.

Joan spent fifteen years as a distinguished YogaWorks Senior Teacher before bringing her expertise to Wanderlust as the Director of Teacher Trainings in 2016. Now, with over twenty years of experience leading retreats, trainings, and international workshops, Joan travels the globe and teaches online, leading her own signature trainings. She has created The School of Yoga, which is a professional education program, helping students and inspiring teachers to work towards their five hundred hours Yoga Alliance Certification. A leader in the yoga community, Joan’s open-hearted approach to teaching yoga keeps both her inner spirit and her students continuously evolving.

YOUR HOSTS

Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett

Yoga teachers (500YTT) Sarah Marriott and Liz Birkett warmly welcome you! Having studied with Joan Hyman since 2018, they are excited to bring her to Wellington shores once again, so she can share her extensive knowledge of Yoga with Aotearoa's Yoga community. 

FAQ

How much is the 3 day training?

It is $520 (early bird) however this increases to $550 from November 1st, 2026.

Can I attend one or two days?

Sorry, no. This is a 3 day training with each day designed to lead on to the next. Please email Sarah and Liz if you have further questions about this.

Who is this training for?

This training is for dedicated practitioners and teachers who feel curious about the energetics behind the physical practice and who want to deepen their experience beyond alignment alone. This training is open to teachers and dedicated yoga practitioners. You do not need to be a teacher to join. A regular yoga practice and curiosity to dive deeper is enough!

Do I need to bring a yoga mat or any props?

We have mats, and props (blocks, straps bolsters) however you are welcome to bring your own.

Is there parking at the venue?

Street parking:
Best option is to Uber or car pool if you can as street parking is capped at 2 hours (around $5 per hour) during the week and 3 hours (around $3/4) in the weekend.

Car parks:
The Hope Gibbons Parking (68 Taranaki Street) is a 2-3 minute walk from the venue or there are other parking buildings 5 minutes away (E.g., Garrett Street Car Park)

What are the lunch options?

Of course you are welcome to bring your own lunch/snacks. However, there are plenty of cafes and restaurants available to you on nearby Cuba street. You have 1.5 hours for lunch so you may like to dine in, take a drive or head to Oriental Pde for a walk!

The Bhakti lounge also serves a delicious plant-based lunch Mon-Fri at a very affordable price.

I'm from out of town. Is there accommodation nearby?

Yes there are plenty of options just a short walk away.

https://sojournhotels.co.nz/
https://www.themarionhostel.com/

events.long_description:
The traditional sound of Appalachian music. bluegrass, country, Americana, and folk will fill the Michael Fowler Centre in February. American singer-songwriters Gillian Welch and David Rawlings blend the traditional music practices together in their first New Zealand concert in over a decade. The partners on stage and in life have 30 years of experience collaborating over haunting covers of folk greats. You might hear songs like Look at Miss Ohio, Orphan Girl, and Empty Trainload of Sky. Expect sparse magical arrangements and exquisite lyricism. 

Since their last visit to Wellington, they've been busy writing and producing music. Their recent album, ‘Woodland’, is the first attributed to both of them. Despite collaborating on most things, previous albums were billed individually. The album shares the name of their Nashville studio Woodland, lost to a tornado in 2020. 

You might recognise Gillian’s voice from the Coen brothers film ‘O Brother, Where Art Thou?’. She contributed to the soundtrack and snuck into the film itself. David is also a record producer and fronts the band Dave Rawlings Machine. Together, the pair are winners of multiple Grammy Awards and a slew of other accolades.

Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON
DRAX PROJECT TO HEADLINE GRAND REOPENING OF
TE WHARE WHAKARAUIKA WELLINGTON TOWN HALL SATURDAY 20 FEBRUARY 2027

Hometown heroes Drax Project are set to make history as the first act to perform at Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall when the doors officially reopen on Saturday 20 February 2027, marking the first event in the iconic venue since its closure for refurbishment 13 years ago.

The landmark concert will honour Wellington’s rich cultural and musical legacy, with Drax Project returning to the city where they first captivated audiences as buskers on central Wellington’s streets, before launching a career that would see them become one of New Zealand’s most successful acts.
Joining them on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved global names, Bret McKenzie, who will open the evening alongside his
eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders.

Tickets go on sale at midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

The show will also feature a host of surprise special guests throughout the night, including some of Drax Project’s favourite collaborators, inspirations and friends, creating a uniquely Wellington occasion and a celebration of the wider New Zealand
music whānau.

For Drax Project, being invited to reopen the historic 122-year-old building is a true full-circle moment as they explain
“This is going to be a very special gig for us! We all met while at uni here and Wellington is where we got our start. The Town Hall closed before Drax became a thing, but playing there is something we've always dreamt of doing as a band.”

Since emerging from Wellington’s busking scene, Drax Project have built an international career that has seen them amass nearly a billion streams resulting in 34 Platinum certifications globally. Renowned for their live show, they have toured extensively across the world including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran, Christina
Aguilera, Camilla Cabello and George Clinton. Though their music has sustained international success, Wellington remains at the heart of the band's story, making their return to reopen one of the capital’s most treasured venues a fitting homecoming.

Don’t miss your chance to be a part of this historic night. Tickets go on sale midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz
